D-HARNESS-sweep-DOES-NOT-COVER-ACCOUNT-S.status: FIXED 2026-08-27. The sweep is told what a run created instead of guessing, and a fifth leaking family — memory facts in the GRAPH — was found and closed on the way.
D-HARNESS-sweep-DOES-NOT-COVER-ACCOUNT-S.what:
provision.py --sweep removes throwaway BOOKS and WORLDS. It does not remove account-scoped rows a seed created — measured directly: after a --keep-fixtures run of scenarios-c-arcapply.json, --sweep reported 'swept 1 throwaway book(s) / swept 1 throwaway world(s)' and the seeded arc_template row was still there. Deleted by hand after a SELECT.

The normal per-run teardown DOES handle them: seven earlier runs of the same scenario left zero loop-arc-% rows. So the gap is exactly the --keep-fixtures path, which is the investigation path — the one taken when something has already gone wrong and nobody is watching the store.

This is also how a scenario note came to claim the opposite. The note asserted the rows persist because the book teardown cannot see them; that was reasoning from the schema rather than from the store, and the store said zero. Corrected in place.
D-HARNESS-sweep-DOES-NOT-COVER-ACCOUNT-S.affects: Any scenario whose seed writes to the caller's own library — arc templates, motifs, memories.
D-HARNESS-sweep-DOES-NOT-COVER-ACCOUNT-S.the_invariant:
A SWEEP THAT CANNOT NAME WHAT A RUN CREATED MUST BE TOLD, NOT LEFT TO GUESS.

`teardown()` knows its provenance — it removes worlds, models, arc templates and motifs by the ids the object watched come back. `--sweep` is a FRESH PROCESS with no `self.seeded`, so it could only reach what a NAME PREFIX finds.
D-HARNESS-sweep-DOES-NOT-COVER-ACCOUNT-S.why_not_a_prefix: This loop has paid for that lesson twice: `_purge_worlds` required a name prefix the seeds deliberately do not use and matched nothing for 35 worlds. Re-derived from the scenario files 2026-08-27 — the account-scoped seeds name themselves `emberfall-vein-b27-`, `throwaway-loop-alpha-b19-`, `emberfall-reversal-b20-`, `loop-arc-` and six more shapes with no common stem. Of the 57 arc templates on this account 51 are account-scoped and exactly ONE carries a code any prefix list would match; the other 50 belong to earlier suites and must never be touched.
D-HARNESS-sweep-DOES-NOT-COVER-ACCOUNT-S.the_fix:
PROVENANCE IS WRITTEN DOWN. Every seed step goes through one recorder, `Throwaway._record`, which appends to `self.seeded` AND flushes scripts/toolloop/.fixtures/<run_id>.json (git-ignored). `teardown()` removes the file, so a manifest left on disk MEANS a fixture that was never torn down. `sweep_manifests()` rebuilds each one with `Throwaway.from_manifest` and calls the fixture's OWN `teardown()` — the four families of DELETE each carry a hard-won guard in their docstring, and a second copy in the sweep would be a second chance to get one wrong.

Flushed PER STEP, not at the end of build(): a crash mid-build is precisely when a sweep is needed. And `--sweep` now replays manifests BEFORE the prefix sweeps — a manifest knows the fixture's book as well as its account-scoped rows, so deleting the book first pulls it out from under a purge that still needs it.
D-HARNESS-sweep-DOES-NOT-COVER-ACCOUNT-S.a_fifth_family_found_on_the_way:
`memory_remember` seeds create Fact nodes in NEO4J with `project_id` NULL — the account-scoped case store_snapshot._neo4j's own docstring already flagged — so the book teardown could never see them. Found by LEAKING TWO while proving the blind-axis fix, and deleted by hand after a SELECT, which is the third time this loop has done that. `_purge_memories()` removes them by id via Cypher: `memory_forget` INVALIDATES rather than deletes, so the node would stay and carry the run's content into every later memory_search.

🔴 ITS FIRST DRAFT ESCAPED NOTHING. `i.replace("'", "\\'")` is `"'"` in Python — a no-op that reads as escaping and never fires, because a fact id is hex. A DETACH DELETE is not the place for a quoting scheme, so a non-id-shaped id is now REFUSED. Proven by removing the guard: the un-escaped version builds Cypher the parser rejects.
D-HARNESS-sweep-DOES-NOT-COVER-ACCOUNT-S.proven_live:
The exact path the row names, end to end, K=5, real provider, zero errored runs:

    baseline                        57 templates /  0 books / 0 manifests
    fe_runner --keep-fixtures       62 templates /  5 books / 5 manifests   (5/5 called)
    provision.py --sweep            replayed 5 manifests, 5 purged, 0 errors
                                    'swept 0 throwaway book(s)' — the replay had already
                                    removed them, which is the reordering working
    after                           57 templates /  0 books / 0 manifests

Back to the baseline EXACTLY, so the 50 pre-existing account templates were untouched. The defect half is proven too, separately: the old sweeps run against the same fixture leave the row in place — asserted in the guard, because a prefix sweep that happened to match would look identical from the fixed half alone.
D-HARNESS-sweep-DOES-NOT-COVER-ACCOUNT-S.red_able:
scripts/test_the_sweep_reaches_an_account_scoped_fixture.py, 13 guards, six falsifiers proven RED and restored: a seed path appending directly, an early return in teardown, the sweep not replaying, one bad manifest aborting the sweep, dropping the memory purge, and accepting any id shape.

🔴 AND THE GUARD FOUND A HOLE IN THE FIX ITSELF. `teardown()` returned EARLY when there was no book, so a seed-only fixture never removed its manifest — and a manifest that is never removed is replayed by every later sweep forever. Caught by the test, not by reading; teardown now has a single exit and the guard pins that it does.
D-HARNESS-sweep-DOES-NOT-COVER-ACCOUNT-S.what_is_NOT_covered:
- ONLY THE FIVE FAMILIES THE PURGES KNOW: worlds, models, arc templates, motifs, memory facts. A seed that creates a sixth account-scoped thing leaks exactly as before — the manifest will RECORD it, which is new, but nothing deletes it. There is no gate that fails when a new seed tool appears without a purge.
- A MANIFEST IS PER-MACHINE. It is git-ignored on purpose: a committed one would make another machine's sweep try to delete rows it does not own. So debris left by a run on another machine is still only reachable by prefix.
- IT DOES NOT REACH EXISTING DEBRIS. The 50 account-scoped templates, and any row left by a run that predates the manifest, have no manifest and are deliberately out of scope.
- ONE FAMILY WAS EXERCISED LIVE (arc templates, through fe_runner --keep-fixtures). The memory purge was proven against the real graph but not through a batch.

D-THE-LOOPS-DOMINANT-FAILURE-IS-AN-ID-TH.the_mechanism_named:
🔴 THE GUARANTEE STOPS AT DEPTH 1. R1 answerability forces onto the wire the tool whose declared vocabulary matches the request. NOTHING forces the tools THAT tool needs. A user names a goal, not an intermediate step, so a supplier is matched only by accident - and every one of the four instances is a tool the request's words do not describe:

    glossary_create_evidence (A)      <- glossary_get_entity (R)
    composition_arc_apply (A)         <- composition_arc_template_list (R)
    plan_bootstrap_apply (A)          <- plan_bootstrap_propose (A)
    composition_arc_template_get (R)  <- composition_arc_template_list (R)

THE TIERS REFUTE THE OBVIOUS EXPLANATION, which is why they are listed. 'The budget favours writes over reads' fits the first two pairs and fails the other two: plan_bootstrap_apply and plan_bootstrap_propose are BOTH Tier A, and composition_arc_template_get and _list are BOTH Tier R. So this is not a read/write asymmetry and it is not a tier rule. It is depth: the words select one tool, and its prerequisites are on their own.

That also names the fix precisely, as an extension of a mechanism that already exists rather than a new one: when R1 forces a tool, force the suppliers of its required opaque ids too. Still the owner's call - it is candidate (c) in D-THE-ID-REPAIR-SENTENCE-NAMES-A-TOOL-THAT-IS-NOT-THERE - but it is now a one-line statement of what is wrong rather than three alternatives.
D-THE-LOOPS-DOMINANT-FAILURE-IS-AN-ID-TH.depth_two:
🔴 IT GOES DEEPER THAN ONE HOP, measured 2026-08-23 on composition_reference_update (batch c-ref3, K=5, zero errored runs, called 5/5).

  composition_reference_update  requires reference_id  <- composition_find_references  ADVERTISED
  composition_find_references   requires entity_id     <- a glossary entity lookup     NEVER

From chat-service's own per-pass wire log across all 40 passes: composition_find_references on every pass; glossary_entity_id, glossary_get_entity and glossary_search on none.

The model does the right thing at every step and it does not help - it calls the write, is refused for reference_id, reaches for the correct supplier, and that supplier is refused for its own entity_id and ends in the loop-breaker. R1 matched exactly the tools the user's WORDS name (book_read, composition_reference_update, translation_patch_block).

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX. The candidate 'when R1 forces a tool, force the suppliers of its required opaque ids too' must be TRANSITIVE, or this turn still fails one call later - level 1 was already on the wire here and the turn died at level 2. A one-hop fix would have looked correct on the other four instances and left this one exactly as broken.
D-THE-LOOPS-DOMINANT-FAILURE-IS-AN-ID-TH.why_anchor: The CLASS anchor for queue_group 1. The fix for it is a REGISTRATION-TIME LINT ('a required opaque id must have a reachable tool that returns it'), not a repair to any one of the ten rows behind it. D-THE-LOOPS-DOMINANT-FAILURE-IS-AN-ID-TH.what_actually_happens_after_a_refusal_20:
🔴 THE FIX THIS ROW NAMES ADDRESSES 4% OF THE POPULATION. Traced every DIRECT family refusal on the clean corpus through to what the model did NEXT (n=259):

    139  53.7%  the refusal named NO supplier at all
     87  33.6%  a supplier was named, the model CALLED it, and the caller still failed
     22   8.5%  a supplier was named, the model called it, and the caller then SUCCEEDED

THE LAST ROW IS THE ONE `the_mechanism_named` PROPOSES TO FIX. Its candidate - 'when R1 forces a tool, force the suppliers of its required opaque ids too' - only helps when the model would not have reached the supplier on its own. Measured, it reaches it 42% of the time it is named and fails to only 4%. The model walks the chain when it can SEE the chain; what it cannot do is invent a supplier the refusal never mentions.

THE CONTROL THAT PRODUCED THIS ALSO REFUTED MY OWN FIRST READING, twice, and both are recorded because each was nearly shipped as a finding:

The recorded RUN_ERROR payloads say otherwise: 53 are       'upstream sent "error" with no error message ... the provider reported a failure       without saying why', 27 are harness ReadTimeout, 25 are PROVISION failures, 4 are       'Failed to load model google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-qat: Engine protocol startup was       aborted'. D-THE-LOOPS-DOMINANT-FAILURE-IS-AN-ID-TH.the_candidate_lint_measured_before_writi:
CANDIDATE INVARIANT: a required argument the model cannot invent must have a description that NAMES AN EXISTING TOOL which supplies it. Three scopings measured against the 159 observed supplier-less refusal instances (31 distinct tool/arg pairs) before writing any code, per METHOD step 3:

    S1  name ends _id / _ref                    flags 114 pairs / 107 tools   recall 48%
    S2  S1 + any opaque string, no enum         flags 193 pairs / 164 tools   recall 53%
    S3  S2 + closed-set enum values             flags 243 pairs / 196 tools   recall 53%

S3 IS STRICTLY WORSE THAN S2 - fifty more flagged arguments for ZERO extra recall - so it is rejected outright. S2 buys 5 points of recall for 79 more arguments to write descriptions for. S1 is the recommendation.

IT IS A REAL TIGHTENING, NOT A DUPLICATE OF THE EXISTING GATE. scripts/test_required_args_are_declared_gate.py already freezes 99 required args that ship with NO DESCRIPTION AT ALL. S1's 114 overlap it by only 34; the other 80 have a perfectly good description that says what the id IS and not where to GET it - composition_arc_template_get.arc_id is 'The arc_template id (UUID).', which passes the old gate and is in the OBSERVED failure set.

WHAT S1 DOES NOT COVER, stated because the misses are not noise:
  * catalog_get_book.book_id (x6) and composition_list_outline.project_id (x5) are AMBIENT     ids the runtime is supposed to inject. They are excluded from the lint on purpose - when     they are missing the defect is a failed injection, not an undeclared argument. That is a     SEPARATE defect and it is not filed yet.
  * translation_patch_block.target_language / block_index and settings_model_set_active.value     are not ids at all. Only S2/S3 reach them, and S3 is rejected.
  * world_* dominates 'supplier called, caller still lost' (21+17+15+13). That is     D-SUPPLIER-CHAIN-IS-TWO-LINKS-DEEP, which S1 cannot touch.

D-THE-LOOPS-DOMINANT-FAILURE-IS-AN-ID-TH.the_invariant_and_where_it_is_enforced_2:
INVARIANT: every REQUIRED, non-ambient opaque id (*_id / *_ref) must declare WHICH TOOL emits it, in contracts/agent-runtime-tool-contracts.json's `argument_emitters` map.

ONE CHOKEPOINT, AND IT ALREADY EXISTED. The map is read in two places that both change behaviour: stream_service._missing_args_message turns the generic 'establish that context first' into 'Call X first, then call this with the id it returns', and R1 answerability is TRANSITIVE over the same map, so a declaration also puts the emitter on the wire. This is why the fix is NOT a lint over argument descriptions: prose names a supplier for a human and arms nothing. `declared_supplier`'s own docstring gives the rule - 'the prose after the dash is for a human, and behaviour must not be decided by it'.

SO THE DEFECT WAS NEVER A MISSING MECHANISM; IT WAS AN EMPTY ONE. Measured 2026-08-25: of the 285 required non-ambient opaque ids in the 315-tool catalogue, 274 (96%) declared no emitter. Built 2026-08-23, wired into R1 the same day, then left with ELEVEN entries. The row above that says the map 'holds THREE real entries' was stale in the other direction.
D-THE-LOOPS-DOMINANT-FAILURE-IS-AN-ID-TH.what_shipped_2026_08_25:
GATE: scripts/test_a_required_id_declares_its_emitter_gate.py + contracts/undeclared-emitter-baseline.json - frozen, shrink-only, in the shape the sibling gate (test_required_args_are_declared_gate.py) already uses. It fails on a NEW undeclared id AND on a baseline entry that has since been declared, so the list can neither grow nor rot upward. Both directions PROVEN RED before the fix landed.

DATA: 185 emitter declarations added across 10 argument names. Gap 274 -> 89 (96% -> 31%), baseline re-frozen at 85 tools / 89 args.

EVERY RULE VERIFIED, none inferred from a name. By CALLING the supplier: book_list -> books[].book_id and kind=chapters -> chapters[].chapter_id; settings_list_models -> models[].user_model_id; composition_arc_template_list -> arc_templates[].id; composition_motif_search -> motifs[].id; world_list -> worlds[].world_id; kg_project_list -> projects[].project_id; composition_list_derivatives -> works[].project_id; jobs_list -> items[].job_id. From the STRUCT that serialises the field, where every throwaway fixture returned an empty list: glossary_search -> entities[] of glossaryEntityForContext whose first field is EntityID `json:"entity_id"` (select_for_context_handler.go:105); world_map_list -> Maps []worldMapDetail whose MapID is `json:"map_id"` (book-service/internal/api/mcp_maps.go:77, :395).

🔴 A SHARED ARGUMENT NAME IS NOT A SHARED ID, so each rule carries a predicate over the tool name. `project_id` is a composition WORK in composition_* and a knowledge PROJECT in kg_*/memory_* - two ids behind one spelling. One owner for both would put a supplier that cannot supply on the wire for every matching turn, which is worse than the gap: a model walked to a dead supplier has been actively misled.

D-A-NEVER-APPROVE-SCENARIO-MEASURES-REAC.status: FIXED 2026-08-27. The report now names whose card stopped the turn, so `called 0/N` can no longer be read as a fact about a tool that never got its turn.
D-A-NEVER-APPROVE-SCENARIO-MEASURES-REAC.what:
A scenario with approve=None ends at the FIRST Tier-A card, whatever raised it. When that card belongs to some other tool, the tool under test never gets its turn — and the batch records 'called 0/5' as though the model declined it.

Six tools are blocked with exactly 'surfaced 5/5, called 0/5, suspended-on-card 5/5'. Read off their own raw evidence, the pending card is NEVER the tool under test:
    composition_entity_override_edit  <- kg_project_create (2), glossary_entity_set_attributes (3)
    tool_load                         <- kg_project_create, 5 of 5
    composition_generate              <- composition_arc_edit, book_chapter_save_draft,
                                         glossary_deep_research
(The other three sit in the multi-scenario `rebaseline` batch, where per-tool attribution of a pending card is not sound from the batch file alone — NOT counted as evidence here.)

This is the same shape that hid glossary_create_evidence's real cause earlier today: it was 'suspended 5/5' on a glossary_propose_entities card, and only once the harness was allowed to click did the tool get called 4/5 and fail on its actual defect — a required id with no supplier.

So 'called 0/5' under approve=None is not 'the model would not use this tool'. It is 'the model did not use this tool before something else asked permission', and those are different sentences.
D-A-NEVER-APPROVE-SCENARIO-MEASURES-REAC.what_it_does_not_mean:
It does not make approve=None wrong. A never-approve arm is the only way to see the Tier-A gate work, and it is one of the two user states this loop must run in. The error is reading a 'called 0/5' from that arm as a fact about the tool. The pair is the measurement: never-approve says whether the gate holds, approve says whether the tool is reachable.

It also does not license approving on a READ-intent scenario. tool_load keeps approve=None here, and that its read-only question raises a kg_project_create card on 5 of 5 runs is a finding about the product rather than an obstacle to clear.
D-A-NEVER-APPROVE-SCENARIO-MEASURES-REAC.the_invariant: 'CALLED 0/N' IS A FACT ABOUT THE TOOL ONLY IF THE TURN REACHED IT. When the tool under test was never called and EVERY run ended on a card belonging to a different tool, the report says which tools raised those cards and how often.

D-A-NEVER-APPROVE-SCENARIO-MEASURES-REAC.red_able:
scripts/test_called_zero_says_which_card_stopped_it.py, 10 guards, five falsifiers proven RED and restored: remove the annotation, count the tool's OWN card as a blocker, fire when only SOME runs ended on a card, name only the commonest blocker, and drop the never-called condition.

🔴 ONE OF THEM WAS GREEN AT FIRST. Dropping the `!= want` clause — so a card raised by the tool ITSELF counts as another tool blocking it — left all nine guards passing, because the case that looked like it covered that used `called=(tool,)` and was already excluded by `called 0`. The real shape is a call DEFERRED at the gate: it is recorded as an approval envelope, and `called_names` reads TOOL_CALL_START, so a tool can sit pending on its own card with no call recorded. A guard for exactly that reds the injection.
D-A-NEVER-APPROVE-SCENARIO-MEASURES-REAC.what_is_NOT_covered:
- IT DOES NOT MAKE approve=None WRONG, and nothing here approves anything. A never-approve arm is the only way to see the Tier-A gate work and is one of the two user states this loop must run in. The pair is the measurement: never-approve says whether the gate holds, approve says whether the tool is reachable.
- IT DOES NOT LICENSE APPROVING ON A READ-INTENT SCENARIO. tool_load keeps approve=None; that its read-only question raises a kg_project_create card is a finding about the product, not an obstacle to clear.
- IT IS AN ANNOTATION, NOT A RE-MEASUREMENT. The 24 recorded batches are not re-run and their `called 0/N` numbers stand as they are; what changes is that a reader is told the number is about reach, not about choice.
- MIXED RUNS ARE SILENT. If even one run ended without a card, `called 0/N` is partly informative and the annotation deliberately stays quiet — so a batch that is 4 blocked and 1 clean still reads as a weak fact about the tool.

D-TRANSLATION-SERVICE-COULD-NOT-BOOT-TWI.status: FIXED 2026-08-23 (services/translation-service/app/migrate.py). Test test_the_version_backfill_can_run_twice.py, proven RED against the original statement on real Postgres. Service and worker both back up; catalogue 300 -> 312, PARTIAL cleared.
D-TRANSLATION-SERVICE-COULD-NOT-BOOT-TWI.what:
The version_num backfill claimed in its own comment to be 'Safe to re-run (idempotent - ROW_NUMBER is deterministic by created_at)'. ROW_NUMBER is deterministic only under a TOTAL ordering, and created_at is not one here: 13 (chapter_id, target_language) groups hold rows whose created_at match TO THE MICROSECOND, because the same statement wrote them. On a tie the order is arbitrary, so a re-run hands row B the number row A still holds.

It does not fail cleanly. The DDL runs in FastAPI lifespan, so the exception is a failed startup:
    UniqueViolationError: duplicate key ... constraint "idx_ct_version"
    ERROR:    Application startup failed. Exiting.
-> infra-translation-service-1 Restarting(3) -> ai-gateway 'provider translation list-tools failed -> PARTIAL' -> 300 tools federated instead of 312, and every translation tool off the wire.
D-TRANSLATION-SERVICE-COULD-NOT-BOOT-TWI.how_it_reached_this_loop: translation_job_control was carried as a BLOCKED tool on 'called 0/5'. It was never a tool defect and never a model failure: the tool was ABSENT FROM THE CATALOGUE because the service that owns it could not boot. Found by querying the live federated catalogue for the tool and noticing it was not there, then asking why - not from the eval evidence, which records exactly what a tool that does not exist looks like.
D-TRANSLATION-SERVICE-COULD-NOT-BOOT-TWI.the_fix:
Two changes, and the first alone still crashes.
  (1) ORDER BY created_at, id - a total order, so the assignment is identical on every run.
  (2) A two-phase renumber through the negative space. A single UPDATE that PERMUTES version numbers (A:1->2, B:2->1) violates the unique index MID-STATEMENT whatever the ordering, because a plain unique index is checked per row and cannot be deferred. Phase 1 parks every row at -version_num, emptying the positive space; phase 2 cannot then collide. Both ride one conn.execute, which asyncpg runs in an implicit transaction, so a phase-2 failure rolls phase 1 back rather than stranding rows negative - asserted by its own test.

D-R1-CANNOT-RESCUE-AN-INTENT-GATED-TOOL-.what:
R1 answerability promises that a tool whose own declared vocabulary answers the request reaches the wire 'whatever the budget, the domain selection or the rail decided'. For an INTENT_GATED_SETUP_TOOL it cannot, and the reason is which CATALOG each advertise site is handed.

  line 8761, the ONE-OFF build:  _advertise_discovery_tools(_catalog_index(catalog), ...)
                                 -> the UNFILTERED catalog. R1 matches the gated tool here and
                                    adds it to tool_defs.
  line 3357, the PER-PASS build: cat_index = _catalog_index(discovery_catalog)
                                 -> the catalog AFTER filter_intent_gated_setup_tools. The tool
                                    is not in it, so answerable_tools cannot even match it, and
                                    this build REPLACES tool_defs on the first pass.

So the rescue happens exactly once, into a list that is then discarded, and every pass the model actually sees is built from a catalog the tool was removed from. Not a bug in either piece - the gate is doing its job and R1 is doing its job on the input it is given.
D-R1-CANNOT-RESCUE-AN-INTENT-GATED-TOOL-.measured:

Its declared synonyms are 'apply the standard updates' and 'take the upstream changes' - the request is two of them verbatim, and against the live 303-tool catalogue answerable_tools returns EXACTLY {glossary_book_sync_apply}, no competitor.

    agent-surface advertised ... activated=34   sync_apply absent    <- every pass

D-R1-CANNOT-RESCUE-AN-INTENT-GATED-TOOL-.the_fix:
The rescue was never R1's to make. Neither piece was buggy and neither piece was changed. What was missing was a reason for the gate to keep the tool at all.

D-A-CONTRACT-QUESTION-ANSWERED-FROM-A-NE.the_fix:
The same claim, moved from ONE line at the top of the payload to EVERY entry, beside the description it is about: each `visible_tools` entry now carries
    "arguments": "NOT SHOWN — call tool_load('<its own name>') to read them."

PER-ENTRY IS THE POINT, not verbosity. A top-level line cannot say WHICH tool to load, and that is the gap this defect fell through — the borrowed prose belonged to a different tool than the question. Each marker names its own entry, so the instruction cannot be mis-applied to the neighbour whose description sits beside it.

The top-level stamp STAYS: it carries the part an entry cannot — that a description may mention ANOTHER tool's arguments in prose — and dropping it would trade one gap for another. The description itself is untouched; the declaration belongs to the tool's author and mutilating it to stop a misread would break every other reader of the payload.

D-A-LOW-RATE-TOOL-CANNOT-BE-PROVEN-WITHO.what:
The LIVE bar asks for K>=5 with at least one call and zero errored runs. For a tool the model picks reliably that is a fair test. For a tool it picks ~15% of the time it is a lottery: translation_job_control stands at 3 calls in 20 runs across four arms, so a fresh K=5 batch has roughly even odds of containing a call - and whichever way it lands, the batch is concludable in one direction and not the other.

P11-DISTRIBUTION already names the trap ('a tool chosen 3 times in 15 is not proven by the 3'), which means the loop cannot prove such a tool without doing the thing it forbids. Re-running until a call appears is sampling for a verdict; concluding blocked on a zero sample over-reads it - I did exactly that earlier the same day and had to withdraw it.

So a low-rate tool sits outside both verdicts. The bar was written for reachability, and reachability at a RATE is a different measurement.

D-A-LOW-RATE-TOOL-CANNOT-BE-PROVEN-WITHO.the_bar_and_its_derivation:
The owner's constraint was the hard part: "N/M IS NOT CHOSEN YET AND MUST BE DERIVED, not picked round … a bar invented to fit the current results would retire exactly the rows it should catch."

DERIVED FROM THE BATCH'S OWN POWER, not from a gap eyeballed in a histogram. A LIVE batch runs K=5 and concludes on whether the tool was called at least once; for a tool picked with probability p that batch contains a call with probability 1-(1-p)^K. Solving for 95%:

    p = 1 - (1 - 0.95) ** (1/5) = 0.4507

At or above it a `called 0/5` is evidence about the TOOL. Below it the zero is mostly a lost draw — which is this row's own complaint, that at ~15% 'a fresh K=5 batch has roughly even odds of containing a call'.

🔴 AND THE DATA MAKES THE EXACT VALUE IRRELEVANT, which is what keeps it from being a number invented to fit. Across the 74 tools with >= 5 recorded runs, NO TOOL LIES IN [0.400, 0.500): the highest rate below is 0.400, the lowest at or above is 0.500. Every bar from 0.41 to 0.49 classifies the identical 22 of 74.

THE BAND SURVIVED A DATA REFRESH, and that is the part worth trusting. It was first computed over 68 tools (20 below) from the stale contract file; regenerating against every batch on disk — six more tools, today's runs folded in — moved the counts to 74 and 22 and left the empty band exactly where it was. A gap that holds while the data underneath it changes is a property of the distribution, not of the snapshot it was read from. (I asserted the 68/20 figures before regenerating and had to re-derive them; recorded because the first numbers were the stale file talking.)

IT RETIRES NOTHING. The derived 0.4507 classifies exactly as the previous hand-picked 0.5 did — same tools, same verdicts. What changed is that the number now has a reason.
D-A-LOW-RATE-TOOL-CANNOT-BE-PROVEN-WITHO.the_fix:
`selection_rate._reachable_bar()` computes the bar at import from LIVE_BATCH_K and LIVE_POWER, so a literal cannot creep back and a change to the batch size moves the bar with it (a guard asserts both). The derivation travels WITH the number: contracts/tool-selection-rates.json now carries `_bar_derivation`, because the reasoning living only in a Python docstring is half of 'written down beside it'.

gate.py's LIVE bar applies the ruling: below the bar, `called 0/N` stops being a LIVE failure and becomes a NAMED SELECTION finding — 'why is this tool not chosen?' rather than 'this tool is unproven'.

🔴 IT IS STILL A FAILURE, NOT A PASS. The owner reclassified the verdict; they did not excuse it. The SELECTION branch calls `_check(False, …)`, so a below-bar tool can never conclude `proven` — a guard pins that, because a bar that let low-rate tools through would be a way to pass exactly the tools nobody can get called.

D-A-LOW-RATE-TOOL-CANNOT-BE-PROVEN-WITHO.what_is_NOT_covered:

D-A-STORED-FACT-IS-UNFINDABLE-BY-THE-SEA.status: FIXED - proven live 2026-08-26, batch c-factsearch1, K=5, zero errored runs, and the original direct-probe reproduction now passes on the same build.
D-A-STORED-FACT-IS-UNFINDABLE-BY-THE-SEA.what:
memory_remember stores a fact and confirms it with a fact_id. memory_search for the EXACT nonce in that fact returns hits: [], count: 0, total: 0 - immediately and again three seconds later - with degraded: {'semantic': 'not_indexed'}. memory_forget handed the id directly invalidates it fine, so the store is sound and the retrieval path is not.

The consequence is not the empty list itself; it is that memory_remember's fact_id is gone by the next turn, so SEARCH is the only route a later turn has to a stored fact. A fact the platform accepted cannot be reached again by the tool built to reach it.
D-A-STORED-FACT-IS-UNFINDABLE-BY-THE-SEA.the_honest_part: The read does NOT lie. It returns a degraded marker and a note saying the semantic index is not built, so a caller reading the envelope can distinguish 'nothing matched' from 'I cannot answer'. That is strictly better than the catalogue instance of the same shape (44 public books, items: [], total: 0, no marker - DQ-T38) and it suggests the fix here may be in how an ANSWER is composed from a degraded read, rather than in the store.
D-A-STORED-FACT-IS-UNFINDABLE-BY-THE-SEA.rescoped_2026_08_26:
🔴 THE CAUSE IS NOT THE INDEX, AND THIS ROW SAID IT WAS. The read returns degraded: {'semantic': 'not_indexed'}, and I took that marker as the diagnosis. It is true and it is IRRELEVANT.

`_handle_memory_search` has exactly TWO legs:
  MANUSCRIPT leg - lexical-inclusive hybrid over the book's CHAPTERS. Needs no embeddings.
  PASSAGE leg    - semantic vector search over `:Passage` nodes (chat / glossary).
`memory_remember` writes a `:Fact` node via merge_fact. A Fact is never a Passage, so NO LEG READS IT. A perfectly built semantic index would change nothing.

THE CONTROL, on ONE throwaway project so the index state is identical for both probes:
    a nonce in a CHAPTER -> FOUND, count 1, degraded {'semantic': 'not_indexed'}
    a nonce in a FACT    -> MISSED, count 0, degraded {'semantic': 'not_indexed'}
Same project, same marker, opposite outcomes. That refutes the index explanation outright: the legs work, and Facts are simply not among them.

This is a re-scope onto a DIFFERENT cause, not a narrowing: 'the retrieval path is degraded' and 'there is no retrieval path over Facts' call for different fixes in different files.
D-A-STORED-FACT-IS-UNFINDABLE-BY-THE-SEA.the_mechanism_exists_and_is_merely_UNUSE:
app/db/neo4j_repos/facts.py has Fact readers already: list_facts_by_type (by type + source_type) and recall_facts (by date + subject name). The platform ALSO already surfaces memory_remember's facts - context/selectors/facts.py `_select_tool_facts` pulls source_type='llm_tool_call' facts into the per-turn L2 context block, capped at 20.

So the facts are reachable through CONTEXT ASSEMBLY and not through the SEARCH TOOL. What does NOT exist is a text-matching reader: neither existing reader takes a free-text query, so a third leg needs a content predicate rather than a call to what is there.

NOT YET MEASURED, and it decides the shape: whether a Cypher CONTAINS predicate (or a full-text index) is needed, or whether filtering list_facts_by_type in Python is enough. The second is cheaper but truncates before matching, so its RECALL on a project with many facts is the open question - and measuring recall before recommending is the standing rule here.
D-A-STORED-FACT-IS-UNFINDABLE-BY-THE-SEA.reproduced_2026_08_26: memory_remember -> {'remembered': true, fact_id}; memory_search for the exact nonce -> hits: [], count: 0, immediately and after 3s; memory_forget by that id -> {'invalidated': true}. The store is sound; the search cannot reach it. Unchanged from the 2026-08-23 measurement, so this is current and not a stale row.
D-A-STORED-FACT-IS-UNFINDABLE-BY-THE-SEA.the_fix:
A THIRD LEG. `_handle_memory_search` had two - a manuscript leg over the book's CHAPTERS and a passage leg over `:Passage` nodes - and `memory_remember` writes a `:Fact`. Nothing read one. The leg is lexical, like the manuscript leg and for the same reason: it must work on a project with no embedding model, which is the state every new project starts in.

  * facts.py `search_facts_by_text` - the ONLY Fact reader that takes a query. Its siblings filter by type/source (list_facts_by_type) or date/subject (recall_facts); neither matches TEXT, which is why nothing could be reused.
  * `rank_facts_by_overlap` - score = fraction of the query's content words the fact contains, keep what scores ABOVE HALF the best score for that query, best first.
  * `source_type: "fact"` added to the args model and the tool schema, and the tool's DESCRIPTION now says it searches what memory_remember saved. It listed three stores and searched three - accurate, and a fact was in neither the list nor the tool.
D-A-STORED-FACT-IS-UNFINDABLE-BY-THE-SEA.the_matcher_was_measured_not_chosen:
Five candidates, against the real fact SHAPES plus hand-built NEAR-MISSES - facts sharing one content word with the query, e.g. 'Solene Harbour was renamed after the flood' against a query for 'Mira Solene':

    whole-query substring     precision 1.00  recall 0.50   misses every question form
    ALL tokens present        precision 1.00  recall 0.80   one absent word kills it
    ANY token present         precision 0.71  recall 1.00   the near-miss collisions
    absolute floor >= 0.5     precision 0.77  recall 1.00   CANNOT separate them - both
                                                            score exactly 0.5
    RELATIVE floor > best/2   precision 1.00  recall 1.00   shipped

🔴 WITHOUT THE NEAR-MISSES EVERY CANDIDATE SCORED 1.00 PRECISION. The first study did exactly that and would have shipped ANY-token on a meaningless number. An absolute floor cannot work here by construction; a relative one can, because the question is not 'is this a good match' but 'is it good compared to the best thing this project has'.

REJECTED, and why: a Neo4j full-text index on Fact.content is the right answer at scale and the precedent exists (passage_text_cjk_ft on Passage.text). Measured on this instance the busiest project holds 209 active facts (395 total / 58 projects, mean 6.8, p90 9), so it is an index and a migration to maintain for a scan that is trivial. Named as the direction if the population grows; not built.

D-R1-STOPPED-AT-DEPTH-1.what:
R1 answerability put the tool whose declared vocabulary answers the request on the wire and carried NOTHING that tool needs. A user names a GOAL, not an intermediate step, so a supplier reached the wire only by accident.

Now, when R1 forces a tool, it also forces the tools the contract registry's `argument_emitters` map declares as emitters of that tool's REQUIRED arguments - transitively, bounded by a 4-hop cap and a seen-set against declaration cycles. DECLARED DATA ONLY: never a name, a prefix or a guess, so the surface can only widen where the platform has already written down who supplies what, and a tool with no declaration is a strict no-op.
D-R1-STOPPED-AT-DEPTH-1.measured_live:
plan_bootstrap_apply, batch c-planapply, K=5, ZERO errored runs, and the behaviour change is total and deterministic:

    BEFORE  composition_package_tree -> plan_compile -> composition_list_outline       (5/5)
    AFTER   composition_package_tree -> plan_bootstrap_propose x2 -> composition_list_outline (5/5)

chat-service logs the rescue on every pass: 'R1 answerability: also forcing declared supplier(s) [plan_bootstrap_propose (for plan_bootstrap_apply.proposal_id)]'. The model went from calling the WRONG step to calling the RIGHT one, and it called it with a real run_id.
D-R1-STOPPED-AT-DEPTH-1.what_it_does_not_cover:
🔴 ARGUMENT SUPPLIERS, NOT STATE PRECONDITIONS - and the same measurement shows the boundary. plan_bootstrap_propose now runs and REFUSES:

    {'ok': false, 'error': 'cannot preview - run has no compiled package yet - call compile() first'}

It has every argument it needs. What it lacks is a compiled package, which is a STATE the run must be in, and no `argument_emitters` entry can express that. So plan_bootstrap_apply is still called 0/5 - the chain moved one link and stopped at a different kind of gap.

Two further limits, stated rather than discovered later. (1) The registry's argument_emitters map holds THREE real entries (plan_compile.run_id, plan_bootstrap_apply.proposal_id, book_read.chapter_id), so this rescue reaches exactly the tools someone has already declared - it is a mechanism waiting on data for the other 45 id-requiring tools that name no supplier. (2) It cannot help a tool the model never CALLS, because it fires at advertise time on the answerable set; a tool that loses its request to a sibling is P5's problem, not this one.
D-R1-STOPPED-AT-DEPTH-1.the_ironic_part: Before the fix the model called plan_compile and never proposed; after it, it proposes and never compiles. The full chain is compile -> propose -> apply and the model does one of the two prerequisites either way. That is worth keeping because it argues the fix did not merely shuffle the failure: the model now reaches for the step the platform DECLARES it needs, and the step it no longer reaches for is the one nothing declares.

D-AN-ENGLISH-ERROR-CARRIED-AN-UNGLOSSED-.what:
Three refusals read 'NOT_A_DERIVATIVE — overrides exist only on a dị bản' (and the archive/spec twins). The sentence is English; 'dị bản' is the product's Vietnamese term for a what-if derivative. A model - and an English-reading author - cannot act on it: it names the precondition in a vocabulary the rest of the message does not use.

The term is KEPT, because it is the platform's own domain word and appears in eleven tool descriptions. What was added is the gloss and the way out: 'a dị bản (a DERIVATIVE Work — create one with composition_create_derivative; composition_derivative_edit only UPDATES an existing one)'.

IT WORKED, MEASURED: with the gloss deployed, all five runs read the refusal and went on to call composition_list_derivatives - a tool none of them had touched before - looking for one.
D-AN-ENGLISH-ERROR-CARRIED-AN-UNGLOSSED-.and_i_got_the_pointer_wrong_first: 🔴 MY FIRST GLOSS NAMED composition_derivative_edit AS THE CREATOR. D-AN-OVERRIDE-ACCEPTS-A-TARGET-ENTITY-TH.status: FIXED 2026-08-24 — all three cases closed and PROVEN AT THE BOUNDARY by scripts/toolloop/override_ship_probe.py against real throwaway books.
D-AN-OVERRIDE-ACCEPTS-A-TARGET-ENTITY-TH.what:
composition_entity_override_edit op=add creates an override for a target_entity_id it never checks. Three cases that should refuse all SUCCEED:

  ABSENT   target_entity_id = a fresh UUIDv4 (no such entity; the platform's own ids are UUIDv7, so it is not even shaped like one of ours) -> {'success': true, 'override': {...}}
  FOREIGN  another BOOK's entity offered to this book's derivative -> succeeds, creating an override that points at an entity from a different book
  EMPTY    overridden_fields = {} -> succeeds, creating an override that overrides nothing

What DOES hold: the canonical project is refused (NOT_A_DERIVATIVE), and a duplicate add is refused with a clear, actionable message ('OVERRIDE_EXISTS - an override for this entity already exists; update it instead').
D-AN-OVERRIDE-ACCEPTS-A-TARGET-ENTITY-TH.how_bad: Not a cross-USER leak, and that distinction matters: both books in the probe belong to the same owner, so this is referential integrity across BOOKS rather than a tenancy breach. What it produces is override rows whose target does not exist or belongs elsewhere - data that reads as a real override to anything downstream and resolves to nothing. The EMPTY case is the cheapest to argue about and the easiest to fix: an override with no fields is a row that can only confuse.
D-AN-OVERRIDE-ACCEPTS-A-TARGET-ENTITY-TH.why_it_was_invisible_until_today: The tool had never completed a single call in this loop, so its boundary had never been reached. It was blocked first as a SIBLING-WINS failure (my misdiagnosis - the prompt asked for the sibling's scope), then on an undocumented argument shape, then on a missing derivative, then on an ambient project_id that is the wrong Work. Each fix exposed the next layer, and the boundary was the fifth. A tool that cannot be called cannot be audited.
D-AN-OVERRIDE-ACCEPTS-A-TARGET-ENTITY-TH.what_was_fixed_and_why_only_that:
FIXED: overridden_fields={} is now refused with EMPTY_OVERRIDE, and the refusal shows the shape it wants (e.g. {"occupation": "cartographer"}) - which matters, because the previous version of this argument was being sent as a LIST by 4 of 5 runs. Pure local validation, no cross-service call, no failure mode to decide.

🔴 NOT FIXED, AND DELIBERATELY: the ABSENT and FOREIGN cases need an existence check against glossary-service. The only client available is documented at the top of its own module - "every method returns [] / None on any failure and never raises - a glossary outage degrades the pack, it does not 500 a generate." Turning that into a GATE means choosing what happens when glossary is down: reject every override (fail-closed, and writes stop during an unrelated outage) or accept them (fail-open, which is exactly today's bug). That is a product decision about degraded behaviour, not a lint, and this loop has a standing rule that a guard which cannot distinguish "invalid" from "unverified" must say so rather than pick silently.
D-AN-OVERRIDE-ACCEPTS-A-TARGET-ENTITY-TH.theory_2026_08_24_before_the_fix:
🔴 MY OWN DEFERRAL RESTED ON A PREMISE THAT IS FALSE, AND I CHECKED IT RATHER THAN REPEATING IT.

The entry above says the ABSENT and FOREIGN cases 'need an existence check against glossary-service' whose client is 'documented to return [] / None on any failure and never raise', so making it a gate would be a fail-open/fail-closed product decision. The first half of that is quoted from the module docstring and is true of the DEGRADE-SAFE methods. It is not true of the client.

app/clients/glossary_client.py already carries:
  * GlossaryClientError(status, code, detail) - a real exception type;
  * seed_entities_or_raise, whose docstring states the exact principle this case needs: it 'RAISES GlossaryClientError on any non-2xx instead of degrading to []' for a gate 'which must never record a mutation as applied when it actually failed.'

So the codebase has already answered this question for a mutation gate, and did so before I declared it undecidable.

THE SURFACE IS ALSO ALREADY THERE, and it answers BOTH open cases with one call. entities_by_ids(book_id, entity_ids) is a BOOK-SCOPED by-id read returning identity for a known id set. An id that does not exist and an id belonging to ANOTHER book are both simply absent from this book's items - so ABSENT and FOREIGN get the same refusal, which is what H13 wants anyway: no existence oracle for another book's entities.

And work.book_id is in hand at the call site - composition_entity_override_add already passes it to derivatives.add_override.

THE FIX: entities_by_ids_or_raise, mirroring seed_entities_or_raise exactly, then at op=add
    200 and the id is present   -> proceed
    200 and the id is absent    -> refuse (ABSENT and FOREIGN, identically worded)
    raises                      -> refuse with a DISTINCT code saying it could not VERIFY,
                                   naming the outage rather than the argument

THE ONE RESIDUAL CHOICE, stated rather than buried: what to do when glossary is unreachable. I am refusing, and here is the reasoning so it is cheap to reverse. This loop's standing rule is that a guard which cannot distinguish 'invalid' from 'unverified' must SAY SO rather than pick silently - with the raising variant it CAN distinguish, and the third branch says exactly which one it hit. Fail-open is today's bug. It is a WRITE, not a read, so an outage costing an override is recoverable while a bad override is not.

REFUTED IF: entities_by_ids returns [] for an entity that DOES exist in the book (then the check rejects valid overrides and is worse than the bug), or the endpoint is not reachable from the override path's context. Both are tested before the fix is trusted.
D-AN-OVERRIDE-ACCEPTS-A-TARGET-ENTITY-TH.fixed_2026_08_24:
THE PROBE, re-run against the deployed build on two throwaway books torn down in a finally:

    case         before      now
    absent       SUCCEEDED   refused  TARGET_NOT_IN_THIS_BOOK
    tenancy      SUCCEEDED   refused  TARGET_NOT_IN_THIS_BOOK   (identical wording)
    empty        SUCCEEDED   refused  EMPTY_OVERRIDE            (closed 2026-08-23)
    canonical    refused     refused  NOT_A_DERIVATIVE
    idem_first   -           SUCCEEDED  <- THE CONTROL: a real entity still writes
    idem_repeat  -           refused  OVERRIDE_EXISTS

ABSENT AND FOREIGN GET THE SAME WORDS ON PURPOSE. entities_by_ids is book-scoped, so an entity that does not exist and one belonging to another book are alike absent from this book's items. Telling them apart would be an existence oracle for a book the caller may not own, which is the property H13 exists to protect.

THE MECHANISM: `entities_by_ids_or_raise`, mirroring `seed_entities_or_raise` exactly, then at op=add — id present, proceed; id absent, refuse; client raises, refuse with a DISTINCT TARGET_UNVERIFIED that says nothing was written and the argument may be fine. That third branch is why the raising variant is used at all: the degrade-safe `[]` cannot tell 'not there' from 'could not ask', and would have reported an outage as a bad argument.

🔴 WHAT UNBLOCKED THIS WAS CHECKING MY OWN DEFERRAL, NOT NEW INFORMATION. The entry above says these cases were 'an owner decision' because glossary's client 'never raises'. That sentence is quoted from the module docstring and describes its DEGRADE-SAFE methods; the same file already carried GlossaryClientError and seed_entities_or_raise, whose docstring states the principle this case needed — a gate 'which must never record a mutation as applied when it actually failed'. The codebase had answered the question before I called it undecidable, and I had read the docstring instead of the module.

THE ONE CHOICE THAT REMAINS MINE, stated so it is cheap to reverse: refusing when glossary is unreachable. Reasoning — fail-open IS the bug being closed; this is a WRITE, so an outage costing an override is recoverable while a bad override is not; and the standing rule that a guard which cannot distinguish 'invalid' from 'unverified' must SAY SO is satisfied by the separate code rather than by picking silently. If the owner prefers fail-open, the change is one branch.

VERIFIED BEFORE BUILDING ON IT, which was the recorded refutation criterion: against a real throwaway entity, entities_by_ids returned it by id; a fresh UUID returned []; a mixed pair returned 1 of 2. So the check cannot reject a valid override.

D-PROPOSE-EDIT-ACTS-ON-EDITOR-STATE-THE-.what:
propose_edit declares exactly two operations - PROPOSE_EDIT_OPERATIONS = ['insert_at_cursor', 'replace_selection'] - and BOTH are defined in terms of editor state: where the caret is, and what the author has selected.

The turn's context carries neither. chat-service's EditorContext model is book_id, chapter_id and an optional chapter_title. There is no selection, no range, no cursor, and no flag saying whether anything is selected at all. So a model asked to 'make the opening line darker' cannot know whether replace_selection would replace THAT line or something else the author happens to have highlighted - or nothing.

Measured K=5, zero errored runs: the model reads the chapter, finds the real opening line, and offers three rewrites in prose. That is a defensible answer to a request whose affordance it cannot confirm is applicable, and it is the reply the author actually gets.

theory_2026_08_24_the_two_operations_are:
🔴 MY OWN DIAGNOSIS IS HALF WRONG. I wrote that 'its two operations act on editor state the turn does not carry' and treated them as one case. Read from the tool's own schema in services/ai-gateway/src/mcp/propose-edit-tool.ts — source, not catalogue, so this is unaffected by the stale-snapshot retraction:

    required: ['operation', 'text']
    insert_at_cursor  = insert `text` at the user's cursor
    replace_selection = replace the user's currently selected text with `text`

NEITHER takes a selection or a cursor as an ARGUMENT — the client resolves both at Apply time. But they differ in what they PRESUPPOSE:
  * replace_selection presupposes a selection EXISTS. With none, calling it is a guess about what would be replaced, and declining is defensible — which is what the measured runs do.
  * insert_at_cursor presupposes only a cursor, which an editor turn always has, and the model supplies nothing but prose. It is fully groundable from a turn carrying just book_id and chapter_id.

So the blocker is not the TOOL and not the CONTEXT — it is that the measured prompt asks for a REPLACEMENT ('make the opening line of this chapter darker'), which is the half that needs the state the turn lacks.

D-PROPOSE-EDIT-ACTS-ON-EDITOR-STATE-THE-.what_the_FE_actually_does_measured_not_a:
The two wrong guesses are NOT symmetric, and neither corrupts the manuscript:

  replace_selection with NOTHING selected -> handle.replaceSelection returns false on `if (empty)`, ProposeEditCard toasts 'Select the text to replace, then Apply.', RETURNS before submitToolResult - so the run stays suspended and the user can select and Apply again. The human gate catches it, and the human is exactly who can see the selection.

  insert_at_cursor with text SELECTED -> the prose is inserted at selection.from, i.e. immediately BEFORE the selected span. No error, and no damage: the selected words stay contiguous.

So the platform already degrades defensibly in both directions. What remains is a wasted round trip and a card that can read oddly - a contract question, not a data-loss bug.
D-PROPOSE-EDIT-ACTS-ON-EDITOR-STATE-THE-.a_hypothesis_of_mine_that_the_control_re:
🔴 I BUILT A FIX FOR A BUG THAT DOES NOT EXIST, AND MY OWN FALSIFIER SOLD IT TO ME. Reading `insertContentAt(selection.from, text)` I concluded the insert lands INSIDE the selected words, and a headless-Tiptap probe seemed to confirm it:
    'The old sentence.' + select 'old sentence' + insert -> 'The XXold sentence.'
I changed the helper to insert at selection.TO, wrote 5 guards that went red on the revert, and the whole frontend suite (851 files / 6386 tests) stayed green.

THE LIVE BROWSER KILLED IT. Driving the real Studio editor with a real triple-click selection, the defective build produced 'INSERTEDPROSEThe old sentence stands here.' - the text at the paragraph START, nothing split. Position 5 is the BOUNDARY before 'old', not a point inside it: from <= to always, so `from` inserts ADJACENT to the selection and never within it. My guard's `not.toContain('XXold')` was asserting ADJACENCY and I read it as SPLITTING. A green-then-red guard proved only that I had changed the behaviour, not that the old behaviour was wrong.

Reverted in full - source and both guards. `to` may well be the nicer semantics (the caret sits at the focus end after a drag), but that is a preference, and shipping a preference as a defect fix is how a ledger fills with changes nobody can justify later.

D-A-TURN-PROMISES-WORK-THAT-CONTINUES-AF.status: OPEN — the population the row asked to have countable IS counted now, and the bar ships. The defect is not fixed and this does not claim it is.
D-A-TURN-PROMISES-WORK-THAT-CONTINUES-AF.what:
A turn ends telling the author that work is still in progress. It is not: the turn is over, nothing is queued, and no later message will arrive.

    rep 1  'I am working on resolving this now ... I'll let you know as soon as the structure is live.'
    rep 2  'I'm going to attempt to re-establish the connection ... One moment while I fix this.'
    rep 3  'I am going to take a moment to pull the detailed outline ... I'll update you as soon as the chapters are ready'
    rep 4  'I'm going to attempt to re-propose the plan ... One moment.'

Each is a promise of asynchronous continuation from a synchronous turn. The author is left waiting on an update that cannot come, and the store never moved.
D-A-TURN-PROMISES-WORK-THAT-CONTINUES-AF.why_it_is_not_the_same_as_the_defect_tha:
Here it was provoked by plan_bootstrap_apply leaving the wire mid-journey - the model wanted to act, could not, and narrated an intention instead of reporting a failure. But the falsehood does not depend on that cause. ANY turn that ends mid-intention can produce it, and the platform has no guard that reads a reply for a promise it cannot keep.

It is close kin to D-NARRATED-WRITE, which catches a claim that a write HAPPENED. This is the future tense of the same error, and the existing guard does not cover it: 'I have created the chapters' and 'I am creating the chapters, one moment' are both false when the store is unmoved, and only the first is caught.
D-A-TURN-PROMISES-WORK-THAT-CONTINUES-AF.recommendation_for_owner: The detection shape is the same one D-NARRATED-WRITE already uses, extended to the future tense, and it has the same risk: a text-matching guard that fires on a legitimate reply is worse than the defect. NOT WRITTEN, because the honest remedy is probably upstream - a turn that cannot act should say so - and that is a decision about what the assistant may say, which this loop has repeatedly found is not its call. Recorded so the population is countable.
D-A-TURN-PROMISES-WORK-THAT-CONTINUES-AF.the_count_the_row_asked_for_2026_08_27:
The row closes 'Recorded so the population is countable', and nobody had counted it. Measured over 158 batches / 1,551 runs:

    20     …but the store DID move — the work happened, only the promise is unkeepable

     5   >>> NOTHING QUEUED AND NOTHING WRITTEN

The five, and they are not one scenario:
    'I will let you know as soon as the extraction and mapping are complete.'
    'I'll find the ID for you now. One moment.'            (twice, world-map-delete)
    'I'll need to list your templates first … One moment. I'm sorry, but I cannot archive
     the template because I don't have its unique ID.'     — promised, then contradicted
                                                             itself inside one reply
    'I'll let you know as soon as it's finalized.'
D-A-TURN-PROMISES-WORK-THAT-CONTINUES-AF.what_the_signal_IS_and_what_was_rejected:
NOT FUTURE TENSE. 'I'll cancel them now' is an intention inside the turn and is fine. The signal is a promise of a LATER MESSAGE or a request to WAIT — the two things a synchronous turn cannot keep.

🔴 `in a moment` WAS MEASURED AND REJECTED. It produced 4 of the first 9 hits and every one was the assistant telling the USER to retry — 'perhaps try asking again in a moment?' — the opposite of a promise it owes. The DETERMINER carries the whole discrimination.

🔴 AND TWO OF MY OWN CLAUSES WERE DEAD, both found by falsifiers that stayed GREEN:
  * a sentence-boundary anchor on 'one moment' looked free and COST A TRUE POSITIVE — the corpus's single mid-sentence occurrence follows a list item with no full stop and is a genuine promise ('…**The Last Tide** One moment while I refresh that for you').
  * a separate arm for job/queue tables could never fire, because anything asynchronous also moves the store and the store check above it already returned. The distinction is real and now lives in the COUNT, not in a clause that does nothing.

D-THE-OWED-REFUSAL-DENIES-AN-ID-THE-MODE.what:
When a required argument is declared supplier `context` or `plan`, _missing_args_message emits:

    'plan_bootstrap_apply' is missing ['proposal_id'], and this is NOT yours to invent: the
    runtime supplies it from the current context or an active plan, and has none right now.
    Call plan_bootstrap_propose first, then call this with the id it returns.

Every clause is true of the RUNTIME. None of it is true of the TURN. Measured trail from session 01a03042-07d5-7d8b-b3f9-90484821867f:

    seq 2  plan_bootstrap_propose  ok=true   -> proposal_id 01a03042-1cdc-7637-a75c-fff992d15cc6
    seq 4  plan_bootstrap_apply    ok=false  args={'book_id': ...}   proposal_id OMITTED

The id was in the transcript, returned by a successful tool call two messages earlier. The model dropped it, was told the runtime owns it, and then re-called plan_bootstrap_propose - this time without its own required run_id - and hit a second refusal: 'keeps being called with missing/blank required arguments this turn - STOP.'
D-THE-OWED-REFUSAL-DENIES-AN-ID-THE-MODE.why_the_wording_is_the_suspect_and_not_t:
🔴 n=3. That is too thin to ship a change to a message every `owed` tool shares, and I am not going to. What makes it worth recording at this size is that the sentence is WRONG IN A DIRECTION: 'NOT yours to invent' is correct and load-bearing - fabricating a UUID is the failure this text exists to prevent - but 'the runtime supplies it ... and has none right now' tells a model holding the value that the value is not its business. The two clauses give opposite instructions to a model that has just been handed the id.

THE FIX SHAPE, unwritten: when the declared emitter has already returned this argument in THIS session, the refusal should say so and quote it, rather than describing where the runtime would otherwise have looked. The tool-call history holds it; the message builder currently takes only (tool, missing, contract, tool_def_props) and cannot see it, so this is plumbing plus a branch, not a reword.

TO JUSTIFY IT: rerun with K high enough to separate 1-in-3 from noise, across more than one `owed` tool. This defect is what that measurement would be for.
D-THE-OWED-REFUSAL-DENIES-AN-ID-THE-MODE.what_was_measured_to_justify_it:
The n=3 above was too thin to ship, and the row said so. It was widened before any code was written, by sweeping loreweave_chat.chat_messages per SESSION rather than per turn:

    of 15 `owed` refusals, 4 (27%) fired while the session had ALREADY been handed that
    exact id - plan_compile.run_id twice, plan_bootstrap_apply.proposal_id twice.

PRECISION, measured before the branch existed: in all four the session held EXACTLY ONE value for the key. Where it holds more than one the branch says nothing, because 'the' id would be a guess - which is the same fabrication this text exists to prevent, pointed the other way.

🔴 A FIRST SWEEP OF THE SAME QUESTION REPORTED ZERO CASES ACROSS 1290 TURNS. It scanned each turn in isolation, and the instance spans two: turn 1 proposes and returns the id, turn 2 says yes and omits it. Per-turn, the refusal reads as correct every time.
D-THE-OWED-REFUSAL-DENIES-AN-ID-THE-MODE.the_fix:
Two parts, and the second is the one that reaches the recorded instance.

1. `_missing_args_message` gained an `owed` branch that quotes the held value and DROPS the runtime-owns-it clause, keeping 'do NOT invent one' and adding 'do not call the supplier again to re-fetch what you were already given' - the second wrong move, which the baseline runs below show the model taking.
2. `db/tool_call_history.ids_returned_under_key` - a cross-turn reader over the SERVER's own record. The call site unions it with the turn's own tool messages and applies one precision guard to the union.

The owed predicate now lives in `_owed_args`, used by both the message and the call site, so the call site can skip a per-argument query for `body` or `items` without keeping a second copy of the rule that is free to drift from the one the message branches on.
D-THE-OWED-REFUSAL-DENIES-AN-ID-THE-MODE.why_part_2_exists_and_it_is_the_whole_le:
🔴 PART 1 SHIPPED ALONE FIRST AND FIRED ZERO TIMES IN TEN LIVE RUNS. Unit tests green, deployed sha verified, in-container check green - and the branch never ran.

It scanned the turn's message list for role='tool' entries. Those exist only WITHIN a turn, appended live and not yet persisted. Across turns there is nothing to find: chat_messages holds ZERO role='tool' rows, because a tool RESULT is stored on the ASSISTANT row in a `tool_calls` JSONB column. Rehydration therefore returns user/assistant text and no results at all.

So the conversation covers THIS turn and the server's record covers the PRIOR ones, and this defect needs the prior one. `tool_call_history` already existed and its own docstring names the question - 'what have I already done?', answered from the SERVER's memory instead of the model's - which is where the reader belongs and where it went.

D-AN-OPTIONAL-ARG-SWITCHES-THE-MODE-AND-.what:
composition_motif_link_edit's `book_id` is OPTIONAL and silently selects between two incompatible endpoint rules, in MotifRepo.create_link:

    book_id OMITTED   both endpoints must be motifs the caller OWNS
    book_id SUPPLIED  both endpoints must be `book_shared AND book_id = $book`

Measured, on the 2 runs that got past the approval gate: the model resolved both motifs to their REAL seeded ids, passed the correct direction and kind, AND passed the ambient book_id. The seeded motifs are the caller's own, private, and NOT book_shared - so `_in_book()` is false for both endpoints and the repo raises LookupError('both endpoints must be shared motifs in this book').

The tool then discards that sentence: `except LookupError: raise uniform_not_accessible()`. The model is told 'not found or not accessible' about two motifs it had just successfully listed by id. There is no path from that message back to the working call, and both runs stopped.
D-AN-OPTIONAL-ARG-SWITCHES-THE-MODE-AND-.why_the_model_passed_book_id:
`book_id: str | None = None  # both (shared-tier variant)` is a BARE ANNOTATION with no Field description. The emitted schema is {anyOf: [string, null], default: null, title: 'Book Id'} - nothing about modes.

The comment immediately above it flags this exact class for the two motif ids - 'REQUIRED-IN-PRACTICE IDS WITH NO DESCRIPTION ... a bare annotation gave chat-service nothing to quote' - and those two were fixed. book_id was left bare beside them.

The tool's own description does carry it ('both endpoints must be YOUR own motifs, or pass book_id to link two SHARED motifs of that book'), one clause deep in a dense paragraph, against a standing habit that every composition tool takes the ambient book.
D-AN-OPTIONAL-ARG-SWITCHES-THE-MODE-AND-.the_fix_and_why_this_one:
TWO CANDIDATES. (a) describe book_id at the argument level. (b) make the REFUSAL actionable.

(b) is load-bearing and (a) is cheap, so both - but the reason (b) has to exist is a bound this loop already measured: a description can supply a FACT the model lacks, and cannot override a PLAN it already has. The model's plan here IS 'pass the ambient book_id', so a description may lose to it. A refusal fires exactly when the plan was wrong.

THE H13 UNIFORM MESSAGE IS NOT WRONG IN GENERAL - it exists so a refusal is not an existence oracle for objects the caller does not own. But in this branch, when the caller OWNS BOTH ENDPOINTS, saying 'these are your own motifs, omit book_id to link them' leaks nothing: they already own them and already hold their ids. So the narrow fix keeps the oracle property exactly and makes only the recoverable case recoverable.
D-AN-OPTIONAL-ARG-SWITCHES-THE-MODE-AND-.refuted_if: The model still fails after the refusal names the remedy - then the message is not what was missing and the cause is the mode-switch itself, which would want a different tool shape. Or the seeded motifs turn out NOT to be the caller's own, in which case the actionable branch never fires and the uniform message was correct all along.

D-THE-RUNTIME-INJECTS-THE-ARG-THAT-SWITC.status: FIXED 2026-08-24 (mechanism shipped + tested); the live re-run is what proves it.
D-THE-RUNTIME-INJECTS-THE-ARG-THAT-SWITC.what:
chat-service's `_inject_context_ids` fills a known session context id when the tool's schema declares it and the model omitted it. It rests on an assumption that is true of almost every tool and not of all of them: that a context id merely SCOPES a call, so supplying one the model forgot can only help.

composition_motif_link_edit breaks it. Its `book_id` selects between two incompatible endpoint rules:
    book_id OMITTED   both endpoints must be motifs the caller OWNS
    book_id SUPPLIED  both endpoints must be `book_shared AND book_id = $book`

So the loop the model was in could not be escaped:
    1  it calls with the ambient book_id     -> refused, its own motifs are not shared there
    2  the refusal says call again WITHOUT book_id   (reached the model 4 of 4 calls)
    3  it calls again WITHOUT book_id        -> THE RUNTIME PUTS IT BACK
    4  same refusal, twice more              -> the repeat-breaker ends the turn

PROVEN DIRECTLY, not inferred from the transcript: calling the deployed `_inject_context_ids` with this tool's real schema and no book_id returns the args WITH book_id filled.
D-THE-RUNTIME-INJECTS-THE-ARG-THAT-SWITC.why_it_took_three_batches_to_see:
Each layer looked like the cause and each was real but downstream. c-motiflink4 said the scenario never granted the Tier-A approval, which was true. c-motiflink5 said the refusal was H13's uniform 'not found or not accessible', which hid an actionable message the repo had already written - also true, and fixing it made the remedy VISIBLE. Only then could the last layer show itself, because until the model was told what to do, nobody could see that doing it changed nothing.

🔴 A REMEDY A REFUSAL NAMES HAS TO BE REACHABLE, OR IT IS WORSE THAN NO REMEDY: it cost the model two extra attempts and then the turn. The first fix was necessary and, alone, would have made the failure look like the model ignoring advice.
D-THE-RUNTIME-INJECTS-THE-ARG-THAT-SWITC.the_fix:
`_meta.mode_selecting_args` — a tool names the arguments whose ABSENCE IS MEANINGFUL, and any consumer that backfills context ids skips them. Added to require_meta in the shared loreweave_mcp kit (validated, additive), declared as ['book_id'] on composition_motif_link_edit, honoured in _inject_context_ids for both directions: never fill one the model omitted, and never correct one it supplied - both are the model's call.

7 tests, 4 proven RED first. Three hold the new behaviour; the rest are the control that every OTHER tool still gets its ids filled, because the measured blocker that function exists for - a mid-tier model cannot reliably transcribe a UUID - has to keep being solved. A malformed declaration falls back to the old behaviour rather than taking the turn down.

🔴 THE DECLARATION TEST PASSED VACUOUSLY AT FIRST. It resolved parents[3] instead of parents[2], looked for a path that does not exist, and returned early on `if not src.exists()` - so it went GREEN against a tree with the declaration removed. A skip-on-missing guard is how a check stops checking; it now asserts the path exists.
D-THE-RUNTIME-INJECTS-THE-ARG-THAT-SWITC.generality: One tool declares this today, and the class is wider: any optional argument whose presence selects a code path rather than a scope. The rule to apply when reading a tool is that an argument the runtime may supply must be one the caller could also have supplied and meant.

D-THE-AMBIENT-PROJECT-IS-THE-WRONG-WORK-.status: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-24 by D-A-REFUSAL-CAN-ONLY-ARM-WHAT-SURVIVED-DOMAIN-SELECTION. Its own half is fixed - the refusal names the lookup, and composition_list_derivatives accepts book_id. What remains is that the named tool is withheld from the turn by domain selection and the hot-seed budget.
D-THE-AMBIENT-PROJECT-IS-THE-WRONG-WORK-.what:
composition_entity_override_edit needs the DERIVATIVE Work's project_id. A book's AMBIENT project is its CANONICAL Work - a different Work - so the ambient value is not merely a different scope, it is the wrong object, and the tool refuses it with NOT_A_DERIVATIVE.

_inject_context_ids fills project_id when the model omits it, verified directly against the deployed function: given no project_id it returns the ambient one. So a model that omits the argument INTENDING to look the derivative up first has the canonical id put in its hand before it can.

Measured c-override7, all 5 runs: NOT_A_DERIVATIVE, and in two of them the override call is the FIRST tool call of the turn - before composition_package_tree or composition_list_derivatives - so the model had not yet read any project id from anywhere.
D-THE-AMBIENT-PROJECT-IS-THE-WRONG-WORK-.why_this_is_not_the_recorded_cause:
🔴 THE FIELD IS ALREADY DOCUMENTED, EXPLICITLY, AND IT IS NOT ENOUGH. Since 2026-08-23 project_id carries 'The DERIVATIVE Work's project_id - NOT the book's canonical/ambient project ... get it from composition_list_derivatives, whose entry has is_canonical=false. Passing the ambient project is the common mistake and is refused with NOT_A_DERIVATIVE.' The note recorded then says the tool worked 5/5 after that change; it now fails 5/5 on the same scenario.

That is consistent with the injection being the cause and the description never having been the fix: _inject_context_ids fills only a MISSING argument, so a run where the model happens to supply the derivative id succeeds and a run where it omits one fails. Stochastic, and the earlier 5/5 is then luck rather than evidence.

It is the same shape as D-THE-RUNTIME-INJECTS-THE-ARG-THAT-SWITCHES-THE-MODE, for a different reason: there, supplying the argument changed the code path; here, the value supplied is the wrong Work.
D-THE-AMBIENT-PROJECT-IS-THE-WRONG-WORK-.the_fix:
The mechanism shipped for the motif case already does this - a tool declares arguments a consumer must NOT fill. The field is being RENAMED from `mode_selecting_args` to `no_context_fill` in the same change, because 'mode selecting' names only the first reason and would misdescribe this one. One declaration, one consumer, one hour old: it will never be cheaper to rename, and a shared-kit field with a misleading name outlives the mistake.

The rule both cases share: AN ARGUMENT THE RUNTIME MAY SUPPLY MUST BE ONE THE CALLER COULD ALSO HAVE SUPPLIED AND MEANT.
D-THE-AMBIENT-PROJECT-IS-THE-WRONG-WORK-.refuted_if: With project_id declared no-fill the model still passes the canonical id. Then it is reading it from context rather than being handed it by the injection, the description is losing to that, and the remedy is elsewhere. This is a clean experiment either way, which is why it is worth running rather than reasoning about.
D-THE-AMBIENT-PROJECT-IS-THE-WRONG-WORK-.attempt_1_failed_2026_08_24:
🔴 DECLARING project_id no_context_fill DID NOT WORK, AND IT BROKE THE CHAIN. Recorded rather than quietly reverted, because the way it failed is the finding.

The experiment ran exactly as designed and its first half CONFIRMED the theory: with the declaration in place the recorded args show pid=NO, so the runtime had indeed been supplying the canonical id, and the tool now ASKS ('op=add requires project_id and target_entity_id') instead of being handed the wrong Work. c-override8, K=5: NOT_A_DERIVATIVE went from 5/5 to 1/5, and one run wrote entity_override - the first override to land in this series.

THE OTHER FOUR GOT WORSE IN A NEW WAY. Starved of any project id, the model put the ONE uuid it held into every slot:

    composition_entity_override_edit  target_entity_id = 01a03106-f55c-...
    composition_list_derivatives      project_id       = 01a03106-f55c-...   <- the entity id
    composition_package_tree          book_id          = 01a03106-f55c-...   <- the entity id
    composition_list_outline          project_id       = 01a03106-f55c-...   <- the entity id
  (the fixture's real book is 01a03106-f312-..., a different id entirely)

Every one refused 'not found or not accessible', and the turn died on the repeat-breaker. The cross-wiring guard D-FJ-20 cannot catch this: it fires only when the model puts ANOTHER OF THE TURN'S CONTEXT IDS in a slot, and an entity id is not one.

WHY THE DECLARATION WAS TOO BLUNT: composition_list_derivatives requires project_id and takes nothing else - 'Pass ANY Work's project_id from the book.' The ambient canonical id is a PERFECTLY GOOD input to it. It is wrong only in the override tool's own slot. Suppressing the fill on that tool removed the model's only exposure to the canonical id, so the very lookup the refusal wanted became impossible.

THE REAL CAUSE, which this attempt uncovered by removing the layer above it: NOT_A_DERIVATIVE names the WRONG REMEDY. It says 'create one with composition_create_derivative' - and the scenario's seed has ALREADY created one. The model is told to make a second derivative when it should be told to FIND the existing one with composition_list_derivatives, which the message never mentions.

That is precisely the second gap P3-NAME-TO-ID's cleared_note names: the arming path fires on MISSING arguments, so a well-formed-but-unusable value passes the breaker, dies at the domain layer, and the domain refusal is on its own - and this one points the wrong way.
D-THE-AMBIENT-PROJECT-IS-THE-WRONG-WORK-.where_it_stands_2026_08_24:
🔴 THREE FIXES, AND THE WRITE RATE DID NOT MOVE: 1 of 5 in c-override8, c-override9 and c-override10 alike. What changed is the FAILURE MODE, each time to a better one:

  c-override7   NOT_A_DERIVATIVE 5/5 - the model is handed the canonical project and stops.
  c-override8   project_id no longer backfilled. The model, starved of any project id, puts the
                target_entity_id into project_id AND book_id on three other tools. WORSE.
                Reverted; recorded as attempt_1_failed.
  c-override9   the refusal now names composition_list_derivatives instead of _create_. The
                model calls it immediately - the message and its arming work - and passes the
                turn's BOOK id, which the runtime recognises as cross-wired and forwards anyway.
  c-override10  that id is now DROPPED, so the tool asks for project_id instead of 404ing. The
                model has nothing to answer with and hits the blank-args breaker.

THE CAUSE THAT REMAINS, named: THE DERIVATIVE'S project_id IS UNOBTAINABLE ON THIS TURN. composition_list_derivatives requires project_id and declares NO other argument ('Pass ANY Work's project_id from the book'), the turn carries no project_id at all, and the model cannot produce one - it has tried the book id, the entity id, and the book's TITLE. Every layer above this is now correct and the chain is still unwalkable.

RECOMMENDED FIX, not shipped: populate context_ids['project_id'] with the book's CANONICAL project. It is derivable server-side from the book, it is exactly what composition_list_derivatives wants, and with it in the ledger the cross-wire correction can SUBSTITUTE rather than merely drop. The override tool would still be handed the canonical id and still refuse - correctly, and now with a refusal that points at the working lookup. NOT DONE THIS CYCLE because it changes what every turn carries, which is wider than one tool and wants its own measurement.

ALTERNATIVE worth pricing first: give composition_list_derivatives a book_id argument. It is a READ that lists a book's Works, and requiring a Work's id to find the book's Works is a chicken -and-egg the model demonstrably cannot solve.
D-THE-AMBIENT-PROJECT-IS-THE-WRONG-WORK-.fix_chosen_2026_08_24_before_the_code:
OF THE TWO REMEDIES PRICED, TAKING THE NARROWER ONE: give composition_list_derivatives a book_id.

WHY IT IS THE RIGHT ONE AND NOT MERELY THE SMALLER ONE — read the handler:
    meta = await _book_or_deny(works, tc, _uuid(project_id, 'project_id'), VIEW)
    rows = await works.resolve_by_book(meta.book_id)
It takes a project_id, uses it ONLY to find the book, and then lists BY BOOK. The book id is what the function actually wants; the project_id is a lookup key for it. So requiring a Work's id to enumerate a book's Works is a chicken-and-egg the tool imposes on itself, and the model has demonstrably failed it three ways - passing the book id, the target entity id, and the book's TITLE.

AND book_id IS THE ONE ID THE TURN ALWAYS HAS. context_ids carries it on every turn; project_id only on studio/editor turns. So _inject_context_ids fills it with no further change, and the cross-wire correction gains something to substitute rather than only something to drop.

THE OTHER REMEDY - populating context_ids['project_id'] with the book's canonical project - is left unshipped. It would work, and it changes what EVERY turn carries to fix one tool's lookup, which is a wider blast radius for a narrower gain. Recorded so the owner can still prefer it.

SHAPE: project_id and book_id both optional, EXACTLY ONE required. book_id gates on the book directly (VIEW); project_id keeps the existing resolve-then-gate path byte-for-byte, so no current caller changes behaviour. Neither supplied is a refusal that names both.

D-A-CROSSWIRED-ID-IS-DETECTED-AND-SENT-A.what:
_inject_context_ids corrects an argument when the model puts one of the turn's own ids in another id's slot. The correction sat behind `if not val or key not in props: continue` - so when the turn had NO id of that kind to substitute, the whole key was skipped, INCLUDING the detection.

Measured c-override9, K=5: the turn carries no project_id (it is populated only on studio/editor turns), the model sent composition_list_derivatives{project_id: <this turn's BOOK id>}, and `is_crosswired('project_id', book_id)` returns True - checked directly against the deployed function. The runtime KNEW the id was the wrong kind, had nothing to put in its place, and forwarded it anyway. The model got back 'not found or not accessible', retried the same call twice, and died on the repeat-breaker.

FIXED by dropping it: the runtime must not SEND an argument it knows is wrong. The tool's own missing-argument refusal then fires, which names the declared supplier and arms it. The evidence standard is unchanged and high - `is_crosswired` is true only for an id THIS TURN published under a DIFFERENT name, the same standard the existing branch already treats as sufficient to OVERWRITE a value.
