Measured in the same batch: one run sent the BOOK'S TITLE as project_id ('LOOP-THROWAWAY-composition-entity-override-edit-...') and it went out. A project_id that is not a UUID is knowably wrong without any ledger, so this is closable; it is recorded rather than fixed because it was found after the change was tested and deserves its own falsifier.

D-A-DOMAIN-REFUSAL-NAMES-A-TOOL-AND-ARMS.ANSWERED_2026_08_24_BY_READING_NOT_RUNNI:
THE MISSING LOG LINE IS EXPLAINED, and it cost nothing to find once I did what I had written down: enumerate the paths a tool result can take, instead of running the batch again.

THERE ARE FOUR mcp_execute_tool CALL SITES. Two are in the main loop (7126 and its helpers). TWO ARE IN `resume_stream_response` - 11067 and 11198 - and that second one is where an APPROVED Tier-A tool actually executes.

The resume dispatch is a far thinner path:
    _ok = bool(envelope.get('success'))
    _tool_payload = envelope.get('result') if _ok else {'error': envelope.get('error')}
    working.append({...})
    _chunk = {..., 'ok': _ok, 'error': envelope.get('error')}
    instrument.stamp_tool_call(_chunk, source=instrument.SOURCE_TOOL, ...)
No arming. No cross-wire correction. No repeat-breaker. That `_chunk` is exactly where the chat_messages.tool_calls record's `ok=false, source=tool` and the NOT_A_DERIVATIVE text come from - so the evidence I kept re-reading was written by the very path that has no arming.

AND IT EXPLAINS THE SPLIT IN THE DIAGNOSTIC PERFECTLY. Every tool that DID log is Tier R - composition_list_outline, composition_list_canon_rules - and runs in the main loop. composition_entity_override_edit is Tier A: it suspends for approval and executes on resume. I instrumented the main loop and measured a tool that never goes through it.

🔴 THIS IS THE SECOND TIME THIS SESSION THE RESUME PATH HAS BEEN THE ANSWER. Earlier: 'R1 answerability was inert on every resumed turn' because _emit_chat_turn was called without request_text. The general fact is worth more than either instance: THE RESUME PATH IS SYSTEMATICALLY MISSING THE MAIN LOOP'S GUARDS, and every guard added to the main loop should be asked of it.
D-A-DOMAIN-REFUSAL-NAMES-A-TOOL-AND-ARMS.fix_shape_not_shipped:
Arming at the resume dispatch is necessary and NOT sufficient, and the reason is in the code's own comments. After dispatching, resume re-enters _stream_with_tools and RE-DERIVES ITS SURFACE FROM SCRATCH - 'a resume re-derives its surface from scratch (WS-3)'. `susp.pinned_step_tools` exists precisely to carry an exemption across that boundary, 'because dropping the exemption here would strand a rail at its FIRST confirm gate'.

So the shape is: resolve the tools named in the resumed tool's refusal, and carry them across the re-derivation the way pinned_step_tools already carries a rail's steps.

BUT THE MEASURED WITHHOLDING IS domain_not_selected AND hot_seed, and filter_intent_gated_setup_tools - where pinned_step_tools is applied - is the INTENT GATE, a different filter. Pinning there may exempt the wrong one. Which of the three filters must honour a refusal-named tool is the question to answer BEFORE writing this, and answering it means reading the surface builder, not running another batch.

NOT SHIPPED. It is a change to how a resumed turn chooses its surface, and I have already learned this cycle what happens when I change surface selection on a hunch: c-override8, where suppressing one backfill starved the model of the only id it had.

D-A-REFUSAL-CAN-ONLY-ARM-WHAT-SURVIVED-D.what:
composition_entity_override_edit's refusal names composition_list_derivatives. That tool is WITHHELD from the turn for two independent reasons, recorded by the platform itself:

    domain_not_selected | domain not in this turn's hot set (book, glossary, knowledge, story)
    hot_seed            | did not fit the hot_seed token budget (2000 tok)

Five of five turns, both reasons. The turn's hot set does not include composition's divergence domain at all, and even if it did the tool did not fit the seed budget.

So the instruction 'Call composition_list_derivatives' is issued into a turn that selected a different set of domains entirely. Arming exists to rescue exactly this - but arming is a mid-turn correction layered on top of a selection made at turn start, and the measurement says the rescue did not happen.
D-A-REFUSAL-CAN-ONLY-ARM-WHAT-SURVIVED-D.why_it_matters_beyond_this_tool: It is P1-SURFACE's invariant reaching a case R1 cannot cover. `answerable_tools` forces a tool onto the wire when the AUTHOR'S REQUEST matches its declared synonyms. Here the tool is needed because of a REFUSAL - the platform's own words, mid-turn - and no author phrasing would ever have named it. A surface chosen from the request cannot anticipate the tools the request's failure will require.
D-A-REFUSAL-CAN-ONLY-ARM-WHAT-SURVIVED-D.recommendation_for_owner:
Two shapes, both wider than one tool. (a) Treat a tool named in a refusal as budget-exempt for the remainder of the turn, the way D-RAIL-NEXT-STEP-EXEMPT already treats a rail's next step - the precedent exists and is narrow. (b) Let a declared emitter pull its consumer's domain into the hot set: composition_entity_override_edit already declares project_id <- composition_list_derivatives, so the platform knows the pair before the turn starts.

(b) is the one I would price first: it acts at SELECTION time rather than patching the selection afterwards, and it uses a declaration that already exists and is already verified.
D-A-REFUSAL-CAN-ONLY-ARM-WHAT-SURVIVED-D.THE_TITLE_IS_REFUTED:
'A refusal can only arm what survived domain selection.' Checked against the deployed code and the live 316-tool catalogue:

    catalogue                                316 tools
    discovery_catalog (post intent-gate)     311 tools — composition_list_derivatives PRESENT
    cat_index = _catalog_index(discovery_catalog)  -> the tool IS in it
    _arm_tools' guard is `discovery and nm in cat_index and nm not in active`

DOMAIN SELECTION FILTERS THE HOT SEED, NOT THE CATALOGUE. `domain_not_selected` and `hot_seed` are SEEDING stages, so a withheld record at either does NOT mean the tool was unreachable — it means the seed did not include it, which is exactly what arming exists to correct afterwards. The row read those two records as proof the rescue could not happen. They are not that.

D-THE-ANSWERABILITY-TIE-IS-MANUFACTURED-.what:
composition_generate's blocked reason calls this a genuine tie — 'R1 is deliberately not a ranking, so when several tools declare the same words they all arrive and the choice falls back to the model.' Measured, the tie is MANUFACTURED by the matcher, twice over.

1. NORMALISATION COLLAPSES DISTINCT DECLARATIONS. `_answer_norm` strips articles, so three tools that declared DIFFERENT phrases become identical:
       composition_generate      'write chapter'      -> 'write chapter'   len 13
       book_chapter_create       'write a chapter'    -> 'write chapter'   len 13
       book_chapter_save_draft   'write the chapter'  -> 'write chapter'   len 13
   The article is load-bearing and the authors used it that way: 'write A chapter' is the CREATE tool, 'write THE chapter' is the edit-existing tool. Stripping it destroys the distinction they encoded, and manufactures an exact three-way tie at length 13.

2. THE LOOP BREAKS ON THE FIRST MATCH, SO THE DISCRIMINATING TERM IS DISCARDED. composition_generate declares NINE synonyms and the request matches TWO of them:
       index 2  'write chapter'   matched by 3 tools in the catalogue
       index 5  'cowrite'         matched by EXACTLY 1 tool in 315   <- never reaches the ranker
   `for syn in synonyms: ... break` stops at index 2. So a tool's contribution is whichever synonym happens to sit earliest in its list — declaration ORDER decides the match, which no author would expect to matter — and the one term that identifies this tool uniquely, in a prompt that says 'with the cowrite engine' outright, is thrown away before ranking begins.
D-THE-ANSWERABILITY-TIE-IS-MANUFACTURED-.recommendation_for_DQ_T41:
DQ-T41 asks what precedence should break an exact tie. On this evidence the more useful question is why the ranker is being handed a tie at all.

RANK BY SPECIFICITY, NOT LENGTH. The current key is `-len(normalised_synonym)`, and length is a poor proxy for how much a phrase identifies a tool: 'cowrite' (7 chars) is matched by 1 tool in 315; 'write chapter' (13 chars) by 3. A count of how many catalogue tools match the same normalised synonym is computable from the catalogue at the same moment, needs no new declaration, and is exactly the signal a tie-break wants.

It resolves the other recorded instances the same way and without a domain-vs-generic rule: jobs_cancel's 'stop the translation' would still tie translation_job_control on length and lose on specificity, because the domain tool's vocabulary is matched by fewer tools. A precedence rule stated as 'longer synonym wins' resolves NEITHER instance, since both are exact ties.

PREREQUISITE, and it is small: collect a tool's BEST matching synonym rather than its first. As written the ranker cannot see 'cowrite' at all, so no tie-break — length, specificity or otherwise — can use it.

NOT SHIPPED. This is a change to how EVERY request selects its surface, and it is DQ-T41's own question. The measurement is the contribution; the decision is the owner's.

What is now known is that the surface handed the model a tie it did not have to.

D-A-PIPELINE-TOOL-COMPETES-WITH-ITS-OWN-.what:
composition_build_cast_and_graph runs a whole pipeline — its first line says so: 'You do NOT pick per-entity tools: this ONE tool runs the whole pipeline — it plans WHAT to build (a worklist), builds each entity in its own focused step, files them as review drafts, then projects them into the graph and proposes their relationships.'

The model runs glossary_extract_entities_from_doc -> glossary_propose_entities instead, on 5 of 5 runs, and SUCCEEDS at the surface goal: glossary_entities moves 5/5. What the author loses is not the cast — they get that — but the worklist, the deep profiles, the review drafts and the proposed relationships.

🔴 AND THE ANSWERABILITY LAYER IS DOING EVERYTHING IT CAN. Measured against the deployed matcher and the live catalogue for this exact prompt:
       R1 forces: ['composition_build_cast_and_graph']   — EXACTLY ONE TOOL, via 'build the knowledge graph' (21 chars)
   Neither competitor declares anything that matches the request: glossary_extract_entities_from_doc's vocabulary is all 'extract entities from a document' / 'parse my notes', and glossary_propose_entities' is all 'create a new entity' / 'bulk create entities'. They are on the wire because the GLOSSARY DOMAIN is in the hot set, not because anything decided they answer this request.

So this is not a tie, not a ranking problem, and not a surfacing problem. The platform favours the right tool as strongly as its design permits — sole forced tool — and the model chooses the parts it can also see.
D-A-PIPELINE-TOOL-COMPETES-WITH-ITS-OWN-.it_corrects_the_recorded_numbers: 🔴 The blocked reason on file says 'answerable_tools ranks this tool FIRST for its own prompt (synonym length 23, against kg_build 21)'. D-A-PIPELINE-TOOL-COMPETES-WITH-ITS-OWN-.why_the_obvious_remedies_are_not_mine:
SUPPRESS THE PARTS. They arrive by domain seeding, and the glossary domain is correctly hot for a glossary request. Removing them would break every job that legitimately needs one entity created — the tools are not wrong, they are wrong FOR THIS REQUEST, and nothing on the surface knows which request it is looking at.

GIVE IT A WORKFLOW. The platform already has the mechanism and states it in the system prompt: 'If the user's request matches one of these, call workflow_load FIRST and follow its steps IN ORDER — do NOT improvise your own tool sequence for a job a workflow already covers.' That is this failure named exactly. But no workflow covers this job: `glossary-bootstrap` is ONTOLOGY setup ('Set up a book's world categories' — list standards, adopt, confirm, read back), not entity building. Checked in loreweave_agent_registry.workflows rather than assumed.

So when no workflow matches, the directive PERMITS improvising — and the model did exactly what the platform allows. Authoring a workflow changes what every user sees in workflow_list, which is a product surface, not a lint.

RECOMMENDATION, in order of what I would price first: (1) a one-step workflow whose step IS composition_build_cast_and_graph, because the rail mechanism already exists and is designed for precisely 'a job a workflow already covers'; (2) nothing else — a description warning is already there, in the tool's FIRST LINE, and did not prevent it on 5 of 5 runs, which is the bound this loop has now measured twice.

D-A-PIPELINE-TOOL-COMPETES-WITH-ITS-OWN-.THE_MEASUREMENT_THE_ROW_ASKED_FOR_2026_0:

The platform already has the mechanism and states it in the system prompt: if the user's request matches one of these, call workflow_load FIRST and follow its steps IN ORDER — do NOT improvise your own tool sequence for a job a workflow already covers' — and asserted that no workflow covers this job. 🔴 SO THE MODEL IS NOT IMPROVISING — IT IS FOLLOWING THE PLATFORM'S OWN RECIPES. extract -> propose is the sequence two authored workflows teach, in that order, as steps 5 and 6 of vision-to-book. The pipeline tool that does the same work in one call is on no rail at all. A system prompt that says 'do NOT improvise a sequence a workflow covers', beside a catalogue where the parts ARE covered and the whole is not, is instructing exactly the behaviour this row records.

AND THE NEAREST WORKFLOW DOES NOT COVER IT. `kg-build` is 'take a book that already has its cast in the glossary and build the connections' — its steps are glossary_book_ontology_read -> kg_project_create -> kg_add_nodes (repeat) -> kg_build. Here is a tool superseded IN PRACTICE that says nothing. Marking it `visibility='legacy', superseded_by='workflow_list'` is the mechanism the kit already provides, and it would remove it from discovery on both federation surfaces. NOTE THE CONSEQUENCE, which is why it is the owner's: a legacy tool is excluded from the agent's discoverable set, so it can never again be PROVEN by a live run — the honest outcome is that it leaves the denominator as deprecated rather than sitting blocked forever.

2. THE CLASS. `answerable_tools` should rank over the tools actually ADVERTISED, not only the federated catalogue, or its ranking stays blind to every consumer-local competitor. D-R1-FORCING-ADDS-THE-RIGHT-TOOL-AND-REM.what:
`answerable_tools` forces a tool onto the wire when the request matches its declared vocabulary. It is ADDITIVE by design — 'deliberately not a ranking' — so it can put the right tool in front of the model and cannot take a wrong one away. The competitors arrive by DOMAIN SEEDING, which answerability never consults.

MEASURED ON THREE TOOLS, each time with R1 forcing the correct tool as the SOLE member of the answerable set:

  composition_build_cast_and_graph   forced alone via 'build the knowledge graph' (21).
      Model ran glossary_extract_entities_from_doc -> glossary_propose_entities, 5/5.
      Neither competitor declares anything matching the request.
  registry_list_workflows      forced alone. Its twin workflow_list is CONSUMER-LOCAL and not
      in the federated catalogue at all, so R1 cannot even see it. Model used the twin 5/5.
  translation_job_control      forced alone via 'stop translation' (16) on the domain
      question. Model called jobs_cancel + jobs_summary, 5/5, and called the tool under test
      ZERO times.

So the answerability layer is doing everything its design permits in all three, and losing in all three. The failure is not that the right tool is missing — it is present, forced, and alone in the set — but that the wrong ones are equally present and more familiar.
D-R1-FORCING-ADDS-THE-RIGHT-TOOL-AND-REM.the_attempt_that_failed:
🔴 I REWORDED translation_job_control's PROMPT TO ITS OWN DOMAIN QUESTION AND IT DID NOT WORK. Recorded because the reasoning was sound and the result refutes it.

The scenario read 'Cancel job — stop translation for this book's running translation job.' Measured, that phrasing makes the tool match BOTH 'cancel job' (10) and 'stop translation' (16), and the matcher BREAKS on the first hit — so it contributed 10 and tied jobs_cancel exactly, while its longer exclusive match was discarded. The prompt front-loaded the generic tie-maker.

'Stop the translation for this book.' forces translation_job_control ALONE — jobs_cancel matches nothing. Batch c-tjc3, K=5, zero errored runs:
        surfaced 5/5, called 0/5, suspended 3/5
        every run: jobs_cancel + jobs_summary
and jobs_cancel then failed on 'missing required argument(s): [job_id]' — the model could not even complete the tool it preferred.

THE HYPOTHESIS WAS THAT AN UNAMBIGUOUS ANSWERABLE SET WOULD DECIDE THE CHOICE. It does not. The precedent I was following — settings_provider_inventory, where asking only the tool's own question moved it from 0/5 to 4/5 — does not generalise: there the sibling ANSWERED THE OTHER HALF of a two-part question, so removing that half removed the competition. Here the sibling answers the SAME question, badly, and stays on the wire regardless of what is asked.
D-R1-FORCING-ADDS-THE-RIGHT-TOOL-AND-REM.what_it_means_for_DQ_T41:
It narrows the decision. A precedence rule — by specificity, by domain, however stated — changes which tools are FORCED. On this evidence that is not the binding constraint for these three, because the right tool was already forced alone and lost anyway.

A rule that only reorders the answerable set would not have moved any of them. What would is a rule that lets a forced tool SUPPRESS a domain-seeded sibling for that turn — which is a much larger claim about the surface, and squarely the owner's.

D-THE-HARNESS-CANNOT-PIN-A-SKILL-SO-FIVE.status: FIXED in the harness 2026-08-24; the live re-measure is what proves it.
D-THE-HARNESS-CANNOT-PIN-A-SKILL-SO-FIVE.what:
INTENT_GATED_SETUP_TOOLS — glossary_adopt_standards, glossary_propose_kinds, glossary_plan, glossary_propose_batch, glossary_book_sync_apply — are filtered out of the TURN CATALOG itself unless the turn carries world-setup intent. The signal is the `glossary_shaping` skill, which skill_registry injects when `"glossary" in enabled_skills`.

The gate is deliberate and was measured: 'the co-writer proactively rebuilt a newcomer's ontology on a plain "write a chapter 1" turn: three prior fixes failed because hot-seed + find_tools exclusions don't cover tool_load, which loads ANY catalog name.' Its stated principle is that guidance and capability move as ONE signal.

🔴 THE FRONTEND SENDS enabled_skills ON EVERY MESSAGE. This harness never did — `enabled_skills` appears nowhere in scripts/toolloop — so every batch it has ever run observed only the GATED half of that signal. Those five tools could not be measured at all: not because the product cannot reach them, but because the instrument could not construct the state the product requires.
D-THE-HARNESS-CANNOT-PIN-A-SKILL-SO-FIVE.why_this_is_the_instrument_and_not_the_p:
glossary_book_sync_apply's recorded reason says 'THE INTENT GATE REMOVES IT FROM THE CATALOG, AND R1 CANNOT PUT IT BACK ... whether that is correct is DQ-T31'. Both halves stand: R1 genuinely cannot rescue an intent-gated tool, and whether a request that NAMES a tool should reach it anyway is still the owner's question.

What was missing is the OTHER half of the same design — that the tool IS reachable when the author signals world work, which is exactly what pinning the glossary skill means. A harness that can only ever send the gated case can only ever report the gate.
D-THE-HARNESS-CANNOT-PIN-A-SKILL-SO-FIVE.the_fix:
`enabled_skills` is now a scenario field, threaded through send_turn into the message body — the same field the FE sends. Additive: a scenario that omits it behaves exactly as before, so no existing batch changes meaning.

It does NOT decide DQ-T31 and does not soften the gate. It lets a scenario say which skills the author has pinned, which is a property of the AUTHOR's session that the harness was simply unable to express.

D-BOOK-SYNC-HAS-NOTHING-TO-APPLY-AND-A-D.what:
glossary_book_sync_apply applies a DIFF between a book's adopted standards and the system standards. With the gate satisfied and the tool advertised 5 of 5, the model does exactly the right thing on every run: calls glossary_book_sync_available first, finds the diff EMPTY, and tells the author so — 'there are currently no upstream changes to apply. Your story bible is up to date with the latest standards.'

called 0/5 is therefore CORRECT BEHAVIOUR, not a failure. There was nothing to apply.

The scenario's own seed_assert says as much and always did: 'Standards adopted, nothing upstream changed since.' The fixture was never built to create a divergence — which nobody could see while the gate kept the tool off the wire entirely.
D-BOOK-SYNC-HAS-NOTHING-TO-APPLY-AND-A-D.why_a_divergence_cannot_be_seeded_within:
Probed directly on a throwaway book, torn down after: adopting a NARROW slice ({genres:['universal'], kinds:['character']}) and then calling glossary_book_sync_available returns {"updates": []}. A partial adopt does not leave the rest pending, so the obvious cheap divergence does not exist.

What WOULD create one is the SYSTEM standards changing after the book adopted — and system standards are shared across every book and every user of this deployment. Writing them to make a test pass is a larger violation than the dogfood book this loop already refuses to touch: it would change what every other author's sync sees. I am not doing it.

RECOMMENDATION: a test-only way to seed a divergence scoped to ONE book — a system-standard version pinned per book, or a fixture hook that records the book as adopted at an older revision. Until then this tool cannot be exercised, and that is a property of what the fixture can safely build rather than of the tool.
retracted_2026_08_24:
🔴 THE SECOND HALF OF THIS DEFECT'S NAME IS WRONG AND I AM RETRACTING IT. I wrote that 'what WOULD create a divergence is the SYSTEM standards changing — and system standards are shared across every book and every user of this deployment... I am not doing it', and recommended a test-only per-book mechanism as an owner decision.

THE PER-BOOK MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS AS A PLAIN COLUMN. Read from the diff query (book_sync_handler.go, syncGenresAvailable):
    WHERE bg.book_id=$1 AND bg.deprecated_at IS NULL AND bg.source_ref IS NOT NULL
      AND ( (sg.genre_id IS NULL AND ug.genre_id IS NULL)
         OR COALESCE(sg.content_hash, ug.content_hash) IS DISTINCT FROM bg.source_hash )
A row is 'available' when the upstream content_hash differs from `bg.source_hash` — and source_hash is a column on book_genres (and book_kinds), keyed by book_id. It is the BOOK's record of what it adopted. Both sides of the comparison are writable; I only ever considered the shared one.

So a divergence is seedable by touching ONE ROW of the throwaway book's own book_genres — isolated by construction, torn down with the book, and invisible to every other book and user. The safety objection was real about the route I had in mind and simply did not apply to the route that exists.

THE FIRST HALF STANDS: with an empty diff the model does the right thing — it calls glossary_book_sync_available, finds nothing, and says the story bible is up to date. called 0/5 was correct behaviour against a fixture with nothing to apply.
D-BOOK-SYNC-HAS-NOTHING-TO-APPLY-AND-A-D.theory_2026_08_24:
Seed a divergence by updating source_hash on the throwaway book's OWN adopted rows, after the adopt step creates them. Then glossary_book_sync_available should report updates, and the tool under test becomes reachable for the first time.

REFUTED IF: sync_available still returns {"updates": []} after the seed (then source_hash is not the axis the diff turns on and I have misread the query), or the rows come back with a status the apply path refuses (e.g. everything reads 'retired' because the JOIN fails rather than the hash differing) — which would mean I seeded the wrong KIND of divergence and must say so rather than accept a green run.
D-BOOK-SYNC-HAS-NOTHING-TO-APPLY-AND-A-D.the_blocker_was_REFUTED_2026_08_26:
The row concluded: 'what WOULD create one is the SYSTEM standards changing - and system standards are shared across every book and every user of this deployment ... I am not doing it.' The refusal was right; the PREMISE was wrong.

book_sync_handler.go states the rule symmetrically, in its own header:
    update available  <=>  source resolves live AND its hash != book.source_hash
`source_hash` is a column on the BOOK's row - 'the standard's content_hash at copy time'. So the diff is a comparison between two sides and perturbing EITHER creates it. One of those sides is book-scoped.

TWO SAFE METHODS, both measured:
  1. Book-scoped SQL: UPDATE the throwaway book's own book_kinds.source_hash. Probed - updates went from [] to 2. Nothing shared is touched. (SELECT ran first, per the rule.)
  2. THE PRODUCT'S OWN PATH, which is what the scenario uses: create a RUN-UNIQUE user-tier kind, adopt it into the throwaway book, then glossary_user_patch it. An author editing their own standard is exactly the journey this tool exists for. Probed - updates [] -> 1, with mine={name:'Loop Kind X'} vs theirs={name:'Loop Kind X RENAMED'}.

🔴 THE SCOPING IS THE SAFETY ARGUMENT, and it is why method 2 is not the violation the row feared: patching an EXISTING user standard would diverge every other book of this account that adopted it, INCLUDING the dogfood book. A standard created for this run is adopted by exactly one throwaway book, so nothing else can see the divergence.

D-BOOK-SYNC-HAS-NOTHING-TO-APPLY-AND-A-D.🔴_AND_IT_IS_STILL_NOT_CALLED_0_of_5:
THE ROW DOES NOT CLOSE, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT OF THIS ENTRY.

    glossary_book_sync_available   called 5/5, ok 5/5, returning a REAL diff every time
    glossary_book_sync_apply       surfaced 5/5, CALLED 0/5

The divergence is genuine — `updates` carries one renamed kind per run (mine={name:'Loop Kind Zipusigi'} vs the renamed standard). So the row's ORIGINAL reading, 'called 0/5 is correct behaviour, there was nothing to apply', does not rescue this: there IS something to apply, the model FOUND it, described it accurately — and then ASKED.

    'I've checked your story bible, and there is one update available … Would you like me to apply this change?'   (5 of 5, in these words or close)

AND THE AUTHOR HAD ALREADY SAID TO APPLY IT. The prompt is 'Is my story bible out of date? Apply the standard updates if there are any.' The model was instructed, found the condition it was told to act on, and stopped to ask anyway.

Whether that is a defect is a real question and I am not deciding it here. The case FOR: the platform's answer to 'this write needs consent' is the CONFIRM CARD — call the tool, let it mint the token, let the author approve the thing with its details attached. A prose question raises no card, mints no token, and costs the author another turn. The case AGAINST: this writes to the author's story bible, and a model that pauses before a write it was told to make is erring in the safe direction.

This is NOT the surfacing defect and must not be folded into it. 'Surfacing is necessary, not sufficient' is already a row of its own, and this is a fresh instance of it with the tool demonstrably present at the moment of the choice.

D-BOOK-SYNC-HAS-NOTHING-TO-APPLY-AND-A-D.the_fix_2026_08_28:
THE INVARIANT: a confirm-minting tool must tell the model that CALLING IT IS HOW YOU ASK. Its description already said the opposite half — 'it does NOT apply; it returns a confirm_token + a preview, which a human reviews before confirming' — which is accurate about the mechanism and reads as an instruction to go and ask the human first. So the model did exactly that, in prose, on an instruction that had already said to apply.

One sentence, appended at the tool's own registration (sync_tools.go):
    CALLING THIS IS HOW YOU ASK: the card carries the question with every row attached and
    editable. If the author already asked for the updates, do not ask again in prose first —
    that raises no card, mints no token, and spends a turn on permission they gave.

The description is the ONE chokepoint that is present whenever the tool is, by construction.

D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.retracts:
🔴 THIS RETRACTS THE BLOCKED REASON I WROTE FOR composition_authoring_run_manage. It said 'CALLED 5/5 AND BLOCKED ON A run_id NOTHING CAN LOOK UP ... NO TOOL LISTS OR RETURNS AN EXISTING RUN'. That is FALSE on two counts, both checkable statically:

I reasoned from the required-args table (every plan_* tool takes run_id, only plan_propose_spec does not) and concluded no reader existed, without reading what the readers RETURN. A required-arg census answers 'what must I pass', never 'what comes back'.
D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.what_actually_happened:
The durable gate task SURVIVES teardown (mcp_gate_tasks), so the model's real arguments are still on disk. They are very nearly RIGHT:
    book_id              01a02fb6-f41c-...   the fixture book, CORRECT
    budget_usd           "5"                 the prompt said 5 dollars, CORRECT
    pause_after_each_unit true               the prompt asked to pause, CORRECT
    plan_run_id          01a02fb6-f4b2-...   a REAL UUIDv7, not a placeholder
So this is NOT the D-UNDECLARED-REF/model_ref class ('default' as an id). Every validator in _execute_authoring_run_create passes on this payload, which leaves exactly one raise: svc.create -> plan_runs.get_for_book(book_id, plan_run_id) -> None -> LookupError('plan run not found') -> HTTPException(400, {'code':'action_error'}) with NO message.

AND THE MODEL'S OWN EXPLANATION IS A CONFABULATION. Run 1 answered 'the plan_run_id I used was actually the book_id itself'. The stored payload shows it was not. A model's account of its own failure is not evidence.
D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.theory:
A CROSS-WIRE, not an invention. The same id 01a02fb6-f4b2 was also sent as `book_id` to composition_package_tree, which failed 'not found or not accessible'. One id in two different id-shaped slots is a cross-wire; and a UUIDv7 stamped ~150ms after the fixture book cannot be fabricated by a model — the timestamp is in the id. So f4b2 is a REAL id provisioning created.

  H1  f4b2 is the fixture's project_id (composition_work, minted right after the book).
      Predicts BOTH observations: not a book -> package_tree 'not accessible'; not a plan run ->       LookupError. Store.before confirms a composition_work row exists.
  H2  f4b2 is the SEEDED plan run's id. REFUTED by the 400 itself: the seed_assert proves a       compiled plan run exists ON THIS BOOK, and get_for_book filters on nothing but (id,       book_id), so if f4b2 were it the create would have SUCCEEDED.
  H3  a third provisioning artifact.
H1 is the one the evidence supports; H3 stays open until the ids are compared.
D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.refuted_if: The seeded plan run's id EQUALS what the model sent (then the fault is in book scoping, not a cross-wire), or the model's plan_run_id differs from the fixture's project_id (then it is H3 and the source must be named before anything is fixed).
D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.why_this_was_not_decidable_before: THE INSTRUMENT DISCARDED THE ONLY IDS THAT INTERPRET THE PAYLOAD. provision.py records `fx.project_id` and `fx.seeded` (every seed step's result), and fe_runner's batch writer picks fields explicitly — it keeps book_id and drops BOTH. So a batch can show a cross-wired id and contain nothing to say what that id IS. That is why this tool got a confident, wrong blocked reason. Recording them is a prerequisite for the measurement, not a convenience.
D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.measured_outcome:
BOTH OF MY HYPOTHESES WERE REFUTED BY THE MEASUREMENT, and recording that is the point of having written them down first.
  H1 the project_id — REFUTED. H2 the seeded plan run — REFUTED.
The id is the fixture's CHAPTER_ID: the editor context the turn carries. Identified on 2 of 2 runs of batch c-authrun4-diag, by an instrument built for the purpose (fe_runner.seed_ids), against the payload recovered from mcp_gate_tasks.

ONE CROSS-WIRE, TWO VICTIMS, AND THE SECOND IS WHY IT IS SELF-SEALING:
  composition_package_tree      book_id      = the chapter id -> 'not found or not accessible'
  composition_authoring_run_manage plan_run_id = the chapter id -> LookupError -> bare 400
package_tree is the tool that RETURNS the real plan run id (`runs.recent`). The cross-wire breaks the lookup that would have corrected it, so the model can never recover inside the turn.
D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.two_named_causes:
C2 — THE DROP EXISTS AND COULD NOT SEE THIS ARGUMENT. `_inject_context_ids` iterates over exactly ('book_id','chapter_id','project_id'), so a context id landing in an argument called anything else is never examined. Verified against the DEPLOYED function: given {book_id: BOOK, plan_run_id: CHAPTER} it returned plan_run_id UNTOUCHED, while the same function given package_tree's {book_id: CHAPTER} correctly SUBSTITUTED the real book. The mechanism was not weak here, it was absent — and the absence is invisible because those three names cover most tools. FIXED: _drop_crosswired_foreign_ids, same evidence standard (exact match against an id this turn published under another name), same emitter narrowing, DROP only and never substitute.

C1 — THE RESUME PATH IS BLIND TO TWO OF THE THREE IDS. resume_stream_response rebuilds context_ids as {'book_id': susp.book_id, 'studio': susp.studio} — chapter_id and project_id are absent, and chat_suspended_runs HAS NO COLUMN FOR EITHER, so they cannot be restored. Every tool call after a suspension therefore runs with a cross-wire check that has nothing to match against. This is the SAME CLASS as the bug the comment directly above that line already records (the dropped `studio` flag), with the same measured symptom on the same two tools — the fix added `studio` and stopped there. NOT fixed in this cycle: it needs a migration, and the tool under test does not depend on it (the manage call is the FIRST call of the turn, on the main loop, where all three ids are present). Filed separately so it is not lost.
D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.also_wrong_in_the_surface: plan_run_id's description named ONE supplier, plan_propose_spec, which PROPOSES A NEW PLAN. On a book that already has a compiled plan that is the wrong instruction, and the only other thing the model held was the chapter id. D-GENERATE-MINTS-A-COST-BEARING-CARD-FOR.status: FIXED and PROVEN 2026-08-24. DQ-T42 is withdrawn — it rested on a premise of mine that was wrong.
D-GENERATE-MINTS-A-COST-BEARING-CARD-FOR.what:
composition_generate validates its SCENE target at propose (the node must exist and be in the gated Work's project) and does not validate its CHAPTER target at all. Measured over MCP: a chapter_id that does not exist mints a confirm_token; so does a chapter belonging to a different book, in both directions. The author is shown a cost-bearing approval card for a generation that cannot succeed.

It is APPROVE-THEN-FAIL, not a cross-book write: the payload carries the GATED project's book_id, the chapter path resolves scenes by scenes_for_chapter(project_id, chapter_id), and the persist targets that same book_id — so a foreign chapter fails at confirm. Read from the code rather than confirmed, because confirming spends.

The behaviour is DELIBERATE and documented in the source: 'The CHAPTER target is validated at confirm by the engine (it needs book-service to resolve the chapter sort/plan).'
D-GENERATE-MINTS-A-COST-BEARING-CARD-FOR.why_i_did_not_just_fix_it:
Because the fix cannot be made without choosing a failure mode, and the choice is not mine.

composition-service holds no authoritative chapter table: outline_node.chapter_id covers only OUTLINED chapters, and a chapter with no scenes is normal and legitimate, so a local check would refuse valid work. Existence therefore requires book-service. The obvious helper, get_chapter_sort_orders, is explicitly NOT book-scoped ('the caller MUST have verified book ownership first') and returns {} on ANY failure — so a guard built on it would fail OPEN, which is the shape this loop has already filed as a defect twice.

So the real question is what the most expensive tool on the platform does while book-service is unreachable, and both answers cost something.
D-GENERATE-MINTS-A-COST-BEARING-CARD-FOR.dq_t42_recommendation:
DQ-T42 — should composition_generate verify the CHAPTER target at propose, and what happens when book-service cannot answer?

MY RECOMMENDATION, and it is a recommendation: verify at propose against a BOOK-SCOPED book-service route (get_draft is scoped by URL: /v1/books/{book_id}/chapters/{chapter_id}), and FAIL CLOSED with a refusal that says the target could not be VERIFIED rather than that it does not exist. Reasons: an unverifiable target during an outage is exactly when a bogus spend is hardest for an author to understand; the refusal costs nothing while the alternative costs money; and 'degrade must surface unverified' is already this platform's rule elsewhere. The cost is real and should be stated plainly: during a book-service outage no chapter generation could be proposed at all.

THE OWNER DECIDES. I am not making this change to unblock a tool.
dq_t42_dissolved_2026_08_24:
🔴 DQ-T42 DISSOLVES AND I RETRACT IT. I filed it because 'existence therefore requires book-service', which made the fix a choice about what the platform's most expensive tool does during an outage of another service — fail-open or fail-closed — and I said that was the owner's. The premise was wrong.

I had reasoned: composition-service holds no authoritative chapter table; outline_node.chapter_id covers only OUTLINED chapters; a chapter with no scenes is normal and legitimate; so a local check would refuse valid work. The last step is false, and the engine says so itself:

    engine.generate_chapter:
        scenes = await outline.scenes_for_chapter(project_id, chapter_id)
        if not scenes:
            raise HTTPException(400, {'code': 'NO_CHAPTER_PLAN',
                                      'detail': 'chapter has no scene plan; decompose it first'})

A chapter with no scene plan CANNOT BE GENERATED AT ALL. Non-empty scenes_for_chapter is a necessary precondition of the whole operation, it is a LOCAL query against this service's own outline_node, and it is scoped by project_id. So the propose-time check refuses exactly what the confirm would refuse, with no cross-service call and therefore no degrade to decide.

And it covers both failing bars by construction: a chapter that does not exist has no scenes in this project, and another book's chapter has no scenes in THIS project either. The same single predicate the engine already trusts.
D-GENERATE-MINTS-A-COST-BEARING-CARD-FOR.theory_2026_08_24_second:
Add the chapter-target branch beside the scene-target branch that already validates, using scenes_for_chapter(pid, chapter_id). Predicts: absent chapter -> refused, foreign chapter -> refused, a real chapter WITH a scene plan -> still mints.

REFUTED IF a chapter that genuinely has a scene plan stops minting — that would mean the predicate is not the one the engine uses and I have broken the tool to satisfy a bar. The control is therefore not optional: it must be asserted in the same test.
D-GENERATE-MINTS-A-COST-BEARING-CARD-FOR.proof:
Falsifier proven RED on the original defect (DID NOT RAISE) and green with the check active, with the CONTROL asserted in the same file: a chapter that HAS a scene plan must still mint, or the predicate is the wrong one and the tool is broken for every real caller.

Verified against the DEPLOYED image, before and after:
    absent chapter                   card minted -> REFUSED
    book B's chapter vs project A    card minted -> REFUSED
    book A's chapter vs project B    card minted -> REFUSED
    a chapter WITH a scene plan      -> STILL MINTS (control)
    a plan-less chapter on book B    -> still refused (the seed did not disable the check)

Live K=5 on an arm that seeds a scene plan: called 5/5, suspended 4/5, store unchanged, zero errored runs.

With a real divergence seeded, glossary_book_sync_apply is reachable — and three SHIP bars fail. Driven over MCP, every one of these MINTED A CARD:

The file also already states the principle — 'Mint-time validation (§11 #8): reject a malformed proposal up front so the agent never shows a card destined to 4xx' — and already validates entity, choice and UUID SHAPE. D-REGISTRY-LIST-WORKFLOWS-IS-NOT-A-DUPLI.status: CONFIRMED 2026-08-24, and the arm is REFUTED by its own falsifier. The tool stays blocked; my recommendation is REVERSED.
D-REGISTRY-LIST-WORKFLOWS-IS-NOT-A-DUPLI.retracts:
🔴 THIS RETRACTS THE BLOCKED REASON I WROTE FOR registry_list_workflows. It says 'THE TWO TOOLS ARE THE SAME CAPABILITY, checked rather than assumed' and recommends marking it visibility=legacy, superseded_by=workflow_list — which would have DELETED a capability from the catalogue on the strength of a comparison that missed the arguments.

What I compared was the two DESCRIPTIONS and the UNFILTERED return (12 rows each). What I did not read was what each tool ACCEPTS:
    registry_list_workflows  properties: {surface: book|editor|studio}
    workflow_list            properties: {}            <- no arguments at all
MEASURED by calling the federated tool, and the filter is not cosmetic:
    (no filter) 12    book 12    editor 11    studio 6
The studio sees HALF the workflows. So there is a question only this tool can answer — 'what workflows are available in the studio?' — and its always-on twin cannot answer it at all.

Same error class as two other reasons I retracted this week: for composition_authoring_run_manage I censused required ARGUMENTS and never read what the readers RETURN; here I read the returns and never read the arguments. Both times the conclusion was 'nothing else can do this' / 'something else already does this', and both times one unread half of the schema decided it.
D-REGISTRY-LIST-WORKFLOWS-IS-NOT-A-DUPLI.theory:
The tool is unreachable for 'What workflows are available to me?' because the always-on twin answers that question completely and first. It should be REACHABLE for a request that names a SURFACE, because the twin structurally cannot narrow and returning all 12 would be wrong.

Verified against the deployed matcher: 'What workflows are available on the studio surface?' makes registry_list_workflows answerable — and it is the ONLY tool in that set, because workflow_list is consumer-local and invisible to R1 (though still advertised).
D-REGISTRY-LIST-WORKFLOWS-IS-NOT-A-DUPLI.refuted_if:
The model answers a surface-scoped question with workflow_list anyway — returning all 12 where 6 are correct — or asks rather than calling. Then the twin wins even where it is WRONG, which is a stronger version of the duplicate finding and I say so rather than reaching for another prompt.

🔴 AND THE ORIGINAL ARM KEEPS ITS RESULT EITHER WAY. 'What workflows are available to me?' answered by workflow_list on 5 of 5 is CORRECT behaviour — the answer was true and complete — and a surface-scoped arm does not retire that finding.
D-REGISTRY-LIST-WORKFLOWS-IS-NOT-A-DUPLI.outcome:
The theory held on the schemas and the refutation clause fired on the model. Measured, K=5:
    4 of 5 runs answered from workflow_list and reported NINE workflows as 'available on the studio surface' — five of them are not (draw-a-map, kg-build, lore-so-far, populate-from-notes, translation-pass). The studio has six.
    1 of 5 called registry_list_workflows and named studio workflows only.

So the always-on twin does not merely win a duplicate race; it makes the model WRONG on a question it structurally cannot answer, and confidently. The arm is refuted and is recorded as such rather than concluded.
D-REGISTRY-LIST-WORKFLOWS-IS-NOT-A-DUPLI.recommendation_reversed:
🔴 DO NOT MARK registry_list_workflows visibility=legacy / superseded_by=workflow_list. That was my recommendation on file and it is WRONG: it would delete the only tool that can answer a surface-scoped workflow question, and the measured consequence of answering such a question without it is a wrong list presented as fact.

THE QUESTION I NOW RECOMMEND PUTTING instead — still the owner's — is how an always-on consumer-local tool should coexist with a federated tool that is strictly more capable. Two shapes worth weighing, neither of which I am choosing:
  * give workflow_list the same `surface` argument, so the always-on answer can be correct; or
  * have workflow_list's description say what it CANNOT do (it cannot narrow by surface) and name registry_list_workflows for that case, which is the cheaper change and leaves the capability where it is.
The first makes the twin sufficient; the second makes the twin honest. The measurement does not decide between them.

THE INVARIANT: a turn that produced nothing of its own says why, in the tool's words — never in invented ones.

D-THE-OUT2-LINT-ONLY-INSPECTS-TOOLS-THAT.what:
scripts/context-budget-defaults-lint.py is the cross-service enforcement for OUT-2, and docs/standards/mcp-tool-io.md cites it as the partial coverage that 'blocks NEW violations'. Its trigger is the presence of the compliance machinery:

    line 222   if "detail" not in params or "limit" not in params: continue
    line 238   if "detail" in fields and "limit" in fields:

So it checks that a tool which ALREADY has `detail` and `limit` defaults them well. A list tool that never implemented either falls through the `continue` and is never looked at. 🔴 A tool is exempted from the check by being MORE non-compliant, not less. Line 18's stated exemption ('a single-item tool — has `detail`, no `limit` — is EXEMPT') is deliberate and correct; the NEITHER case is not an exemption anyone wrote, it is a fall-through.

D-THE-OUT2-LINT-ONLY-INSPECTS-TOOLS-THAT.the_fix:
1. TRIGGER ON LIST SHAPE. The old trigger fired only when a tool ALREADY had both `detail` and `limit`, so a list tool that never implemented either fell through a `continue` — exempted for being MORE non-compliant, not less. A list-shaped tool missing either field is now FLAGGED.

2. THE GO HALF, which the owner called the point: 'a lint that only reads Python misses most of this catalogue … a Python-only version would report a clean bill of health over a minority of the population.' Go registration files are found BY CONTENT (a `Name: "…"` literal beside an mcp registration) rather than by directory, because the Go services do not share the Python `/mcp/` convention — glossary keeps them in `internal/api/`.

3. SEEDED AS FLIP-PENDING DEBT, K37-style: 21 offenders, 10 Python and 11 Go, each row saying it is debt to drain rather than an exemption.

🔴 WHY A NAME PATTERN IS ACCEPTABLE HERE AND NOWHERE NEAR THE RUNTIME. This repo deleted a name classifier (CP-4.d) for inferring a tool's read/write LANE from fragments of its identifier — that gated real actions and got them wrong. This is a LINT: its output is a flag a human reads, its false positives get an ALLOW row with a reason, and nothing it decides reaches a user. The cost of a wrong guess is a review, not a wrong write. Guards pin that it does not fire on single-item tools (the standard's own stated exemption) and that a substring is not a shape (`book_blocklist_read` is not a list tool).
D-THE-OUT2-LINT-ONLY-INSPECTS-TOOLS-THAT.the_ratchet:
The owner's build note: 'the allow-list may only SHRINK … it is what stops a seeded baseline from becoming a place to hide new violations.'

The seed is recorded in contracts/out2-allow-baseline.json and scripts/test_the_out2_allow_list_only_shrinks.py fails on any key not in it. Removing a key — draining the debt — stays legal, which is the only direction the list should move. The guard also asserts the baseline is NON-EMPTY, because a ratchet over an empty set passes forever and this loop has shipped one of those before.
D-THE-OUT2-LINT-ONLY-INSPECTS-TOOLS-THAT.proven:
COVERAGE, before and after, over the same tree:
    before   inspected 8 of 41 list-shaped tools (recall 20%); 32 Go files outside it entirely
    after    21 offenders found — 10 Python, 11 Go — where the old trigger found ZERO of them

THE CLAIM IN THE STANDARD NOW HOLDS. docs/standards/mcp-tool-io.md cites this lint as the coverage that 'blocks NEW violations'. Tested directly: a temporary list-shaped tool with no detail and no limit was added to composition-service, the lint FAILED naming it, and removing it returned the lint to green.

Inverse edits proven RED: adding a key to ALLOW fails the ratchet; reverting the trigger to the old condition drops the Python findings from 10 to 0 — which is the measurement that shows the widened trigger is what finds them.
D-THE-OUT2-LINT-ONLY-INSPECTS-TOOLS-THAT.what_is_NOT_covered:
- 21 TOOLS ARE SEEDED, NOT FIXED. Every one is a list-shaped tool with no small-shape selector, and each stays that way until someone drains it. The lint now blocks the NEXT one; it does not repair these.
- SKIPPED IS STILL NOT OVER BUDGET. The row's own caution stands: only one of these (settings_list_models, 10,380 bytes) was ever measured. The other 20 are UNMEASURED and some are certainly fine — a short template list costs nothing. This is a static recall gap closed, not a payload census.
- THE GO SCAN IS REGEX AND PER-FILE, deliberately, and says so in its own docstring: it asks whether a list-shaped registration's FILE declares detail/limit, so it cannot tell which struct a tag belongs to. That coarseness is why every Go finding is seeded as reviewable debt rather than asserted as a violation.

D-THE-JARGON-SCRUBBER-REWRITES-IDENTIFIE.status: NAMED and MEASURED 2026-08-25 at 5/5. Found by reading a reply in full instead of trusting my own counter. RECOMMENDED, not shipped — see why.
D-THE-JARGON-SCRUBBER-REWRITES-IDENTIFIE.what:
services/chat-service/app/services/stream_events.py::scrub_jargon is the Track C §4 'speak plainly' guard: a deterministic table of regex rewrites applied to the assistant's user-facing text at the wire chokepoint, because a mid-tier model does not reliably comply with being asked. The intent is sound and the table is thoughtfully scoped — its own comment excludes kind/tool/spec/job/token precisely because rewriting them 'would mangle normal prose'.

But the rules are word-boundary regexes, and `-` is a word boundary. So they fire INSIDE identifiers, which the guard has no concept of:
    glossary-bootstrap   -> 'story bible-bootstrap'
    entity-triage        -> 'element-triage'
    vision-to-book       -> 'book-building'
None of those three names exists. The guard was designed not to mangle PROSE and was never asked about NAMES.
D-THE-JARGON-SCRUBBER-REWRITES-IDENTIFIE.measured:
c-regwf4, 5 of 5 runs. Every reply answers the studio-surface question correctly — the right six workflows, no non-studio ones — and then hands the user two identifiers that do not exist. Verbatim from run 2:
    * **Clean up a book's suggested items** (`element-triage`): …
    * **Set up a book's world categories** (`story bible-bootstrap`): …
This is 5/5, not the 1-in-5 effects this loop usually argues about, and it needs no live run to reproduce — scrub_jargon('glossary-bootstrap') shows it in one line.

AND IT SILENTLY CORRUPTED MY OWN MEASUREMENTS. Cycle 36 recorded that a reply 'names workflows by TITLE — Book-building'. That was never the model paraphrasing: it is vision-to-book with this table applied. Any counter of mine that matches raw slugs under-counts by exactly these three names, so the c-regwf4 numbers above were re-taken with a scrub-aware matcher (importing the real _JARGON_SUBS, not a copy of it) before being believed. They were unchanged.
D-THE-JARGON-SCRUBBER-REWRITES-IDENTIFIE.why_it_blocks_the_tool: registry_list_workflows' DATA bar is answer-is-true. The answer that reaches the user misnames two of the six things it is listing, in a form the user cannot use and a subsequent workflow_load(slug) cannot resolve. Calling that a true answer to get a green would be exactly the gaming the standing rule forbids, so the tool stays blocked — but on this cause rather than the one it was blocked on, which is a different problem and is recorded as such.
D-THE-JARGON-SCRUBBER-REWRITES-IDENTIFIE.the_fix_and_why_not_here:
The narrow fix is to leave inline code spans alone: the slugs arrive wrapped in backticks, and a code span is by definition a NAME rather than prose, which is the distinction the guard's own comment is reaching for. Doing it inside scrub_jargon alone is a trap, though — it is also called per-DELTA on a hold-back buffer, so a span split across two deltas would still be rewritten. A correct fix has to teach _is_risky_tail to hold an unterminated span the same way it already holds an unfinished multi-word phrase.

That is a change to a flagship streaming guarantee, and the half of it that fits in the end of a cycle is precisely the half that leaves a silent seam. Filed with a 5/5 measurement and a one-line reproduction so it can be done properly.

D-THE-DEFECT-COUNTER-PARSED-ENGLISH-AND-.found_by: being asked what remains in runstate, and counting the rows instead of reading the headline
D-THE-DEFECT-COUNTER-PARSED-ENGLISH-AND-.invariant: A counter reads a CLOSED machine field. A row it cannot classify STOPS the count; it is never absorbed into a remainder. Prose may sit beside the field and must never be parsed for meaning.
D-THE-DEFECT-COUNTER-PARSED-ENGLISH-AND-.what:
`recompute_progress` classified defects with `defect_state(d).startswith('open')` over `state or status`. `status` is free prose - 104 of 156 rows carried ONLY that field, median 89 chars, max 311 - and this ledger writes it in capitals ('OPEN - measured 2026-08-23'). So 57 open rows matched neither bucket and fell into `defects_other`, which was DEFINED as `total - proven - open` and therefore always absorbed them silently.

Reported 14 open / 117 other. Actual, after every row was classified: 80 open / 39 fixed / 25 proven / 11 withdrawn / 1 superseded.
D-THE-DEFECT-COUNTER-PARSED-ENGLISH-AND-.why_it_survived: The guard over it asserted `proven + open + other == total`. Since `other` is the remainder, that identity holds for EVERY possible partition, including a classifier that scores nothing at all. A vacuous assertion over a remainder bucket cannot go red.
D-THE-DEFECT-COUNTER-PARSED-ENGLISH-AND-.the_fix: `state` is now closed (open|fixed|proven|withdrawn|superseded), is the only field consulted, and an unrecognised or missing value raises. `defects_other` is deleted, and `apply_progress` drops retired keys so it cannot linger at its last value. All 156 rows were classified by rule where the first clause is unambiguous and by an explicit OVERRIDE table where it is not; each override carries its reason in the row as `state_reason`.
D-THE-DEFECT-COUNTER-PARSED-ENGLISH-AND-.what_the_triage_found: 13 overrides, and 4 of them were rows the loop had already closed and never re-statused - the synonym tie (lint now reports 0 live ties), the jargon scrubber (guard shipped at stream_events.py:142), the registry tenancy bar (probe exists). D-THE-DEFECT-COUNTER-PARSED-ENGLISH-AND-.red_on_original: PROVEN RED, in memory on a deepcopy - never by editing and restoring the ledger. Parametrised over the shapes that actually shipped: a missing `state`, the verbatim 'OPEN - measured 2026-08-23', 'opened', and 'Open'. Each must raise; under the old counter each was scored as not-open and counted as `other`.

D-THE-MODEL-FABRICATES-A-MONEY-VALUE-ON-.what_is_NOT_covered:
- ONE ARGUMENT ON ONE TOOL. `budget_usd` is the only money-typed argument in live use TODAY; a new one would not be covered until it is added to `MONEY_ARGS`, and nothing fails the build when that happens.
- THE AUTHOR TEST IS SESSION-WIDE, NOT TURN-WIDE. An author who mentioned a budget many turns ago licenses a number the model picks now. That is deliberate — the alternative refuses a figure they really gave — but it is a hole and a long session widens it.
- IT DOES NOT CHECK THE NUMBER IS THE ONE THEY SAID. An author who says '5 dollars' and a model that passes 50 sails through: the guard asks whether money was raised at all, not whether the value matches. That is a strictly harder test and is not attempted.

D-RECORDED-TOOL-RESULTS-ARE-TRUNCATED-AT.status: FIXED 2026-08-27. The cap is raised past every result these tools return, and — the durable half — a clipped record now SAYS SO and is refused rather than parsed.
D-RECORDED-TOOL-RESULTS-ARE-TRUNCATED-AT.what:
Tool-result content stored in docs/eval/toolloop/*-raw.json is cut at EXACTLY 4000 characters, mid-token. Distinct recorded content lengths in c-gbuild9 top out at 4000, and 17 kg_project_list results raise 'Unterminated string starting at ... column 3970' on json.loads.

So any analysis that PARSES a recorded result silently fails on every large one, and fails in the direction that looks like a finding: an empty parse reads as 'the tool returned nothing', not as 'the recording is clipped'.
D-RECORDED-TOOL-RESULTS-ARE-TRUNCATED-AT.how_it_bit: My kg_build provenance check reported the project_id came from kg_project_list on 0 of 10 runs. That is the shape of a real and serious finding - it would mean the runtime's context-fill supplied the id and the declaration did nothing. Reading one run by hand refuted it; a substring check gave 10/10.
D-RECORDED-TOOL-RESULTS-ARE-TRUNCATED-AT.why_it_matters: This loop's conclusions are largely derived by sweeping these files. Every such sweep that json.loads a result is under-counting by an unknown amount, and none of them says so.
D-RECORDED-TOOL-RESULTS-ARE-TRUNCATED-AT.not_yet_known: WHETHER THE MODEL SAW THE TRUNCATED TEXT TOO, or only the recording is clipped. Those are very different defects - the first is a live capability bug, the second is an instrument bug - and this row does not claim either. The cap is a suspiciously round 4000, which points at a deliberate recording limit rather than a transport failure, but that is a lead, not a finding.

D-RECORDED-TOOL-RESULTS-ARE-TRUNCATED-AT.the_fix:
1. `RESULT_CAP = 250_000` replaces the inline 4000 at the recording site.
2. `content_length` is recorded WHETHER OR NOT it clipped, with a `truncated` flag. This is the half that survives the next big result: a cap can always be exceeded, and raising one alone moves the cliff rather than removing it.
3. `parsed_result()` REFUSES a clipped record with `TruncatedResult`, naming the cap and the true size. A bare json.loads raises JSONDecodeError, an analysis catches it, and the tool reads as having returned nothing — which is exactly how this loop twice reported a provenance defect that did not exist.
4. THE 676 RECORDS ALREADY ON DISK ARE HANDLED. They predate the length field, so a content of exactly 4000 with no `content_length` is treated as the signature of a clip and refused. A result that genuinely ends at 4000 would be refused too — a false refusal, and the safe direction: the caller is told to re-run, not told a number.

D-RECORDED-TOOL-RESULTS-ARE-TRUNCATED-AT.what_is_NOT_covered:
- THE 676 RECORDS STAY UNREADABLE. Nothing recovers text that was never written down; the fix is that they are now REFUSED instead of parsed into a wrong answer. Any conclusion this loop drew by parsing a result before 2026-08-27 is suspect and must be re-derived from a fresh batch.
- ONLY `results` IS FIXED. The same file still clips `error` at 300, `prior_turns.text` at 800 and the batch `answer` at 2000, and none of those records its true length. They were left alone because no analysis parses them as structured data — which is an argument about today's usage, not a property of the record.
- `parsed_result` IS OPT-IN. An analysis that calls json.loads directly still gets a JSONDecodeError it can swallow. Nothing forces the reader; what the record now guarantees is that the information to tell clipped from empty is THERE.
- THE LEGACY RULE IS A HEURISTIC on the exact old cap. A pre-2026-08-27 result of exactly 4000 real characters is refused as if clipped.

D-A-STOP-REQUEST-PROPOSES-A-COST-BEARING.the_spend_declaration_is_missing_2026_08:
🔴 THE ROW SAYS THESE TOOLS SPEND MONEY. THE PLATFORM DOES NOT KNOW THAT. Checked against `_meta.paid`, which is the ONLY thing that makes a call clear the SPEND gate:

    translation_start_job          description says 'COSTS money'   paid: FALSE
    translation_retranslate_dirty  description says 'COSTS money'   paid: FALSE
    translation_job_control        description says 'SPEND money'   paid: FALSE
    translation_start_extraction   description says 'COSTS money'   paid: FALSE
    composition_authoring_run_manage   schema takes budget_usd      paid: FALSE
    composition_authoring_run_create   schema takes budget_usd      paid: FALSE

Six tools, two independent arms, no overlap. Across the whole 316-tool catalogue only 13 declare `paid`, and of the 5 whose own DESCRIPTION says they cost money exactly ONE does.

SO WHAT STOPPED THESE RUNS WAS THE MUTATION CARD, NOT A SPEND GATE. `_required_kinds` gains 'spend' only when `tool_paid()` is true, so for all six the spend check is never consulted and the card is never marked `spend: True` — which is precisely the wire signal that lets the FE render 'this costs money' differently from 'this modifies data'. A user holding a standing mutation allow would run them with no money prompt at all.

The platform's own recipe says it out loud for one of them — 'composition_authoring_run_manage (op="start") … This SPENDS money' — beside a declaration that says it does not.

🔴 AND A SESSION-LEVEL COUNT WOULD HAVE SAID 116. That was my first query and it is wrong by construction: a session holding a stop turn also holds every other turn, so a start called two turns earlier counts against the stop. The per-turn pairing is the honest unit and it cuts the number by six.

D-A-STOP-REQUEST-PROPOSES-A-COST-BEARING.the_spend_declaration_CORRECTION_2026_08:
🔴 THE ENTRY ABOVE OVERCLAIMED AND IS CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN EDITED AWAY. It said these tools 'SPEND MONEY' and the platform 'does not know that'. What `_meta.paid` declares is whether CALLING the tool spends — and translation_start_job / translation_retranslate_dirty are Tier-W tools that ESTIMATE and mint a confirm token; the spend happens on the human's approval via a separate re-pricing route. On the flag's documented meaning, `paid: False` is correct for them.

SO WHAT STOPPED THESE RUNS — the confirm card — IS THE DESIGNED GUARD, not a lucky substitute for a missing spend gate, and this row's own 'THE CONFIRM CARD, AND NOTHING ELSE' reading was right as written.

WHAT SURVIVES: the platform has no single meaning for `paid` on a confirm-minting tool — composition_library_translate declares True on the identical shape — which is now DQ-T60's actual question. It does not change this row's defect, which is that a STOP request produced a START proposal on 5 of 5 runs.
D-A-STOP-REQUEST-PROPOSES-A-COST-BEARING.the_spend_declaration_RESOLVED_2026_08_2:

The real finding moved elsewhere: composition_library_translate carried the flag on the identical shape, and it is the one that was corrected. THIS ROW'S DEFECT IS UNTOUCHED — a STOP request produced a START proposal on 5 of 5 runs, and no reading of `_meta.paid` makes that acceptable.

D-A-STOP-REQUEST-PROPOSES-A-COST-BEARING.the_invariant: A turn that asks to STOP work must not propose STARTING it. The confirm card is the LAST line, not the only one: a card reading 'start translation' put in front of an author who asked to cancel one is a single click from the opposite of what they asked for.
D-A-STOP-REQUEST-PROPOSES-A-COST-BEARING.the_fix:
TWO PIECES, both deterministic and both keyed on DECLARED data.

1. `request_mood` gains a HALT mood, built exactly as `inspect` is — literal match, no inference, no LLM, and a construct verb anywhere disqualifies it so a mixed request keeps every existing behaviour.

2. A gate at the tool-dispatch chokepoint: on a HALT turn, a Tier-W/A/S call whose OWN declared vocabulary does not answer a stop request is refused BEFORE it runs, and comes back as a tool error the model can act on.

🔴 THE TEST IS THE TOOL'S DECLARATION, NEVER ITS NAME. There is no `starts_work` flag to read: against the live catalogue translation_start_job, translation_retranslate_dirty, translation_start_extraction and composition_authoring_run_create carry only {tier, scope, synonyms, async}. A `*_start_*` prefix rule would be the name classifier CP-4.d deleted for inferring a property from fragments of an identifier. So the gate asks what `answerable_tools` already answers everywhere else — does THIS declaration answer THIS request? Measured on the rows' own prompts: translation_job_control and jobs_cancel answerable, all four start tools NOT. Four for four on the wrong side, with no list of names written anywhere.

SCOPED TO WRITES: a READ is how the turn finds the job to stop, so jobs_list stays free. Both scopes are pinned by inverse edit — dropping the answerability check blocks the CANCEL tool itself, dropping the tier check blocks the read.
D-A-STOP-REQUEST-PROPOSES-A-COST-BEARING.the_control:
THE MOOD WAS NARROWED TWICE BY ITS OWN FALSE POSITIVES, measured over 1,917 real user messages, and each narrowing was FORCED rather than chosen up front:

    v1  bare halt verb                    47 matched (2.5%) — including 'Count from 1 to 2000 … Do NOT stop early', which asks for the OPPOSITE of a stop.
    v2  + must name WORK, no construct    12 matched (0.63%) — still catching harness probe LABELS like 'RUN-D7-KILL: list the chapters…', where the label says KILL and the request says list.
    v3  + verb not hyphen-joined           8 matched (0.42%) — all eight genuine stop requests.

Controls hold in both directions: the negation and probe-label cases are excluded, the rows' own instances are included, and a mixed request ('Cancel the job and then rewrite chapter 2') stays CONSTRUCT so nothing existing changes.
D-A-STOP-REQUEST-PROPOSES-A-COST-BEARING.proven_live:
batch c-haltgate2, K=5, this row's OWN scenario extracted verbatim (batch39 `jobs-cancel`: list the jobs, then the follow-up 'Stop the translation one.') — the shape that produced 5/5 start proposals.

    runs that still REACHED for translation_start_job     3 of 5
    attempts refused by the gate                          6 of 6
    start tools that EXECUTED                             0
    confirm tokens minted for a start                     0

And the recovery is the part worth quoting: after the refusal the model turns to the thing actually asked for — 'I can cancel that translation job for you' — rather than looping or reporting an error at the author.

🔴 THE MODEL'S TENDENCY IS UNCHANGED AND THE ROW SAYS SO. It still reaches for the start tool on 3 of 5 runs; what changed is that the reach can no longer become a card. This is a platform guard over a model behaviour, not a correction of the model.

Suite 3,767 passed. Two inverse edits proven RED. Deployed and verified by sha256 from inside the container.
D-A-STOP-REQUEST-PROPOSES-A-COST-BEARING.what_is_NOT_covered:
- THE MODEL STILL PROPOSES IT (3 of 5). The gate stops the proposal reaching the author; it does not stop the model reaching for the tool, and nothing here claims to.
- HALT IS A LITERAL MATCHER, deliberately. It fires on 0.42% of the corpus and answers `unknown` whenever it is not confident, so a phrasing it does not recognise is simply unprotected — the same conservative bargain `inspect` makes.
- A MIXED REQUEST IS UNPROTECTED BY DESIGN. 'Cancel the job and then rewrite chapter 2' is CONSTRUCT, so the gate is inert there; suppressing writes on a turn that also asks for one would break the request.
- IT RESTS ON DECLARED SYNONYMS. A stop-capable tool that declares no stop vocabulary would be refused on a halt turn — the failure mode is a REFUSAL, not a silent wrong action, and the message names what to do instead.

Asked to record that two characters know each other, the turn spends its passes and approvals one node at a time and SUSPENDS on the card for the second node - before kg_propose_edge is ever reached.

D-A-TWO-ENDPOINT-EDGE-NEEDS-N-SEQUENTIAL.and_this_rows_own_case_is_not_in_the_map:
🔴 kg_propose_edge DECLARES NO EMITTER. Its endpoints are described as 'The id of the relationship's source entity.' and nothing says where an entity id comes from - it is in the 53-pair group the emitter-arm cycle measured, where the description states WHAT the value is and never WHERE to get it.

AND THE OBVIOUS DECLARATION WOULD BE WRONG, which is why it is not being made here. The endpoints must be EXISTING `:Entity` node ids (existing_entity_node_ids, matched by Entity.id, with KG_ENDPOINT_NOT_NODE rejecting anything else up front). The free Tier-R reader that returns node ids is kg_graph_query - but in this scenario the two characters exist in the GLOSSARY and not yet as graph NODES, so kg_graph_query would return nothing and pointing the model at it would be pointing at an empty tool. The supplier here is a CREATE, and which create depends on state the declaration cannot express.
D-A-TWO-ENDPOINT-EDGE-NEEDS-N-SEQUENTIAL.theory_recorded_BEFORE_the_change_2026_0:
Per METHOD step 2 and this row's own 'measures before it names a cause'.

THE BASELINE, re-derived rather than taken from the row. The artifact does NOT carry the mode argument - c-kgedge2-raw.json records tool NAMES and no args, so 'chose manual on 5 of 5' cannot be re-derived from the file the row cites. It IS recoverable from the store: over the five sessions, chat_messages.tool_calls holds mode='manual' on 5 kg_add_nodes calls and from_glossary on ZERO. The row's claim is corroborated, by a different source than the one it names.

THE THEORY. The `mode` description states neither CARDINALITY nor COST:
    'manual = create one node (name+kind); from_glossary = project the book's glossary entities into the graph.'
A model asked to record two named characters matches 'create one node' to its task and repeats it. Nothing there says from_glossary handles MANY endpoints in ONE call, nothing says manual costs one confirm card PER node, and 'project ... into the graph' is jargon that does not read as 'create nodes for the people you already defined'. The row's own evidence supports this over the 'listed first' guess: on two runs the model called tool_load to RE-READ this very description and still chose manual - it read the words and the words did not carry the fact.

THE CHANGE UNDER TEST, deliberately minimal: state each mode's cardinality and its approval cost. No advice about which to prefer beyond those facts, because this loop has measured twice that telling the model HOW to choose makes it choose badly (D-WORKFLOW-LIST..., where the self-filter invitation was reverted).

WHAT I WILL COUNT, K=5, same scenario, same approvals (approved_always):
    from_glossary chosen at all      baseline 0/5 runs
    runs reaching kg_propose_edge    baseline 1/5 (and its endpoints missing on all 3 tries)
    runs ending SUSPENDED            baseline 4/5

REFUTED IF from_glossary is still chosen on 0 runs, or the suspended rate does not move. PREDICTION: I expect from_glossary on at least 2 of 5. I hold it loosely - this loop's description predictions have been wrong four times running, every time by UNDER-estimating what a description does to this model.

D-A-TIER-R-TOOL-WRITES-TO-THE-STORE.investigated_2026_08_26:
The row admitted it had not read the write path. Read now, and it is worse than the row guessed. `plan_validate` (Tier R) calls TWO writes in PlanForgeService.validate:
    save_artifact(created_by, run_id, 'validation_report', report)   - the report
    if all_pass: update_run(book_id, run_id, status='validated')     - a STATE TRANSITION

🔴 AND THAT STATUS IS AN AUTHORISATION GATE. authoring_run_service.py:113 reads
    _APPROVED_PLAN_STATUSES = ('validated', 'compiled')
so a plan in 'validated' is authorised to start an autonomous authoring run - the multi-chapter drafting run that SPENDS LLM tokens. A tool the platform classifies as a READ moves a plan into the approved set.

WHAT TIER R MEANS HERE, from the SDK's own definition (sdks/go/loreweave_mcp/meta.go):
    R = read - no confirm, doesn't count against the write budget
    A = auto-commit + activity/Undo strip
So this transition needs no confirmation, is invisible to the write budget, AND never appears in the activity/Undo strip. The plan's status changes and the author has no record that it did.

🔴 A CONFOUND WAS CHASED AND REFUTED BEFORE ANY OF THIS WAS BELIEVED. The harness snapshots AFTER seeding (deliberately - its docstring says a seed inside the window would make every scenario report a change), but a seed's ASYNC tail could still land after the snapshot and read as a turn write. Tested by dating every write against fixture creation, which the UUIDv7 book_id encodes: the median gap is 15-40s and the MINIMUM across all tables is 10.5s, so no write sits in the seed's immediate wake.
