D-SEED-ASSERT-CANNOT-ADDRESS-THE-GRAPH.status: FIXED 2026-08-26 — `db: "neo4j"` now routes to cypher-shell, proven in both directions: a graph assertion PASSES when the fixture matches and REFUSES when it does not, which is the seed_assert's real job the row said was missing.
D-SEED-ASSERT-CANNOT-ADDRESS-THE-GRAPH.what:
A scenario's `seed_assert` runs `psql` against a named Postgres database. Facts, entities and events live in NEO4J, so an assertion over them cannot be written: the harness refused the batch with 'db_query failed (neo4j): psql: error: ... database "neo4j" does not exist'.

THE REFUSAL IS CORRECT AND IS NOT THE DEFECT - a scenario whose assertion cannot execute measures nothing, and declining to start is the right call. The defect is that a whole class of seeded state cannot be preflighted at all, so a graph-seeded scenario runs with no guard that its seed landed.
D-SEED-ASSERT-CANNOT-ADDRESS-THE-GRAPH.the_workaround_used: store_snapshot._neo4j already emits `neo4j.Fact.project` {rows, latest}, so the before/after Fact count IS in every run's store_diff and the falsifier can read it. That covers the count; it does not cover a seed_assert's real job, which is to refuse to START when the fixture is wrong.
D-SEED-ASSERT-CANNOT-ADDRESS-THE-GRAPH.candidate_direction_NOT_MEASURED: seed_assert already dispatches on a `db` field; a 'neo4j' value could route to cypher-shell the way store_snapshot._neo4j already does, reusing that helper rather than adding a second way to reach the graph. Not built and not measured - the expect-value comparison for a Cypher scalar is the open question.
D-SEED-ASSERT-CANNOT-ADDRESS-THE-GRAPH.measured_by: assert_seeded + preflight_seed_asserts exercised against the live graph, 2026-08-26; store_snapshot re-run through the unified reader
D-SEED-ASSERT-CANNOT-ADDRESS-THE-GRAPH.the_chokepoint_is_db_query_not_the_call_: The candidate direction was right and the placement mattered. Both seed-assert paths go through `oracle.db_query(c['db'], sql)` — `preflight_seed_asserts` (every query once, before the batch spends a turn) and `assert_seeded` (per-run, against the real fixture) — so the dispatch lives THERE. Routing at each call site would have been two chances to diverge, and the preflight is exactly the half that would have been forgotten.
D-SEED-ASSERT-CANNOT-ADDRESS-THE-GRAPH.the_open_question_answered_itself: The row recorded 'the expect-value comparison for a Cypher scalar is the open question'. It needs no new rule: cypher-shell `--format plain` prints a header line then the rows, the same shape psql's `-tA` gives, so `rows[0][0]` compared as a stripped string is identical on both stores. Pinned by a guard that asserts the two return the same shape.
D-SEED-ASSERT-CANNOT-ADDRESS-THE-GRAPH.one_reader_not_two_and_the_second_one_he:
The row's own instruction was to reuse the existing helper 'rather than adding a second way to reach the graph'. store_snapshot._neo4j had an inline cypher-shell call; it now calls oracle.cypher_query, and a guard fails if a second one appears in the harness.

🔴 WRITING THAT GUARD FOUND A THIRD READER, AND IT HARDCODED THE CREDENTIAL. memory_forget_idempotency_probe.py ran its own cypher-shell with `-p loreweave_dev_neo4j` written into the tree. Unified onto the shared reader, which asks the container that owns the connection — and a second guard now fails on that literal anywhere in the harness.

The guard is SCOPED to the harness, and its first version was not: it asserted nothing under scripts/ reaches the graph except oracle, which was never true. scripts/seed_fengshen_demo.py is a one-off DEMO SEEDER outside the measurement path — excluded by name rather than silently.
D-SEED-ASSERT-CANNOT-ADDRESS-THE-GRAPH.a_diagnosis_defect_found_by_exercising_t:
The first preflight run rejected a VALID query and blamed the JVM. cypher-shell prints four lines of 'WARNING: A restricted method in java.lang.System has been called' to stderr on every invocation, so a bare [:400] truncation showed only those — a syntax error in the caller's Cypher arrived as a Java module warning. Warnings are now stripped before the message is built:
    BEFORE: cypher_query failed: WARNING: A restricted method in java.lang.System ...
    AFTER : cypher_query failed: 42I06: syntax error ... Invalid input 'RETURN', expected: a parameter, '&', ')', ':', 'WHERE', '{' or '|'
This is the same class as the harness's own recorded lesson about an ExceptionGroup burying a clear server error — an instrument that reports the wrong cause costs more than one with no message.
D-SEED-ASSERT-CANNOT-ADDRESS-THE-GRAPH.proof:
assert_seeded against the live graph (455 Facts):
    expect '455'    -> PASSED, the batch would start
    expect '999999' -> REFUSED: 'SEED ASSERTION FAILED: the seeded facts are present / expected 999999, store says 455'
preflight_seed_asserts, which is the half that runs before any turn is spent:
    valid Cypher  -> accepted
    broken Cypher -> rejected, naming the real syntax error
store_snapshot still reads the graph through the shared runner (neo4j.Fact.total = 455), and Postgres is untouched (`SELECT 1` -> [['1']]).
D-SEED-ASSERT-CANNOT-ADDRESS-THE-GRAPH.what_is_NOT_covered:
- NO SCENARIO USES IT YET. The capability is proven directly; scenarios-c-factsearch.json, the file that hit this, still carries the recorded reason it has no graph assertion. Rewriting it is a separate change and would want its own batch.
- READ-ONLY IS BY CONVENTION, NOT ENFORCED. `cypher_query` will happily run a write — nothing rejects a CREATE/MERGE the way a scenario author might assume. The Postgres side has the same property, so this is not a regression, but a seed_assert that mutates the graph would corrupt the very fixture it is checking.
- ONE CELL PER ROW. The parser returns each line as a single cell; a multi-column Cypher RETURN is not split the way psql's `-F|` splits columns. Every assertion this loop writes is a scalar, so it was not built — but a two-column query would silently come back joined.
- THE DEMO SEEDER IS UNTOUCHED and still has its own cypher-shell call, named above.
D-SEED-ASSERT-CANNOT-ADDRESS-THE-GRAPH.red_able: scripts/test_a_seed_assertion_can_address_the_graph.py, 8 guards: the defect verbatim (db='neo4j' reaches the graph at all), shape-parity with a Postgres scalar, Postgres unaffected, a bad query RAISES rather than reporting zero, an unreachable graph is not silently clean, one reader in the harness, no hardcoded password, and the snapshot still reads through it. Whole scripts suite: 516 passed.

D-THE-EMITTER-ARM-IS-UNREACHABLE-WITHOUT.what:

R1 transitivity only expands from tools the request already made ANSWERABLE, so a tool reached by any other route - a rail, the hot seed, an explicit tool_load - gets no supplier forced onto the wire and a refusal that names none either. On c-forgetchain2 the chain closed via transitivity; the refusal contributed nothing.
D-THE-EMITTER-ARM-IS-UNREACHABLE-WITHOUT.candidate_direction_NOT_MEASURED: Name a declared emitter regardless of the `owed` branch - the map is the same structured source either way, and a declaration is a fact about the catalogue, not about who owes the value. NOT measured: whether that would change the model's behaviour where transitivity already surfaces the supplier is exactly the question a stripped-declaration control answered NO to once already this run, so the recall must be measured before it is recommended.

D-THE-MODEL-ASKS-INSTEAD-OF-RAISING-THE-.the_root_cause_2026_08_28:
DROPPING A DECLARATION WAS DROPPING ITS VOCABULARY.

`answerable_tools` carries a rule it calls R2: *whatever phrasing reaches A must also be able to reach the tool that REPLACED A*, because 59 of 62 superseded pairs orphan at least one phrasing. R2 implements it as a union over the catalogue it is handed — if A matched, add A's `superseded_by`.

The 2026-08-25 widening silently disabled it. Per-pass answerability reads `cat_index = _catalog_index(discovery_catalog)` (stream_service.py:4260), and `discovery_catalog` is the OUTPUT of `drop_superseded_tools`, with every legacy tool already removed. So R2 had nothing left to union from, at exactly the pairs it was written for.

MEASURED in the deployed container against the live 316-tool catalogue, this row's own prompt:
    answerable over the FULL catalogue       -> {composition_canon_rule_restore,
                                                 composition_canon_rule_edit}   (R2 fired)
    answerable over drop_superseded_tools'
      OUTPUT (what per-pass R1 reads)        -> {}                              (R2 inert)

The successor DOES declare 'restore canon rule', but the author wrote 'please restore it'; the phrase that actually matched, 'undo delete rule', belonged to the tool the gate had just deleted.

THE SERVER'S OWN LOG SAID SO AND I HAD NOT READ IT: `R1 answerability: request matches [...]` appears ONCE per session (the discarded first-pass build, which reads the full catalogue) and every wire pass then logs `0 promised for pass N, 0 on the wire`. One 'matches' line against six '0 promised' lines is the defect, in the platform's own words.
D-THE-MODEL-ASKS-INSTEAD-OF-RAISING-THE-.the_invariant: Dropping a declaration must not drop its VOCABULARY. When the superseded gate removes a legacy tool, the phrasing that tool declared transfers to the live successor that replaced it — following a chain of `superseded_by` hops to the first non-legacy tool.
D-THE-MODEL-ASKS-INSTEAD-OF-RAISING-THE-.the_fix:
ONE chokepoint: `drop_superseded_tools` (tool_discovery.py), the function that destroys the information, now carries it forward via `_inherit_superseded_vocabulary` + `_final_live_successor`. Non-mutating (the federated catalogue is cached per-user in knowledge_client and shared across turns, so an in-place edit would leak one turn's inheritance into every later reader).

Free on the wire: `_meta` is consumer-only and `strip_tool_meta` removes it before the provider request, so an inherited synonym costs ZERO tokens. It repairs every reader of the narrowed catalogue at once — R1 answerability, find_tools recall, the declaration arm, the reads-only mood check — not R1 alone.

The withheld record now names where the vocabulary went: 'superseded by X, which now also answers to this tool's declared phrasing'.

    COST   mean 0.069 extra tools forced per turn, median 0, max 3
    RECALL 115 of 1,917 turns (6.0%) gain at least one, across 7 distinct successors

dominated by the two pairs R2's own comment names — book_get->book_read (52) and book_scene_list->book_list (70). A second variant (make R1 read the full catalogue instead) measured 0.055/turn and 100 turns (5.2%) across 13 successors; it was rejected for needing a new parameter threaded through 3 call sites and 2 signatures while fixing R1 ALONE.

It passed 20 unit tests, deployed clean (sha256 verified from inside the container), and did NOTHING live — batch c-canonrestore2, 0/5, store unchanged.

Two independent reasons, both found only by reading the server's records:
  1. It could not fire for this instance at all. `composition_canon_rule_edit` was ALREADY      in `discovery_catalog` when the function ran, so `replacement in kept_names` skipped      it — which is why the withheld record still showed the un-promoted reason text.

🔴 `--turn-timeout` WAS INERT. `send_turn`'s signature read `timeout=TURN_TIMEOUT`, and a default binds at IMPORT — so setting the module global in `main()` moved the AsyncClient's timeout and never the per-turn request that overrides it.

SILENCE, NOT TURN LENGTH. `httpx.Timeout(N)` sets read=N, which on a streaming response is the gap between CHUNKS. Measured while trying to force a failure: at 4s not one run timed out, because the SSE stream keeps emitting; at 0.6s all three did.

So a ReadTimeout in this row's failures means the stream WENT SILENT for 180 seconds — which agrees with the row's own finding that the timed-out runs recorded no tool calls and an empty answer. It is a turn that produces nothing, not a slow one. Raising the timeout would only have made the harness wait longer on a dead stream, so even a working flag would probably not have moved the number.

1. `request_mood` gains a HALT mood, built exactly as `inspect` is — literal match, no inference, no LLM, and a construct verb anywhere disqualifies it so a mixed request keeps every existing behaviour.

2. A gate at the tool-dispatch chokepoint: on a HALT turn, a Tier-W/A/S call whose OWN declared vocabulary does not answer a stop request is refused BEFORE it runs, and comes back as a tool error the model can act on.

A `*_start_*` prefix rule would be the name classifier CP-4.d deleted for inferring a property from fragments of an identifier. So the gate asks what `answerable_tools` already answers everywhere else — does THIS declaration answer THIS request? Measured on the rows' own prompts: translation_job_control and jobs_cancel answerable, all four start tools NOT. Four for four on the wrong side, with no list of names written anywhere.

SCOPED TO WRITES: a READ is how the turn finds the job to stop, so jobs_list stays free. Both scopes are pinned by inverse edit — dropping the answerability check blocks the CANCEL tool itself, dropping the tier check blocks the read.

D-FROM-GLOSSARY-REPORTS-SUCCESS-HAVING-C.status: FIXED - proven on the deployed build in BOTH directions: the measured call is refused with an actionable message, and the path that works is untouched.
D-FROM-GLOSSARY-REPORTS-SUCCESS-HAVING-C.what:
kg_add_nodes mode=from_glossary was called with entity_ids=['Mira Solene', 'Aldric Vane'] - NAMES, where the argument takes glossary entity UUIDs. The tool returned:
    ok: true, nodes: [], entities_seen: 0, nodes_created: 0, nodes_existing: 0
and the activity strip recorded 'Did kg_add_nodes'. A call that matched nothing, created nothing and touched nothing is reported to the model, and to the human's activity feed, as a completed write.
D-FROM-GLOSSARY-REPORTS-SUCCESS-HAVING-C.why_it_matters: The model has no way to tell this apart from a real projection. Its next move assumes two nodes exist. `entities_seen: 0` is the tool's own evidence that the argument matched nothing - it is IN the payload and nothing acts on it. This is the same shape as an unconditional success that discards its own signal.
D-FROM-GLOSSARY-REPORTS-SUCCESS-HAVING-C.the_two_halves: (1) A zero-match from_glossary should say so - 'none of the 2 entity_ids matched a glossary entity in this book' - rather than ok:true with empty counts. (2) The arg description reads 'mode=from_glossary: optional specific glossary entity ids; omit for the whole active glossary' and never says they are UUIDs, nor where to get them (glossary_search / glossary_propose_entities return them). A name is the obvious thing to pass.
D-FROM-GLOSSARY-REPORTS-SUCCESS-HAVING-C.not_investigated: Whether the omit-entirely path (no entity_ids, 'the whole active glossary') works - it was never exercised, and it is the path that would have projected both characters in one call.
D-FROM-GLOSSARY-REPORTS-SUCCESS-HAVING-C.measured_by: direct MCPDirect probe of both directions against the deployed build, 2026-08-26; the original observation in docs/eval/toolloop/2026-08-14/c-kgedge3.json
D-FROM-GLOSSARY-REPORTS-SUCCESS-HAVING-C.the_fix_is_narrow_and_the_narrowness_is_:
The predicate is 'the caller NAMED entity_ids AND none of them matched', not 'nothing was projected'. Omitting entity_ids means 'the whole active glossary', and a book whose glossary is genuinely empty is a legitimate no-op - that is ALSO the route measured working end to end in c-kgedge4 (entities_seen 2, both nodes created, edge parked, 5/5). Refusing on a bare zero would have closed this row by breaking the only path that succeeds, which is the kind of fix this loop exists to catch.

The PARTIAL match gets a note rather than a refusal: naming five ids and matching three is the same defect in miniature - a cheerful success that never mentions the two which do not exist - but three real nodes WERE created and refusing would throw them away.
D-FROM-GLOSSARY-REPORTS-SUCCESS-HAVING-C.also_fixed_the_argument_that_invited_the: The description read 'mode=from_glossary: optional specific glossary entity ids; omit for the whole active glossary'. It never said they are UUIDs, and never said where one comes from - so a NAME is the obvious thing to pass, and the model passed two. It now leads with the easier and usually-correct route (omit it) and says the ids are glossary entity UUIDs from glossary_search, not names.
D-FROM-GLOSSARY-REPORTS-SUCCESS-HAVING-C.proof:
Deployed build, file sha256-verified equal in the container, gateway re-federated:

  A) THE MEASURED DEFECT - entity_ids=['Mira Solene','Aldric Vane']:
     REFUSED: 'none of the 2 entity_ids matched a glossary entity in this book, so nothing was projected and the graph is unchanged. `entity_ids` takes glossary entity UUIDs, not names - get them from glossary_search, or omit the argument entirely to project the book's whole active glossary.'
     Before: ok:true, nodes:[], entities_seen:0, nodes_created:0, and 'Did kg_add_nodes' in the activity strip.

  B) THE RECALL CONTROL - entity_ids omitted, on a project whose glossary is empty:
     OK, entities_seen=0, nodes_created=0 - NOT refused, because no ids were named. This is the case that would have caught a too-wide predicate, and it is the reason it was run.
D-FROM-GLOSSARY-REPORTS-SUCCESS-HAVING-C.what_is_NOT_covered:
- NO CHAT BATCH. The refusal fires only when the model passes ids that match nothing, and after the argument description changed it has no reason to - the batch that produced this defect (c-kgedge3) is exactly the run whose behaviour the sibling fix moved. Engineering a prompt to force bad ids would be building a scenario to hit my own fix; the live proof is the direct probe of both directions.
- THE ACTIVITY STRIP IS UNTOUCHED. 'Did kg_add_nodes' was the human-facing half of the same falsehood, and a refused call no longer reaches it - but a call that projects ZERO nodes legitimately (empty glossary, path B) still records 'Did kg_add_nodes' to a human. Not fixed, not measured, and arguably correct.
- OTHER ZERO-EFFECT SUCCESSES IN THIS FAMILY ARE UNAUDITED. The same shape - a filter argument that matches nothing and returns ok:true with empty counts - is available to any tool taking an id list. Only this one was measured and only this one is fixed.
D-FROM-GLOSSARY-REPORTS-SUCCESS-HAVING-C.red_able:
services/knowledge-service/tests/unit/test_a_projection_that_matched_nothing_is_not_a_success.py, 10 guards including a four-case truth table that drives the REAL handler. Inverse edit - the guard disabled with `if False and ...` - reds the measured case; source restored byte-identical.

🔴 AND THE INJECTION EXPOSED A WEAKNESS IN MY OWN GUARDS. The SOURCE-TEXT assertions stayed GREEN through it, because `if False and entity_ids and res.seen == 0` still contains the string they look for. Only the behavioural case caught it. D-ENTITY-ID-MEANS-TWO-DIFFERENT-IDS-IN-A.status: FIXED - proven live 2026-08-26, batch c-kgedge4, K=5: the turn completes end to end on 5 of 5 runs (0 of 5 the batch before). Two id families, a description that named neither, and a recovery path that named a DEAD tool.
D-ENTITY-ID-MEANS-TWO-DIFFERENT-IDS-IN-A.what:
A GLOSSARY entity id and a graph `:Entity` NODE id are different objects with the same shape and the same name. kg_propose_edge's arguments are `source_entity_id` / `target_entity_id`, described as 'The id of the relationship's source entity.' - and it requires NODE ids: existing_entity_node_ids matches on Entity.id and KG_ENDPOINT_NOT_NODE rejects anything else.

Measured: on 3 of 3 edge calls the model passed the GLOSSARY entity ids, matched exactly against the run's own seed_ids (glossary_propose_entities.results[N].entity_id). Well-formed UUIDs, real objects, wrong family.
D-ENTITY-ID-MEANS-TWO-DIFFERENT-IDS-IN-A.why_it_matters: This is the root of D-A-TWO-ENDPOINT-EDGE-NEEDS-N-SEQUENTIAL-CONFIRM-CARDS and it survives every fix aimed at the card cost. Cheapening the node-creation path does not help a caller who does not know it needs to create a node at all - it HAS an 'entity id' and the argument asks for one.
D-ENTITY-ID-MEANS-TWO-DIFFERENT-IDS-IN-A.candidate_directions_NOT_MEASURED: (a) name the argument for what it is (source_node_id), which is a breaking rename of a published tool; (b) say it in the description - 'a graph NODE id from kg_add_nodes or kg_graph_query, NOT a glossary entity id' - and declare the emitter, which the emitter-arm fix now makes sayable in a refusal; (c) ACCEPT a glossary entity id and project it, which turns a rejection into the one-call path the model keeps reaching for. Each is a different owner-level trade and none is measured.
D-ENTITY-ID-MEANS-TWO-DIFFERENT-IDS-IN-A.measured_by: docs/eval/toolloop/2026-08-14/c-kgedge4.json vs c-kgedge3.json (K=5 each); chat_messages.tool_calls + withheld_tools; drop_superseded_tools source, 2026-08-26
D-ENTITY-ID-MEANS-TWO-DIFFERENT-IDS-IN-A.the_second_half_was_worse_than_the_first:
🔴 THE PLATFORM'S OWN REMEDY NAMED A TOOL THE TURN CANNOT SEE. KG_ENDPOINT_NOT_NODE said 'project the glossary entities into the graph first (kg_project_entities_to_nodes)'. That tool is `visibility: legacy` — and on 2026-08-25 drop_superseded_tools was WIDENED to drop every legacy tool from every turn catalogue unconditionally ('a legacy tool is a DEAD tool'), not just those whose replacement is on the same wire. Measured over batch c-kgedge3, from chat_messages.withheld_tools: withheld on 5 of 5 runs, at stages `superseded` AND `domain_not_selected`.

So the sentence the runtime emits when a caller gets this exact thing wrong instructed the model to call something provably absent from its wire. Naming a tool is also what ARMS it onto the turn, so an unreachable name arms nothing: the refusal was not merely unhelpful, it consumed the one mechanism that could have helped.
D-ENTITY-ID-MEANS-TWO-DIFFERENT-IDS-IN-A.the_fix_three_surfaces_one_cause:
The cause is that a caller cannot tell the two id families apart, so it is answered at every point the caller could learn it:
  * THE ARGUMENTS say which family they need and where one comes from - 'The graph NODE id ... NOT a glossary entity id. Get it from kg_add_nodes ... or kg_graph_query; if the entity exists only in the glossary, kg_add_nodes with mode=from_glossary turns it into a node first.'
  * THE REFUSAL names the LIVE replacement and says which family was passed - 'these look like glossary entity ids, and an edge needs GRAPH NODE ids. Call kg_add_nodes with mode=from_glossary ... then use the node ids it returns.'
  * THE REGISTRY declares the emitter (kg_propose_edge.{source,target}_entity_id <- kg_add_nodes), which the emitter-arm fix earlier the same day makes SAYABLE in a refusal for a tool with no contract row - kg_propose_edge is exactly such a tool.

    projected BOTH entities              0/5         0/5         5/5
    reached kg_propose_edge              1/5         3/5         5/5
    edge PARKED (the turn's whole point) 0/5         0/5         5/5
    nodes created                          0           0          10

A census of instruction strings naming a `visibility: legacy` tool found ~11 live sites across knowledge and composition (kg_adopt_template twice, composition_motif_archive/restore/bind, composition_arc_move/create/assign_chapters, composition_authoring_run_pause, kg_build_graph). On 2026-08-25 `drop_superseded_tools` was widened to drop EVERY `visibility: legacy` tool from every turn catalogue unconditionally - 'a legacy tool is a DEAD tool'. An unreachable name therefore fails twice: the instruction cannot be followed, and the arming mechanism is spent on a tool that will be dropped again. Measured on the fixed instance: withheld 5 of 5 runs at stage `superseded`.
D-A-REFUSAL-NAMES-A-LEGACY-TOOL-THE-CATA.the_gate_this_needs: A build-failing check that no instruction string in a service names a tool that service registers with visibility=legacy. D-A-REFUSAL-NAMES-A-LEGACY-TOOL-THE-CATA.the_census_is_4_sites_not_11:

D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.status: FIXED - deployed and verified by content 2026-08-26. The scenario that lost 60% of its runs is clean 5/5, and 6 aborted turns since deploy produced ZERO duplicate-key 500s.
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.what:
Posting a message allocates its position with a READ-THEN-WRITE and no lock:
    seq = SELECT COALESCE(MAX(sequence_num),0)+1 FROM chat_messages WHERE session_id=$1 AND branch_id=0
    INSERT INTO chat_messages (... sequence_num ...) VALUES (... seq ... 0 ...)
and `idx_chat_messages_branch_unique` is UNIQUE on (session_id, sequence_num, branch_id). Two concurrent writers therefore compute the same number and one gets a 500.

The second writer is the platform's own: when a client aborts a turn, stream_service DETACHES the persist — 'interrupt-persist detached for session ... (write continues after cancel)' — and then writes the interrupted assistant reply. A client that retries the aborted turn races that detached write.
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.measured:
Reproduced 2026-08-26, batch c-motiflink13, 2 of 5 runs, with the chat-service log open. The sequence in one session:
    POST /messages -> 200 OK, turn starts
    interrupt-persist detached for session 01a03eaa-823b-... (write continues after cancel)
    terminal-persist: saved interrupted assistant reply ... 0 chars, outcome=abandoned_by_user
    POST /messages (the retry) -> 500
    duplicate key value violates unique constraint "idx_chat_messages_branch_unique"
    DETAIL: Key (session_id, sequence_num, branch_id)=(01a03eaa-..., 2, 0) already exists.
The interrupted assistant row took position 2; the retry's user message computed 2 as well.
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.why_it_matters:
This is what a user does when a reply is slow: stop it and ask again. The second ask 500s. It needs no harness and no unusual client — only an abort followed by a retry on the same session, which is the ordinary shape of impatience.

It also corrupts MEASUREMENT wherever it happens, because the two presentations look like different problems: the retry either 500s (HTTPStatusError) or hangs behind the same contention (ReadTimeout). The instrument row this was traced from recorded the second shape for weeks as 'the scenario times out'.
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.the_mechanism_does_NOT_exist: Checked before proposing one: there is NO advisory lock anywhere in chat-service (`pg_advisory` appears zero times), and the enclosing `conn.transaction()` does not help — under READ COMMITTED two transactions read the same MAX quite happily. Five other sites derive a sequence the same way (stream_service x3, voice_stream_service x2), so a fix at one call site would leave the class open.
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.candidate_direction_NOT_YET_MEASURED: A per-session advisory lock taken inside the existing transaction (pg_advisory_xact_lock on the session id) serialises allocation and releases at commit, with no migration and no schema change. The alternatives — retry-on-unique-violation, or a real per-session sequence — are heavier and one of them still needs the lock to be correct.
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.measured_by: docs/eval/toolloop/2026-08-14/c-motiflink13.json (reproduction with the log), c-motiflink14.json (my broken SQL), c-motiflink15.json (0/5 errors); chat-service log counts since deploy, 2026-08-26
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.the_fix:
`app/db/message_sequence.py::next_sequence_num` takes a per-session advisory lock (pg_advisory_xact_lock on hashtextextended(session_id, namespace)) and then reads MAX+1. The lock is held to COMMIT, so allocation and the INSERT that uses it are one indivisible step for a session; different sessions never contend.

Applied to the THREE allocation sites that already run inside a transaction — the message endpoint (the retry's user insert) and stream_service's two persist paths (the detached writer). A retry-on-unique-violation was rejected: it papers over the race while leaving two writers free to interleave, where the lock asserts the property the unique index is already claiming.
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.what_is_deliberately_NOT_converted:
The two VOICE sites (voice_stream_service:313 and :625) acquire a connection WITHOUT a transaction. pg_advisory_xact_lock there would be taken and released by its own statement — protecting nothing while looking protected, which is worse than no lock at all. So next_sequence_num REFUSES outside a transaction rather than degrading, and those two sites keep the old unlocked read: they carry the SAME race and are named here rather than silently half-fixed. Converting them means wrapping voice persistence in a transaction, a behaviour change on a surface this defect was never measured on.

A sixth MAX(sequence_num) read in stream_service is a cadence CLOCK, not an allocation, and is correctly untouched.
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.the_first_fix_was_worse_than_the_defect:
🔴 IT SHIPPED BROKEN SQL AND 3,608 GREEN TESTS COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT. The first version called `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended($1, 0), $2)` — a bigint AND an int — where Postgres has only `(key bigint)` or `(key1 int4, key2 int4)`. Every message POST then failed with `function pg_advisory_xact_lock(bigint, unknown) does not exist`: batch c-motiflink14, 5 of 5 runs, 0 tools called. Strictly worse than the defect it replaced.

The whole chat suite was green through it and always would have been: every test of this path uses a FAKE connection, so not one of 3,608 assertions executes a character of the SQL. Verifying the statement against the real database costs two seconds and is the only thing that could have caught it — which is now a test.
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.proof:
Deployed, container/host sha256 equal on all three files.

  BATCH, same scenario/concurrency/timeout as the failing ones:
    c-motiflink10   3/5 errored (ReadTimeout)
    c-motiflink11   3/5 errored (ReadTimeout, concurrency 2, timeout 300)
    c-motiflink13   2/5 errored (500 duplicate key) - reproduced with the log open
    c-motiflink14   5/5 errored - MY broken SQL
    c-motiflink15   0/5 errored, 5/5 called

  INDEPENDENT OF THE BATCH, from the service's own log in the 25 minutes after deploy:
    6  'interrupt-persist detached' events — the race's precondition, six times
    0  duplicate-key violations on idx_chat_messages_branch_unique
That second measurement is the stronger one: it counts the precondition occurring rather than hoping a batch reproduces it.
D-AN-ABORTED-TURNS-DETACHED-WRITE-RACES-.red_able:
services/chat-service/tests/test_the_sequence_lock_is_real_sql.py, 4 guards run against the REAL database: the statement is valid SQL, the WRONG overload genuinely fails (anti-vacuity — if both spellings worked the first test would prove nothing), two concurrent allocators for the same session SERIALISE (the second blocks until the first commits), and calling it outside a transaction RAISES.

Explicit opt-in via CHAT_DB_URL. Falling back to DATABASE_URL made all four FAIL rather than skip in an ordinary run, because that variable points at the container-internal host — and a live-DB test that breaks the default suite is one somebody deletes. Chat suite: 3,608 passed, 7 skipped.

So this row's claim is narrowed to what is measured: the DUPLICATE-KEY 500 is fixed — 6 'interrupt-persist detached' events since deploy with zero unique-constraint violations, and c-motiflink15 clean 5/5. The ReadTimeout failures are a DIFFERENT cause and are back on their own row, which was wrongly superseded into this one.

🔴 REJECTED 1 — `tool_calls[].iteration`. 🔴 REJECTED 2 — an independent per-pass counter. `stream_job_id` is minted once per pass (M3) and persisted NOWHERE: no column in loreweave_chat or loreweave_jobs holds it. There is no LLM-call-count on a chat turn either — that counter rides unified-JOB params, and a chat turn is not a job.

D-THE-PERSISTED-PER-PASS-RECORDER-DROPS-.the_lead_is_now_VERIFIED_in_the_useful_d:
The row's standing lead was: 'a pass that runs after the last persist would not be in the column. NOT VERIFIED — it is where to look, not what happened.'

It is now settled that the pass was RECORDED, which is the half that matters, because it kills every hypothesis of the shape 'the chunk never reached the recorder' and leaves only the write.

THE ARGUMENT IS STRUCTURAL — no 1-in-15 live run was needed:
  1. In `_stream_with_tools`, under `if advertised:`, the pass chunk is yielded UNCONDITIONALLY at the branch's own indent, and the 'agent-surface advertised (session=...)' log line — the ONLY witness the gap has ever had — sits BELOW it.
  2. An async generator resumes past a `yield` only when its consumer requests the NEXT item. So it cannot reach that log line until the consumer's loop body for that chunk has run to completion — and `record_pass` is in that body.
  3. The one layer in between, `_bounded_turn_stream`, does NOT prefetch: it awaits `iterator.__anext__()` one item at a time under `wait_for`. Its ceiling trip `aclose()`s the inner generator, raising GeneratorExit AT the yield — which loses the LOG line and never the recorded pass, i.e. the opposite direction from this defect.

So every 'agent-surface advertised' line the log printed PROVES `record_pass` ran for that pass. The row's instance logged 5 and stored 4, therefore the fifth was recorded and then lost at write time.

🔴 WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: which write lost it. The recorder is already cleared (it appends unconditionally and `advertised_json` returns `self._passes` whole), so the remaining space is the persist call itself and the segment merge — and the abandoned-suspend path is already excluded because the merge keeps a NULL. Nothing here identifies the cause; it removes the half of the space that was still open.
D-THE-PERSISTED-PER-PASS-RECORDER-DROPS-.the_metric_compares_two_DIFFERENT_popula:
Found 2026-08-28 while reading the emit sites. `pass_ledger.gap` subtracts two counts that do not measure the same thing:

    store    = EVERY pass — tool-bearing and tool-free alike (all three emit sites feed `record_pass`)
    wire_log = TOOL-BEARING passes only — the 'agent-surface advertised' line sits inside `if advertised:` and inside `if surface_tracker is not None:`

Consequences for how this row's own evidence must be read:
  * store >= wire_log is the NORMAL relation, not agreement. A turn with tool-free passes     (the D7 forced-final answer, a D8 provider rejection, ask-mode filtering all) makes     store legitimately larger.
  * A gap the other way — store < wire_log, which is this row's instance — remains a REAL     loss of a tool-bearing pass. That reading is unaffected.
  * 🔴 BUT A LOSS CAN BE MASKED. One lost tool-bearing pass plus one tool-free pass in the     same turn cancel to gap 0. So '0 gaps in 5' is weaker evidence than it appears, and the     1-in-15 rate is a FLOOR rather than an estimate.
  * `surface_tracker is None` suppresses the log line without suppressing the record, which     biases the same way.

A sharper instrument would compare per-pass, not per-turn: for each recorded entry with non-empty `names`, require a matching log line. NOT BUILT — it still needs the 30-minute log window, so it buys precision, not a historical witness, and this cycle did not measure whether the extra precision changes the rate.

D-A-ROWS-STATUS-PROSE-CONTRADICTS-ITS-OW.the_fix:
`gate.py audit` gains `status_state_drift`, which REFUSES BY NAME and does not rewrite: a row edited by a tool is a row nobody re-read, the rule `dq_alias_drift` states one block up in the same file.

PRECISE, NOT BLANKET, and the hook's THIRD row is the proof: D-KG-BUILD-… opens with "DECLARED and DEPLOYED 2026-08-24 — and UNMEASURED", which asserts nothing about open-versus-closed, so it is correctly left alone. A check on "does the prose contain the word open" would have flagged much of the ledger and been switched off.

BOTH DIRECTIONS. A row reading FIXED while its state is open is the same lie and the more dangerous one — it retires work that was never done.
D-A-ROWS-STATUS-PROSE-CONTRADICTS-ITS-OW.the_seven_were_repaired_by_hand: Each keeps its ORIGINAL SENTENCE VERBATIM, labelled as what the status said when the row was filed, behind a lead naming the row's actual state and the field that records why. D-THE-NORMALISER-DROPS-ARTICLES-BUT-NOT-.invariant: A request that uses a tool's declared synonym must reach that tool, whatever ordinary punctuation the author wrote it with.
D-THE-NORMALISER-DROPS-ARTICLES-BUT-NOT-.what: `_answer_norm` normalises articles out of a synonym match and does NOT normalise hyphens, so a compound an author would naturally write loses the tool entirely.
D-THE-NORMALISER-DROPS-ARTICLES-BUT-NOT-.measured:
Against the DEPLOYED matcher, over the live 316-tool catalogue, one character apart:

    'Run the golden-rules validation on my plan for this book'
        answerable = {book_steering_list}          plan_validate NOT answerable
    'Run the golden rules validation on my plan for this book'
        answerable = {plan_validate, ...}          plan_validate answerable

plan_validate declares the synonym 'golden rules'. The hyphenated form is the one a careful writer uses for a compound modifier, and it is the one that fails.
D-THE-NORMALISER-DROPS-ARTICLES-BUT-NOT-.how_it_was_found:
It cost a whole K=5 live batch. The DQ-T45 proof scenario used 'the golden-rules validation' and came back 0/5 called, 0/5 surfaced with ZERO errors — a clean-looking run that measured nothing. The tool was never on the wire, so 'the plan_run did not advance' was true and vacuous.

🔴 A ZERO-ERROR BATCH IS NOT A WORKING BATCH. Every bar this scenario carries would have read as satisfied.
D-THE-NORMALISER-DROPS-ARTICLES-BUT-NOT-.the_class_it_belongs_to: Same function, same failure shape as D-THE-ANSWERABILITY-TIE-IS-MANUFACTURED-NOT-GENUINE: `_answer_norm`'s coverage decides which tools a request can reach at all. There the normaliser was too AGGRESSIVE (stripping the articles that told create from edit and manufacturing a three-way tie); here it is too NARROW. Both are the same question — what the normaliser is for — and a fix to either should be measured against the other, because widening it further is exactly what manufactured the ties.
D-THE-NORMALISER-DROPS-ARTICLES-BUT-NOT-.not_yet_investigated: How large the population is. One instance is measured. What is NOT known: how many of the 1,472 declared synonyms contain a term an author would hyphenate, and whether the reverse case exists (a synonym declared WITH a hyphen, unreachable from the spaced form). Neither is guessed here. Per the owner's 2026-08-27 scoping rule, that census must be over LIVE tools only.
D-THE-NORMALISER-DROPS-ARTICLES-BUT-NOT-.status: FIXED 2026-08-27. `_answer_norm` now treats every dash as a word break, on both sides of the match, at the one function both sides pass through.
D-THE-NORMALISER-DROPS-ARTICLES-BUT-NOT-.the_fix:
`_answer_norm` is the single chokepoint: the match loop normalises the REQUEST (`lp`), each SYNONYM (`ns`) and the tool NAME (`nn`) through it. So one line fixes both directions — a hyphenated request reaching a spaced synonym, and a spaced request reaching a synonym declared with a hyphen.

Unicode dashes (U+2010..U+2015) are included: an em dash is how an author separates clauses, and 'Write chapter — draft the prose for …' is a measured live prompt.
D-THE-NORMALISER-DROPS-ARTICLES-BUT-NOT-.the_widening_was_MEASURED_before_it_was_:
Because widening THIS function is the thing that manufactured the ties. Stripping ARTICLES collapsed 'write chapter' / 'write A chapter' / 'write THE chapter' into one string and destroyed the create-vs-edit distinction their authors had drawn (D-THE-ANSWERABILITY-TIE-IS-MANUFACTURED-NOT-GENUINE). So the same question was asked of this widening BEFORE shipping it, over the 1,194 synonyms of the 199 LIVE tools — legacy excluded per the owner's catalogue-census rule, and it matters: the catalogue holds 316, so the whole-catalogue figure would have been a different and wrong denominator.

    colliding normalised synonyms today        13
    colliding after the fix                    13      NEW COLLISIONS: 0

RECALL BOUGHT: 10 synonyms are declared WITH a hyphen and were unreachable from the spaced form — `co-write`, `re-translate changed`, `un-index chapter`, `reverse-engineer arc`, `multi-chapter structure`, `spawn what-if` — and 1,095 multi-word synonyms were unreachable from a hyphenated request.

🔴 RE-DERIVED AGAINST THE SHIPPED REGEX, NOT MY APPROXIMATION OF IT. The first measurement used `.replace('-', ' ')` — ASCII only — while what shipped covers the unicode dashes too. A number that vouches for code which does not exist is not evidence, so the collision count was recomputed INSIDE the running container using the deployed `_answer_norm`: still 13 before, 13 after, 0 new.
D-THE-NORMALISER-DROPS-ARTICLES-BUT-NOT-.the_control_that_refuted_the_OBVIOUS_ver:
🔴 COLLAPSING `_` AS WELL AS `-` IS THE NATURAL GENERALISATION AND IT IS WRONG.

`_exact_name_pattern` guards a tool NAME with `(?<![a-z0-9_])` precisely because a name is an IDENTIFIER — its own docstring records `book_list` matching inside `book_list_chapters` before it shipped. Turning `_` into a space makes that boundary a space and the bug returns. Measured over the live tool names:

    hyphen only            a name matching inside another name:  0
    hyphen AND underscore  a name matching inside another name:  3
        book_list          inside composition_motif_book_list
        world_map_update   inside world_map_update_marker
        world_map_update   inside world_map_update_region

`world_map_update_marker` is a tool this ledger already records reporting a write it never made (5/5). So the broader fix would have dragged a destructive sibling onto the wire to solve a punctuation problem. The docstring predicted it; the measurement confirmed it before it shipped rather than after.

D-A-TOOL-REACHES-THE-WIRE-WITHOUT-ITS-DO.why_it_matters: The skills carry the rules that keep a domain safe and coherent — 'emit ONE confirm card per turn', 'never claim a change happened until a tool result confirms it', the adopt-before-propose ordering. A turn that can call the domain's tools without any of that is operating the domain with its instructions removed, and nothing reports the gap.
D-A-TOOL-REACHES-THE-WIRE-WITHOUT-ITS-DO.what_is_NOT_known:
* FREQUENCY. One prompt, three batches. How often a turn calls a domain's tools with that domain's skill absent is unmeasured, and the honest instrument is a join over recorded turns: advertised/called tool prefixes vs injected_skills.
  * WHETHER IT IS ALWAYS WRONG. A read-only glossary lookup arguably needs no ontology guidance, so 'inject the skill whenever a domain's tool is advertised' may over-inject. The candidate fix is not obvious and should be measured before it is written.
  * SCOPE ACROSS DOMAINS. Only glossary was observed. composition, knowledge and translation have the same two-mechanism split and were not checked.
D-A-TOOL-REACHES-THE-WIRE-WITHOUT-ITS-DO.the_real_cause_traced_2026_08_28:
Traced past the symptom to why the router NEVER fires under the deployed default (lazy_skill_bodies=True, the ONLY path that can add a domain skill on an unpinned turn): `route_additional_skills` needs `_resolve_embedding_model(user_id)`, which called the STRICT `get_default_model("embedding", user_id)` — 404s unless the user EXPLICITLY set an 'embedding' default.

MEASURED against the live platform, not assumed: `SELECT capability, count(*) FROM user_default_models GROUP BY capability` returns planner/rerank/chat/distill rows and ZERO for 'embedding' — not one account, on the whole deployment, has ever set one. Meanwhile 7 ACTIVE embedding-capable user_models exist across the platform, including TWO on this loop's own test account. D-A-SINCE-WATERMARK-BACKSTOP-IS-BLIND-TO.status: OPEN — found 2026-08-28 answering the owner's question 'why not it cancel, is it a other defect?'
D-A-SINCE-WATERMARK-BACKSTOP-IS-BLIND-TO.what:
The projection has a designed backstop for exactly this drift — `ReconcileSweeper` in jobs-service, whose own header says 'outbox = primary; reconcile = safety net'. It cannot heal a job that VANISHED.

`_sweep_source` fetches `GET /internal/{svc}/jobs?since={watermark}` and calls `upsert_job_event` for each row RETURNED. There is no pass over rows it expected and did not see, no terminal-marking for an absent job, no deletion. So it is additive-only, and it is keyed on CHANGE: a job row that stopped changing — or was removed — never appears in any `?since=` window again, and the projection keeps claiming it is running forever.

A safety net that reads only what the source still reports catches DRIFT and is blind to ABSENCE. Those are different failures and only one of them has a backstop.
D-A-SINCE-WATERMARK-BACKSTOP-IS-BLIND-TO.measured:
loreweave_jobs.job_projection vs the composition owning tables, 2026-08-28:

    composition projection rows                                          910
    status=completed   job row FOUND 460   ABSENT 414
    status=failed      job row FOUND   3   ABSENT  10
    status=running     job row FOUND   0   ABSENT  12
    status=pending     job row FOUND   0   ABSENT  10

🔴 THE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THIS READABLE, AND IT REFUTED THE OBVIOUS READING. 'The job row is gone' is NOT by itself the defect — 414 COMPLETED jobs are also absent, so the projection routinely outlives its source rows and that is unremarkable for history. What is not unremarkable is the asymmetry: 22 of 22 CONTROLLABLE rows are absent, against 53% found among completed. Had I only looked at the stuck rows I would have published 'the job row is gone' as the cause and been half wrong.

AND THEY NEVER TERMINATED: 10 of 12 running and 10 of 10 pending have job_updated_at - job_created_at < 1 second — one status write, then silence. Oldest 2026-07-10, still 'running' 47 days later. Meanwhile 874 composition jobs completed normally in the same period, so this is a ~2.4% leak, not a broken pipeline.
D-A-SINCE-WATERMARK-BACKSTOP-IS-BLIND-TO.why_it_matters: It is the reason the owner's question has an answer. `jobs_list` advertises control_caps ['cancel'] on all 22 (checked against the deployed derive_control_caps), 3 of them belonging to real users, and every cancel would fail because there is nothing to cancel. control_caps is not lying — it is being told the job is running by a projection whose backstop cannot discover otherwise.
D-A-SINCE-WATERMARK-BACKSTOP-IS-BLIND-TO.the_two_causes_are_separate:
1. A job reaches running/pending and never emits a terminal event. That is a producer liveness bug and it is where the rows come from.
  2. The backstop cannot correct it, because `?since=` can only carry rows that changed. This row is about (2). (1) is worth its own investigation per producer and is NOT claimed here — 22 rows across three services is not enough to say which producer drops them or why.
D-A-SINCE-WATERMARK-BACKSTOP-IS-BLIND-TO.what_is_NOT_known:
* WHICH PRODUCER, AND WHY. Not diagnosed. The rows span composition (22 of them), knowledge and lore_enrichment.
  * WHETHER ABSENCE IS EVEN DETECTABLE CHEAPLY. A 'rows I expected and did not see' pass needs the sweep to enumerate rather than tail, which is a different and heavier query against every owning service. Not designed, not costed.
  * WHETHER THE 414 ABSENT COMPLETED ROWS ARE INTENDED. They may be deliberate retention (the projection as history outliving the source) or the same leak in a terminal state. Unmeasured, and it changes what a fix may safely delete.
D-A-SINCE-WATERMARK-BACKSTOP-IS-BLIND-TO.measured_by: loreweave_jobs.job_projection joined against loreweave_composition plan_run/generation_job/authoring_runs, 2026-08-28; code read of services/jobs-service/app/reconcile.py

A real fix here is new capability in five services, sized and safety-gated by DQ-T65.

D-A-TURN-DENIES-THE-WRITE-ITS-OWN-TOOL-R.what:
The turn performs a Tier-A write, receives an explicit success, and then tells the author it did not — on 3 of 5 runs (RE-DERIVED 2026-08-30; the row was filed claiming 5/5, see below).

Batch c-canonrestore3. Every run: composition_canon_rule_edit {op: restore} -> {ok: true, is_archived: False, active: True}. Three of the five then close with a denial: 'the archived rule has not been restored', 'I have not made any changes to your saved data, and the rule remains archived', 'there is a technical issue preventing the restoration'. The store disagrees with the prose: the row was restored on all 5.

🔴 THIS IS THE INVERSE OF THE FAMILIAR FAILURE. The known shape is a turn CLAIMING work it did not do; here the turn DENIES work it did do, which is worse for a write — an author told the restore failed will redo it, and for a non-idempotent operation that is a second row.
D-A-TURN-DENIES-THE-WRITE-ITS-OWN-TOOL-R.first_lead: SUPERSEDED by the re-derivation above and kept as a recorded wrong guess. It read: 'the retraction reads like a self-correction pass reacting to something in the turn AFTER the successful result … a plausible hypothesis is that a LATER failed retry is being reported as the outcome of the whole turn.' The tails refute it — reps 0 and 3 have the same later retries and end TRUE, and the retraction is aimed at the model's own PREMATURE claim rather than at any tool failure.
D-A-TURN-DENIES-THE-WRITE-ITS-OWN-TOOL-R.why_it_is_not_part_of_the_row_that_expos: D-THE-MODEL-ASKS-INSTEAD-OF-RAISING-THE-CARD-IT-HAS was a SURFACE defect — the model had no card to raise — and is fixed. This is about how a turn REPORTS an action it completed. Different cause, and the two use different vocabularies (turn-outcome vs call-outcome).
D-A-TURN-DENIES-THE-WRITE-ITS-OWN-TOOL-R.attribution_re_validated_2026_08_30:
RE-VALIDATED 2026-08-30 by `scripts/toolloop/was_it_on_the_wire.py` over every OPEN model row, because this loop has twice found a model row that was really a SURFACING row (D-THE-MODEL-ASKS-INSTEAD-OF-RAISING-THE-CARD-IT-HAS, reattributed; D-THE-MODEL-CLAIMS-A-BINDING-IT-NEVER-MADE, evidence gone stale). ATTRIBUTION CONFIRMED: the tool this row says the model declined WAS on the wire in its own sessions, so 'the model chose wrongly' is a statement the evidence supports. It is a model row.

🔴 READ THE SWEEP'S 0/N FLAGS WITH CARE — most are NOISE. It harvests candidate tool names from a row's PROSE, so a tool merely mentioned in passing shows as 'NEVER ON THE WIRE' while the row's actual subject was advertised. Three rows here carry such a flag and none is misfiled: the flagged names are neighbours, not the tool under test.

THIS ROW: composition_canon_rule_edit 5/5 advertised (c-canonrestore3) — and it was CALLED and SUCCEEDED on all five, which is the row's whole point.
D-A-TURN-DENIES-THE-WRITE-ITS-OWN-TOOL-R.RE_DERIVED_2026_08_30_MY_OWN_5_of_5_WAS_:
🔴 I FILED THIS ROW EARLIER TODAY WITH '5/5' AND 'Every run then closes with a retraction'. Both are wrong, and they are wrong because I read the concatenated `text` field instead of what the author is LEFT WITH.

A turn here spans several passes — the model narrates, a card is raised, the harness approves, the tool executes, the model narrates again — and `text` glues every pass's prose together. Read whole, every run looks like it retracts. Read at the TAIL, which is what the author actually ends on:

    rep0  TRUE   'I have now successfully restored the rule: Magic always costs HP.'
    rep1  FALSE  'there is a technical issue preventing the restoration … try restoring it manually through the Studio UI'
    rep2  FALSE  'the archived rule has not been restored'
    rep3  TRUE   'I have now successfully called the tool, and the rule … has been restored'
    rep4  FALSE  'I have not made any changes to your saved data, and the rule remains archived'

So it is 3 of 5, not 5 of 5, and two runs self-correct CORRECTLY. The defect is real and the harm is unchanged for the three — an author told the restore failed will redo it — but the rate was overstated by my own reading on the day I filed it.

AND THE MECHANISM IS DIFFERENT FROM THE ONE I GUESSED. My `first_lead` blamed a later failed retry being reported as the turn's outcome. The tails show the real shape: the model claims success PREMATURELY, on the pass that mints the card and before anything executes ('I've restored the rule' is the FIRST thing every run says). It then notices it spoke too soon and apologises — and the apology lands correctly on 2 of 5 and OVERSHOOTS into denying the now-completed write on 3 of 5. The retraction is a correction of the PREMATURE CLAIM, not a report of a failed call.
D-A-TURN-DENIES-THE-WRITE-ITS-OWN-TOOL-R.status: OPEN and BLOCKED on DQ-T71. The measurable half is done — the population is derived by a shipped predicate — and what remains is what the AUTHOR is told, which is a product call.

A turn spans several passes and the recorded `text` glues them together, so read whole EVERY run looks like it retracts — which is how this row was filed claiming 5 of 5 when the tails show 3. The author is left with the END of the reply, so the end is what is judged. The predicate reproduces the hand reading exactly on both batches (3/5 and 2/5, same reps).

CORPUS RATE: 28 of 1,786 recorded runs (1.57%), across a dozen batches and several tool families — override, trunc, booksync, canonrestore — so it is a class, not one scenario's quirk.

🔴 THE FIRST MEASUREMENT SAID 35 AND SEVEN OF THEM WERE MY OWN INSTRUMENT. The turn-ceiling close (DQ-T56) reads 'the turn did not complete … Any tool calls already made in this turn ran, and THEIR EFFECTS STAND' — true, server-authored, and the opposite of a denial. Every deterministic line the platform appends is now excluded by a phrase only it uses: a detector that counts the platform's own honest sentences as the defect is measuring itself.
D-A-TURN-DENIES-THE-WRITE-ITS-OWN-TOOL-R.the_mechanism_2026_08_30:
ESTABLISHED FROM THE TAILS, and it is not what the row's first_lead guessed.

The model claims success PREMATURELY — in the pass that mints the approval card, before anything executes. 'I've restored the rule' is the FIRST thing every run says. It then notices it spoke too soon and apologises, and the apology lands correctly on some runs and OVERSHOOTS into denying the now-completed write on others. The retraction corrects the model's own premature claim; it is never a report of a failed call.

WHY THE PLATFORM DOES NOT ALREADY CATCH IT: the Tier-W/S confirm-token path appends `_CONFIRM_CARD_STOP_NOTE` — 'Nothing is saved until they click Confirm … Reply with ONE short sentence telling the user the change is ready for them to confirm, then stop.' The Tier-A `tool_approval` path appends NOTHING; it breaks straight to the suspend. So the one path that tells the model not to speak in the past tense is the path this defect does not use.

DQ-T54's line (shipped today) already puts a true server sentence beside the premature claim on the SUSPEND. It does not touch the post-approval overshoot, which is where the denial lands.
D-A-TURN-DENIES-THE-WRITE-ITS-OWN-TOOL-R.what_is_NOT_covered:
- NOTHING IS FIXED. This cycle established the mechanism and shipped the DETECTOR; the remedy is DQ-T71.
- THE RATE IS NOT ESTABLISHED PER SCENARIO. 3/5 then 2/5 on the same scenario is n=5 twice; the corpus 1.57% is solid, the per-turn-shape rate is not.

D-THE-BOOK-TO-PROJECT-RESOLVER-DENIES-TH.what:
`composition_get_work` is the ONE tool that bridges book_id -> project_id. Its own description says so: 'otherwise pass book_id — the book's Work is resolved, which is ALSO how you discover the project_id every other composition_* tool requires (a book_id is NOT a project_id)'.

Called with the session's own book_id it returns the H13 uniform deny — 'not found or not accessible' — on 5 of 5 runs, while `composition_list_outline` succeeds against that same book's project_id in the same turns. The caller owns the book and the project exists; the bridge between them denies.
D-THE-BOOK-TO-PROJECT-RESOLVER-DENIES-TH.why_it_matters: It is the entry point of every composition workflow, and its failure is INDISTINGUISHABLE from 'you do not have access to this book'. Measured downstream on 5 of 5 runs: the model retried it up to three times, tripped the repeated-failure breaker, then asked the author to confirm which book it should be working in — for the book the session is bound to. Two runs went further and passed a MOTIF id as book_id/project_id, which is what a model does when the id it holds keeps being rejected.
D-THE-BOOK-TO-PROJECT-RESOLVER-DENIES-TH.first_lead_NOT_a_root_cause:
`WorksRepo.resolve_by_book` selects `WHERE book_id = $1 AND status = 'active' AND book_lifecycle = 'active' AND NOT pending_project_backfill`, and 0 rows becomes the uniform deny. Its own C16 comment explains the exclusion: a lazy null-project Work is a placeholder, so excluding it makes resolution fall through to the knowledge book-project lookup, which is meant to hit the 'create_project -> BACKFILL' seam.

Every composition_work row surviving in the live DB is stuck at exactly that placeholder state — 8 of 8 with `pending_project_backfill = true` and a NULL project_id, the newest from 08:32 that morning. So the backfill that is supposed to clear the flag appears not to be clearing it.

🔴 THIS IS A LEAD AND IT IS NOT SUFFICIENT. The harness calls `composition_create_work` during provisioning and READS a project_id back from it, so something did resolve a project — yet no row carries one. Whether create_work backfills a different row, returns a project without persisting it, or the rows examined are unrelated leftovers is NOT established, and no fix should be attempted until it is.
D-THE-BOOK-TO-PROJECT-RESOLVER-DENIES-TH.what_is_NOT_covered:
- NOT REPRODUCED IN ISOLATION. Observed as a side-effect of re-running c-bindarc1; there is no dedicated scenario for it yet.
- WHETHER IT AFFECTS NON-FIXTURE BOOKS IS UNKNOWN. Every observation is on throwaway harness fixtures, which are created differently from a book made in the UI. This may be a provisioning-path defect rather than a platform-wide one, and saying which requires a book created the normal way.
- IT BLOCKS a clean re-measure of D-THE-MODEL-CLAIMS-A-BINDING-IT-NEVER-MADE.
D-THE-BOOK-TO-PROJECT-RESOLVER-DENIES-TH.status: WITHDRAWN 2026-08-28, same session it was filed. It is not a defect; I misread it.
D-THE-BOOK-TO-PROJECT-RESOLVER-DENIES-TH.the_control_that_refuted_it:
🔴 THE TOOL WAS RIGHT AND I WAS WRONG. The row claimed `composition_get_work` denies 'the session's own book_id'. It was never given the book's id.

The run record carries a `seed_ids` map naming every id the fixture minted. For rep0:

    fixture book_id                       01a04e44-3bc5-74e3-b779-eadd7e02df87
    fixture chapter_id (editor context)   01a04e44-3c70-7333-b714-068005828c4d
    what the model passed as book_id      01a04e44-3c70-7333-b714-068005828c4d

The model passed the CHAPTER id as `book_id`. The caller owns no book with that id, so the H13 uniform deny is exactly correct — and it is correct that it does not explain itself, because explaining would make it an existence oracle. Same on every run.

The two ids share a uuidv7 millisecond prefix (`01a04e44-3...`), which is why they read as the same id at a glance. I compared them by eye instead of against `seed_ids`, which the harness records for precisely this purpose.

AND THE FIRST LEAD WAS ALSO WRONG, in a way worth keeping. I found 8 of 8 surviving `composition_work` rows stuck at `pending_project_backfill = true` with a NULL project and took that as corroboration. Provisioning a fresh fixture and reading its row directly:

    project_id  01a04e4d-54c4-...   status active   book_lifecycle active   pending false

— a perfect row that `resolve_by_book` finds. The stuck rows are OLD leftovers from earlier sessions, not what today's fixtures look like. Two wrong readings agreeing with each other is not evidence; it is the same mistake twice.
D-THE-BOOK-TO-PROJECT-RESOLVER-DENIES-TH.what_was_actually_true: The model conflated `chapter_id` with `book_id` — the editor context carries the chapter id, and it reached for that when a tool asked for a book. That is a real observation about the surface, but it is NOT this row, and it is not filed as one on a single incidental sighting.

D-ONE-PASS-RECORDED-TWICE-WHEN-THE-SURFA.found_by: Reading the code while narrowing D-THE-PERSISTED-PER-PASS-RECORDER-DROPS-A-PASS-ON-THE-SECOND-TURN — not by a batch. Establishing which log line witnesses a pass meant reading all three emit sites, and two of them turn out to overlap.
D-ONE-PASS-RECORDED-TWICE-WHEN-THE-SURFA.the_invariant: One model pass emits exactly one `advertised` chunk, and so records exactly one entry.
D-ONE-PASS-RECORDED-TWICE-WHEN-THE-SURFA.why_it_matters:
It corrupts the DENOMINATOR this whole loop divides by. 'advertised in N of M passes' reads M from this column, and M was one too many whenever this fired.

It also MASKS its own opposite. D-THE-PERSISTED-PER-PASS-RECORDER-DROPS-A-PASS-ON-THE-SECOND-TURN detects a lost pass by comparing this column against the 'agent-surface advertised' log line — and that line prints only for TOOL-BEARING passes (it sits inside `if advertised:`), while the column counts every pass. So a spurious empty entry can cover a genuinely lost tool-bearing pass and show the two counts agreeing.
D-ONE-PASS-RECORDED-TWICE-WHEN-THE-SURFA.the_control:
MEASURED over the live store BEFORE the fix: adjacent entries with empty `names` in the same segment, which is the shape the duplicate leaves — 1 pair across the 5,759 messages carrying the column, on 1 message.

🔴 AND THAT 1 IS AN UPPER BOUND, NOT A COUNT: two genuine consecutive tool-free passes produce the same shape, so the true incidence may be zero. The path is real by CONSTRUCTION — the tests drive it — and very rare in practice. This is a correctness guard, not the repair of an observed measurement error, and it is not credited as one.
D-ONE-PASS-RECORDED-TWICE-WHEN-THE-SURFA.the_fix: A per-pass `_adv_emitted` flag, reset beside `offered_tools` (so it cannot outlive its pass and suppress the NEXT one's record), set at both legitimate emit sites, and read by the third: `if not offered_tools and not _adv_emitted:`.
D-ONE-PASS-RECORDED-TWICE-WHEN-THE-SURFA.red_able:
services/chat-service/tests/test_one_pass_records_exactly_one_advertised_entry.py, 3 tests. They DRIVE THE REAL GENERATOR rather than assert on source text — the bug is not a missing line, it is two live lines whose guards overlap, and only running the block distinguishes them.

INVERSE-EDIT: removing the `and not _adv_emitted` guard turns 2 of the 3 RED — the ask-mode path and the tool-free path both record 2 entries for 1 pass. The third (a normal tool-bearing write-mode pass) stays green, which is the point: the guard is a no-op on the path every real turn takes. Restored byte-identical.
D-ONE-PASS-RECORDED-TWICE-WHEN-THE-SURFA.proven_live:
PARTIALLY, AND THE UNPROVEN HALF IS NAMED.

WHAT WAS PROVEN LIVE — no regression. batch c-passguard1, K=5, real provider, throwaway fixture per run: `pass_ledger` gap 0 on all five (store == wire_log at 4,4,4,4,6 — both sides non-zero, so the agreement is not the vacuous kind), and the scenario's own behaviour is unchanged, restoring the canon rule 5 of 5.

🔴 WHAT WAS NOT PROVEN LIVE — the defect path itself, and it CANNOT be. Reaching it needs `advertised` to come back empty while `offered_tools` is still True. The discovery advertise chokepoint always adds ALWAYS_ON_CORE_NAMES (tool_list / tool_load / confirm_action / web_search) before any tier filtering, so `advertised` is never empty there — every agui turn takes that path. Only the NON-discovery ask-mode path can empty it, and that requires a legacy non-agui tool-calling client the harness cannot drive. So the fix is proven by the generator under test and by no-regression live, never by a live run through the defect itself.
